companies.name: 80,000 Hours
companies.description: 80,000 Hours is an independent nonprofit, founded in 2011 by Benjamin Todd and William MacAskill out of Oxford, that provides free research and support to help people use their careers to help solve the world's most pressing problems. The name refers to the roughly 80,000 hours a typical person works over their lifetime. It publishes an evidence-based career guide, in-depth problem profiles, a long-form podcast, and one-on-one advising, and runs a curated high-impact job board at jobs.80000hours.org. Since 2016 it has ranked helping navigate the transition to advanced AI as its top priority. It is a content and career-advice organization rather than an API producer; no public developer API is published, though it does serve a machine-readable llms.txt index of its content.

companies.description: ApplePie Capital is a San Francisco-based franchise-finance marketplace lender that connects franchisees and franchisors with the capital they need to start, refinance, and grow multi-unit franchise businesses. Founded in 2014 by Denise Thomas, the company operates an online lending platform focused exclusively on franchising, offering conventional term loans, SBA loans, refinancing, equipment financing, and accounts-receivable financing, and partnering with banks such as Fifth Third and providers like LSQ. ApplePie has provided billions in loans across 200+ franchise brand partners. It is backed by QED Investors and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a fintech company profile; no public API or developer program has been identified as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Atoms
companies.description: Atoms is a direct-to-consumer footwear brand founded in 2019 by Waqas Ali and Sidra Qasim and headquartered in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, New York. The company designs, develops, and sells minimalist everyday sneakers - notably its Model 000 and Model 001 lines - and differentiates itself with quarter-size sizing and the ability to buy a pair in two different sizes for each foot. Product features include lightweight foam cushioning, a copper-infused antimicrobial lining, stretch slip-on laces, and an 8mm heel-to-toe drop. Atoms sells online via a Shopify storefront and is backed by Initialized Capital, Kleiner Perkins, DST Global, and Serena Ventures. It has no public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

companies.name: AWST
companies.description: AWST is the software company behind WorkRamen, a productivity and business-operations platform aimed at small and medium businesses, startups, agencies, and freelancers. WorkRamen brings meeting scheduling (with Google Calendar and Outlook sync, plus Google Meet and Zoom), trackable document sharing, secure e-signatures, routing forms, visitor management, and Stripe-based payment acceptance into a single workspace. AWST is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a SaaS product only — its brand domain awst.io redirects to workramen.com, and no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or API documentation surface could be found.

companies.name: Beewise
companies.description: Beewise is an agricultural technology company building the BeeHome, an AI- and robotics-enabled beehive that autonomously monitors, cares for, and protects honeybee colonies to reduce colony loss and deliver reliable pollination. Founded to address bee colony collapse, Beewise combines computer vision, robotics, and cloud software to detect pests and disease, regulate hive climate, and dispatch precision pollination for growers. The company serves growers with guaranteed pollination services, beekeepers with technology-enhanced hive management, and property owners through its Bees for Buildings program. Beewise is a venture-backed company (Insight Partners portfolio) surfaced into the API Evangelist network; it operates a customer grower portal but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

companies.name: Bellhops
companies.description: Bellhops (branded as Bellhop) is a US technology-enabled moving-services company that operates an online booking platform for residential and commercial relocations. Customers get a free estimate and reserve local moves, long-distance relocations, hourly moving labor, packing help, and last-minute moves with no money down, then manage their reservation through an online dashboard staffed by background-checked movers. The company reports more than 300,000 completed moves and a 4.8/5 average rating across 20,000+ reviews. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and Initialized Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Bellhops is a consumer-facing service with no publicly documented API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface as of this profile.

companies.name: Blend Financial
companies.description: Blend Financial Inc., doing business as Origin Financial (useorigin.com), is a consumer wealth management and personal finance platform that unifies income, net worth, spending, investments, assets, and liabilities into a single application. Origin pairs AI-powered budgeting and spend tracking with investment tools, estate and tax planning, and access to CFP professional advice; investment advisory services are provided through Origin Investment Advisory LLC, a subsidiary of Blend Financial Inc. The company is a consumer (B2C) product backed by 500 Global, Felicis Ventures, Founders Fund, and other investors, and also offers employer-sponsored financial wellness. As surfaced in the API Evangelist network it is a company profile; Origin publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

companies.description: Block Renovation is a home renovation and construction platform that connects homeowners with vetted, local contractors and provides free design, cost-estimation, and project-planning tools for kitchen and bathroom remodels, home additions, basement renovations, ADUs, new construction, and commercial projects. It operates across all 50 US states and layers on a protection program covering price assurance, progress-based payments, a workmanship warranty, and dedicated Project Planner support. Backed by Obvious Ventures and the SoftBank Vision Fund, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; as of this enrichment pass Block Renovation publishes a consumer-facing marketplace but no public developer API, documentation, or machine-readable specification.

companies.name: Boltzbit
companies.description: Boltzbit builds General Learning Intelligence (GLI) — AI systems that organizations can own, train, and control, learning continuously from proprietary data rather than depending on static, vendor-controlled models. Its product suite forms an operating system for AI-native software: BoltzHub, a marketplace where creators sell AI-powered apps and consumers subscribe to them; BoltzAgent, a self-learning assistant for research-backed chat, document editing, and production-ready code generation; BoltzLearn, an LLM fine-tuning platform for building custom models from your own data; and BoltzCloud, a multi-cloud deployment backbone across GCP, AWS, and Azure. Boltzbit is backed by Speedinvest. The company references an API product surface but does not yet publish public API documentation, an OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile will be enriched as those surfaces are released.

companies.name: Booqed
companies.description: BOOQED is a Hong Kong-based proptech company building flexible workplace technology that turns underutilized real estate into bookable, on-demand workspace. Its flagship product QUBIC is a line of sound-isolating, modular smart booths and work pods (for one to six people) with soundproofing, ventilation, power, and a proprietary access-control system managed through a mobile web app. Alongside the hardware, BOOQED offers space-management SaaS that makes existing meeting rooms and desks bookable and trackable with utilization analytics, plus the BOOQED app for individuals to book hot desks and meeting rooms on demand across Hong Kong, Singapore, and Shenzhen. Founded by David Wong, Charles Oh, and Ken Huang, BOOQED went through the Colliers and Techstars proptech accelerator and raised seed funding in 2019. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; BOOQED does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

companies.name: BoxGreen
companies.description: BoxGreen (BoxGreen Pte. Ltd., incorporated 2014 in Singapore) is a Certified B Corporation and social enterprise selling all-natural, individually packaged healthy snacks direct to consumers and to businesses. Its consumer offering is a Shopify-based e-commerce store with build-your-own snack boxes, curated collections (nut mixes, crunchies, vegan and gluten-free ranges), gift and party packs, and a subscription delivery model; its B2B side covers corporate gifting, office pantry supply, and cashless healthy-snack vending machines. Every BoxGreen snack is packed in prison by beneficiaries of Singapore's Yellow Ribbon Project to build skills and employability. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company, BoxGreen publishes no first-party API or developer program; the only machine-readable surface on its domain is Shopify's New Customer Accounts OIDC/OAuth discovery.

companies.name: buynomics
companies.description: Buynomics is a Cologne, Germany-based software company providing an AI-powered Revenue Growth Management (RGM) platform for consumer goods, retail, telecom, and consumer software companies. Its proprietary "Virtual Shoppers AI" runs agent-based simulations of consumer purchasing behavior so commercial teams can optimize pricing, promotions, price pack architecture (product mix), and trade terms before going to market — capturing cross- effects, cannibalization, and competitive response. The platform's Decision Guide generates prescriptive recommendations from thousands of evaluated scenarios. Buynomics is used by brands including Unilever, Nestle, L'Oreal, Danone, General Mills, Vodafone, and Ferrero, and is backed by Insight Partners and Seedcamp. The product is delivered as a web application; no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is published at this time.

companies.name: Cactos
companies.description: Cactos is a Finnish clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and operates smart battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and grid-scale use. Its hardware line (Cactos Mylo commercial storage and Cactos Cardo backup power, built in part from second-life Tesla EV batteries) is paired with Cactos Spine, a cloud software platform that optimizes each unit for load shifting, peak shaving, demand-charge reduction, solar self-consumption, backup power during outages, and participation in electricity and grid-balancing markets. Cactos serves logistics, manufacturing, EV charging, agriculture, real estate, and commercial-property operators. It is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. As of this profile, Cactos publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; the Cactos Spine app at app.cactos.com is a customer-facing management console rather than a documented developer API.

Borrowers apply online, receive fast funding decisions, and manage their accounts through a self-service client portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and profiled in the API Evangelist network; CAN Capital publishes a marketing site, application flow, and customer portal but no public developer API or discovery surface at this time.

companies.name: CarNow
companies.description: CarNow is an AI-enabled conversion platform built specifically for automotive dealerships, helping them turn more website visitors into leads, more leads into sales, and more buyers into lifelong service customers. Its product suite spans website solutions (AI-powered chat, digital retail, and shop-by-payment experiences), sales follow-up automation (Cruise Control, which prioritizes high-intent shoppers and automates nurture workflows), and service retention (Lane Assist, which drives post-sale engagement and service scheduling). CarNow works with more than 4,000 dealer partners and integrates with major OEM programs including Acura, Audi, BMW, Ford, General Motors, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Land Rover, and Lexus. The company is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina and is backed by Battery Ventures. CarNow does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs; its api.carnow.com endpoint is a partner/internal AWS API Gateway that requires authentication.

companies.name: Casper
companies.description: Casper (Casper Sleep Inc.) is a direct-to-consumer sleep and home goods brand that sells mattresses, bedding, pillows, and sleep accessories online at casper.com and through retail partners. Its casper.com storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agentic-commerce surface: a published llms.txt/agents.md with agent instructions, the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, a UCP shopping MCP endpoint for AI agents to search, cart, and check out, and Shopify Customer Account API OpenID Connect authentication. Casper was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IVP and Slow Ventures and enriched from its live public agent/commerce surface.

companies.name: Catalant
companies.description: Catalant is a consulting platform that connects organizations with a global marketplace of experienced independent consultants and boutique firms, positioning itself as "Consulting 2.0" fit-to-purpose consulting that is faster, more flexible, and more cost efficient than traditional large consulting firms. Its network spans 10,000+ vetted consultants (many from Fortune 500 companies and top-tier consulting firms, averaging 19+ years of experience) and serves 700+ businesses across 20+ countries. Catalant covers engagement areas including Digital & AI, Transformation & Value Creation, Operations, Sales & Marketing, M&A / Integration & Separation, Strategy & Finance, and Organization & People. Catalant is a General Catalyst portfolio company. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, and support properties.

companies.name: ChangEd
companies.description: ChangEd (Changed) is a consumer financial-technology company whose mobile app helps people pay off debt faster by automatically rounding up everyday purchases to the nearest dollar and directing those micro-savings toward student loans, credit cards, mortgages, personal loans, and auto loans. Founded by brothers Dan Stelmach and Nick Sky, the app launched in 2017, appeared on Shark Tank and took investment from Mark Cuban, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It links to a user's bank account, tracks spending, automates extra debt payments, supports savings goals, and visualizes payoff progress for a $4/month subscription, with banking services provided by nbkc bank (Member FDIC). ChangEd is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Circulo de Belleza
companies.description: Círculo de Belleza is an authorized distributor of professional beauty products in Mexico, operating an e-commerce storefront at circulodebelleza.com. It sells salon-quality hair care, hair color, nail, barbershop, and facial/spa supplies from 40+ professional brands (L'Oréal Professionnel, Olaplex, Wella, Schwarzkopf, Matrix, Alfaparf Milano) at professional pricing with no minimum purchase, same-day fulfillment, and nationwide Mexico delivery. The store is built on Shopify and exposes a native agent-commerce surface: a published llms.txt/agents.md, OpenID Connect and OAuth authorization-server discovery documents, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout.

companies.name: Club Feast

It began as a subscription-based consumer meal service delivering signature dishes from neighborhood restaurants at deep discounts through a pre-order, scheduled batch-delivery model, and has since focused on corporate catering, group meal ordering with individual customization, event catering, and managed office pantry services for teams. Club Feast handles restaurant partnerships, menu curation, driver logistics, and delivery while employees select meals through its web app. The company raised seed funding led by General Catalyst and operates primarily in the San Francisco Bay Area. Club Feast does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or specification; this profile tracks its company identity and public web surface within the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: CNC24
companies.description: CNC24 is a German online manufacturing platform for ordering custom CNC parts and precision components. Customers upload CAD files (STEP, STP, DWG, DXF, PDF and 3D data) and receive a binding quote within 48 hours, with production routed through a vetted network of 500+ manufacturers across 21 countries and roughly 5,500 machines. An AI-powered matching algorithm assigns each request to partners with the right expertise and production environment. Supported processes include CNC milling, turning, laser and waterjet cutting, sheet metal bending, punching, EDM, 3D printing, injection molding and die casting, serving aerospace, automotive, medical, robotics, construction and energy customers. The platform runs a fully digital workflow from quoting to delivery with order tracking, ISO 9001:2015 quality assurance, AES-256 encryption and anonymized drawings shared with partners. CNC24 is a Seedcamp portfolio company. No public developer API, SDKs or API documentation are published.

companies.name: Codi
companies.description: Codi is a managed flexible office-space provider (office-as-a-service) operating in San Francisco and New York City. Codi delivers fully-managed private offices for teams, bundling furniture, cleaning and restocking, tech and network management, vendor coordination, room booking, and an AI office assistant into a single turnkey monthly subscription — positioned as an alternative to traditional commercial leases, coworking, and short-term space marketplaces such as Regus, Breather, and Peerspace. Codi was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation — its digital surface is a members' web app and a hosted help center.

Con.doit is a FLIR Global Approved App and reports over 4.5 million electrical assets under management across 2,000+ critical facilities nationwide. companies.name: Corca
companies.description: Corca is an AI-native, collaborative workspace for mathematics — a browser-based editor that lets people write math naturally (without special syntax), run calculations in real time, and collaborate the way teams do in Figma or Google Docs. Typing keywords like "sum" or "integral" surfaces the right symbols and functions, documents import from and export to LaTeX, and built-in AI helps solve problems, manipulate expressions, and generate code without switching tools. It is used for lab research, lecture creation, team knowledge bases, and publishing academic work. Founded in 2023 and based in New York, Corca raised a $7.8M round (led by NEA, with Bloomberg Beta, NVIDIA's NVentures, Daft Capital, Slow Ventures, Liquid 2, Path Ventures, and Mana Ventures). The product is a consumer/team SaaS application; no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profile.

companies.name: CyberTalents
companies.description: CyberTalents is a global cybersecurity platform that ranks and connects security talent with employers based on real, hands-on skills. The platform automates Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions, delivers cybersecurity courses and training camps, runs technical assessments for enterprises, and provides recruitment and headhunting services to close the global cybersecurity skills gap. Backed by 500 Global, CyberTalents operates from Egypt, the UAE, and the United States and hosts one of the largest cybersecurity practice communities in the world. companies.description: Dapper Labs is a Vancouver-based blockchain company (originally spun out of Axiom Zen) that builds consumer crypto and NFT experiences and the developer platform behind them. It created the Flow blockchain, CryptoKitties, and the Dapper Wallet, and operates licensed digital-collectible marketplaces including NBA Top Shot, NFL All Day, LaLiga Golazos, UFC Strike, and Disney Pinnacle. Its developer surface ("Dapper Core") exposes Cadence smart contracts, the Dapper Wallet / Dapper Connect authentication flow, and Flow blockchain SDKs so third parties can build on top of Dapper's collectibles and on-chain assets rather than through a traditional REST/OpenAPI API.

companies.description: Dare Drop is a gaming influencer marketing platform that connects game publishers and brands with content creators across Twitch, YouTube, and TikTok. The platform runs reward-driven "Dares" — challenges that incentivize streamers and creators to produce longer, more engaging content around a title, while automating creator targeting, campaign management, and reporting. Dare Drop offers influencer campaigns, ongoing influencer programs, and organic outreach, and has facilitated over 18,000 publisher Dares and distributed more than 30,000 rewards to creator communities. Its customers include game studios and publishers such as EA, Respawn, Raw Fury, Tencent, Obsidian, and Gearbox. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been found to date.

It serves asset owners, general contractors, and engineering and consulting firms across roads, highways, rail, bridges, and earthworks, giving multi-site visibility from design validation through construction to final inspection. The company reports 125+ active customers, thousands of managed sites, and tens of thousands of processed drone flights. Datumate has Israeli engineering roots (Technion) with leadership based in Miami, Florida, and is backed by Battery Ventures.

companies.name: Daupler
companies.description: Daupler provides a cloud-based Response Management System (RMS) for utilities, public works, and service organizations that automates and coordinates emergency and service-request response. Its product suite spans Daupler Answering (after-hours call center), Dispatch Assist and AI-driven call management, Callout crew notification, Notify mass notification via SMS/email/phone, Engage customer portal, Event Detection for multi-incident coordination, and Analytics for incident and team-performance insight. Daupler serves water, sewer, electric, multi-utility, trash-collection, and public-works operators. The RMS is built on RESTful services and integrates with CMMS, work-order, AMI, IoT sensor, billing, CIS, CRM, OMS, GIS, and citizen-request systems, though Daupler exposes no public self-serve developer API or documentation. Backed by Techstars.

companies.description: DELLI is a UK online marketplace for independent food and drink makers, founded in 2022 by Depop founder Simon Beckerman with co-founder Marie Petrovicka. Often described as "the Depop for food," DELLI curates niche and small-batch products — snacks, sauces and condiments, pantry staples, drinks, alcohol, sweets and lifestyle goods — from micro-bakers, picklers, olive-oil producers and drink makers, and sells them to consumers, in part through a drop-style release model. The platform has since evolved into an AI-powered companion for makers and retailers, adding tools that cut the operational overhead of running a small food business. DELLI is backed by Balderton Capital and HV Capital, the original investors in Depop. The storefront runs on Shopify; DELLI publishes no first-party developer API at this time.

companies.name: DevAI
companies.description: DevAI (DevAI Solutions, Inc.) is a Silicon Valley enterprise IT company, founded in 2024 by Susie Wee (CEO) and Edwin Zhang, that builds agentic AI for IT operations teams. Its DevAI Network Intelligence Engine reconciles data across fragmented IT tools of record (CMDB, vCenter, NetBox and other infrastructure, network, compute, and security systems) into a single trustworthy operational view, and its Network Intelligence Agent "Neo" streamlines IT planning, incident response, patch management, and security and compliance workflows through a chat interface. DevAI reports deployment at Fortune 50 enterprises and won Best-in-Show (Automation) at the AI Networking Summit 2025. The company raised a $6M seed round led by Emergence Capital with Pear VC, Base10 Partners, and Benchstrength. No public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal has been published to date; this profile captures the company identity and the security posture of its public web surface.

Sellers publish AI-powered catalogs, reach qualified buyer demand, and see live equipment searches in real time across categories such as subtractive manufacturing, forming, joining, surface treatment, and polymer processing, and OEMs including DMG Mori, Trumpf, Okuma, FANUC, and Mazak. Campers search national parks, state parks, RV resorts, and private land stays (farms, ranches, vineyards) in one app, with filters, Pro map layers (BLM/USFS land, cell coverage, dark skies), road-trip search, and free availability alerts. Hosts list and manage campsites, sync calendars, and take weekly payouts. Hipcamp integrates with campground reservation systems (ResNexus, Cloudbeds, Newbook, RMS, Bedful) but publishes no public developer API — /api and /graphql are internal-only. Surfaced as an a16z / Bond Capital / Slow Ventures portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Horizon Quantum Computing
companies.description: Horizon Quantum Computing is a Singapore-based quantum software company founded in 2018 by Dr. Joe Fitzsimons. It builds software infrastructure for quantum applications, centered on Triple Alpha, an integrated development environment that lets developers write hardware-agnostic quantum programs at multiple levels of abstraction and deploy them to quantum processors. Triple Alpha's final workflow step packages a program and deploys it as an API so developers can invoke quantum backends from Python scripts, web pages, and other technologies. Horizon operates its own quantum computing testbed at its Singapore headquarters and supports a range of external quantum processors, aiming to bridge the gap between today's quantum hardware and real-world applications. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or client SDK; API-based program deployment is offered to early-access users of the Triple Alpha platform.

companies.name: Hornet
companies.description: Hornet is a queer social networking platform operated by Queer Networks, Inc., serving the global LGBTQ+ community with more than 100 million users worldwide. The Hornet app combines profiles, feeds, live video, one-on-one video chat, messaging, and location-based discovery into a privacy-first digital home for gay men and the broader queer community. Backed by 500 Global (and previously part of BlueCity Holdings), Hornet operates as a consumer social/media company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs — so this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public identity, policy surface, and domain-security posture rather than developer artifacts. Hornet is number one in several key markets including France, Brazil, Turkey, and Taiwan, and monetizes through premium subscriptions and queer-audience advertising.

companies.name: Housable
companies.description: Housable is a California-focused proptech company that helps rental-property owners and operators develop Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) as a portfolio value-add strategy. Its platform manages ADU projects end to end — from concept and financial feasibility analysis through design, permitting, bidding, construction, and lease-up — and lets operators run many parallel developments across their properties at once, converting underused spaces such as leasing offices, garages, and parking areas into new rental units alongside ground-up ADU construction. Housable is an early-stage startup backed by Kindred Ventures and other seed investors. It is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Housewhisper
companies.description: HouseWhisper (legal name Real Estate Productivity, Inc.) is a Seattle-based AI platform for real estate teams and brokerages, founded by former Zillow executives. It acts as a 24/7 AI teammate that automates the full lead lifecycle through personalized voice and text conversations: a Lead Engine that re-engages and revives cold database contacts, a Rules Engine that routes leads to the right agent with fallback escalations, and an AI Teammate that handles CRM updates, follow-ups, scheduling, reminders, and administrative busywork by call or text. It connects to real estate CRM, dialer, and calendar systems via API keys with no data migration, integrating with Follow Up Boss, Sierra Interactive, kvCORE, MoxiWorks, Salesforce, Lofty, HubSpot, and others. Pricing is outcome-based (a small monthly platform fee plus referral fees on closed deals). HouseWhisper has raised roughly $10M in seed funding led by Mayfield. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

The company operates on a commission model and also runs an operating-partner and affiliate programme. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is currently published.

companies.name: National Bank of Canada
companies.description: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada, TSX: NA) is a Schedule I chartered bank headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, founded in 1859. It is the sixth-largest of Canada's Big Six banks and the leading bank in Quebec, serving personal, commercial, wealth-management, and financial-markets clients. On open finance, National Bank is a notable first-mover: it was the first major Canadian bank to launch a secure, consent-based data-sharing API for retail customers, but it does NOT operate a public self-serve first-party developer portal. Programmatic access to customer financial data is delivered through aggregators rather than a downloadable public API — principally Flinks, the Montreal aggregator in which National Bank holds an ~80% stake, via its Open Banking Environment (OBE), and also through Plaid. National Bank and Flinks are founding participants of the FDX Canada working group, aligning their data-sharing on the FDX technical standard, and the bank is positioning ahead of Canada's forthcoming, legislated-but-not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FCAC oversight). Today access is voluntary and aggregator-mediated; there is no operational open-banking mandate and no public first-party API surface.

companies.name: REST API
companies.description: Representational State Transfer (REST) is an architectural style for designing networked applications using standard HTTP methods and stateless communication between client and server. REST APIs define how client and server applications communicate over the web using GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and PATCH methods against resource-oriented URLs. REST is the dominant API paradigm, used by 89% of organisations as their primary API format. This index covers the REST API landscape including specifications, tools, frameworks, best practices, and educational resources.

companies.name: REST Services
companies.description: Representational State Transfer (REST) is an architectural style for designing networked applications using stateless communication and standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) to interact with resources identified by URLs. REST services underpin modern web APIs and support the full software development lifecycle from design through deployment and maintenance. This index covers REST service implementations, frameworks, best practices, patterns, tooling, and educational resources that guide how REST services are built, managed, and consumed.

companies.name: Sallie Mae Bank
companies.description: Sallie Mae Bank is a Utah state-chartered industrial bank (industrial loan company) founded on November 28, 2005 and headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, operating as the FDIC-insured banking subsidiary (FDIC cert #58177) of SLM Corporation (NASDAQ SLM), the publicly traded, S&P 400 consumer-finance company best known as the largest originator of private student loans in the United States. Beyond student and education lending, the bank offers retail deposit products including high-yield savings accounts, money market accounts, and certificates of deposit through salliemae.com. Sallie Mae Bank does not operate a first-party public developer program - there is no developer.salliemae.com portal, no api.salliemae.com host, and no published OpenAPI/Swagger definitions. Consumer account and transaction data is reachable only on a permissioned basis through third-party data aggregators (historically Plaid), and no first-party FDX data-access API or published CFPB Section 1033 data-rights posture could be confirmed. This is an identity-only, aggregator-access record reflecting the honest reality that this institution exposes no public API surface.

companies.name: Stel

Its cellular-enabled vitals hubs and connected medical devices — blood pressure monitors, pulse oximeters, glucometers, thermometers, and scales — let patients transmit vital-sign readings to electronic health record (EHR) systems without WiFi, broadband, a smartphone, or app setup, targeting elderly, low-income, rural, and low-tech-literacy populations. Health systems and digital health organizations use Stel across the care continuum, from wellness and chronic-care management to hospital-at-home. Stel is backed by Bloomberg Beta.

companies.name: Thruster
companies.description: Thruster was a yield-first decentralized exchange (DEX) built natively on the Blast Ethereum Layer 2, offering Uniswap-style v2 and v3 concentrated liquidity AMMs, a stableswap AMM, and a token launchpad. Backed by Pantera Capital, the protocol shut down on July 29, 2025 after completing THRUST holder redemptions; its thruster.finance website is offline, while the GitBook documentation and the ThrusterX GitHub organization (Solidity contracts and audit reports) remain the surviving public record. No REST/HTTP API was published; the developer surface was on-chain smart contracts on Blast.

companies.name: Turquoise Health
companies.description: Turquoise Health is a healthcare price transparency company (backed by a16z) that runs a platform aggregating and normalizing hospital and payer machine-readable price transparency files, negotiated contract rates, and out-of-network pricing into searchable, benchmarked rate data and analytics. Its products span rate analysis and benchmarking, contract management, clear rates and data assets, healthcare transactions, out-of-network pricing, patient cost estimates / Good Faith Estimates, and price-transparency compliance tooling, serving providers, payers, life sciences, and employers.

Its white-labeled Grower Portal (web and mobile) gives ag retailers a branded storefront, CRM, sales enablement, digital billing, and integrated payments, while its Nexus product extends the platform to manufacturers and distributors across the ag supply chain. The platform integrates with major ag and energy ERPs, agronomy planning tools, and grain and financing systems, and exposes an API Access Driver that lets customers pull structured platform data into external reporting and BI tools such as Power BI. companies.description: Archer Aviation is a U.S. eVTOL aircraft company developing Midnight, a piloted four-passenger all-electric aircraft designed for rapid back-to-back urban flights of roughly 20-50 miles with a ~10 minute charge between trips. Archer is pursuing FAA Type Certification and operates through commercial and defense business lines. Key partnerships include Stellantis (contract manufacturing at Archer's Covington, Georgia facility), United Airlines (launch routes including the Manhattan-Newark corridor), and a Launch Edition program in the United Arab Emirates with Abu Dhabi Aviation. Archer also has a dedicated defense division (Archer Defense) developing hybrid VTOL platforms with Anduril and supporting U.S. government missions. The company trades on the NYSE under ACHR.

Atari does not publish a general-purpose public REST API; its developer surface is limited to Atari VCS content-submission guidance (developers email vcs@atari.com and use the VCS submission portal) and legacy HTML5 Atari Arcade SDK libraries on GitHub. companies.name: Berkshire Grey

Berkshire Grey originally went public via SPAC merger with Revolution Acceleration Acquisition Corp in 2021, then entered into a definitive merger agreement with SoftBank Group in 2023 (approximately $375M / $1.40 per share) and is now operated as a private SoftBank portfolio company. Integration with warehouse-management systems is delivered through a proprietary RESTful API surfaced via professional services and a 24/7 remote monitoring and predictive-maintenance support model; the API, BG-OS platform, and any associated SDKs are not publicly documented, and Berkshire Grey does not operate a public developer portal, downloadable SDK, or open-source release for its robotic operating environment.

companies.name: CodeKarma
companies.description: CodeKarma is a production intelligence platform that maps 100% of production traffic directly to source code, giving engineering teams and AI agents code-level visibility into how software actually behaves in production. Its products include KarmaLens (an IDE plugin for JetBrains and VS Code surfacing dead code, method frequency, and performance hotspots), KarmaDomain (live API-level dependency graphs across microservices, databases, and async systems), KarmaPulse (an operations command center with API health, error drift, and AI root cause analysis), and KarmaIQ (an MCP server that feeds production context to AI coding agents such as Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Claude). Deployed as managed SaaS or bring-your-own-cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), CodeKarma is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and collects only behavioral telemetry — no PII, payloads, or request bodies. Founded by Anantharam Vanchi Prakash and Priyanka Nahata, based in Bengaluru, India, and backed by Prosus, Accel, Xeed Ventures, SenseAI Ventures, and Stargazer Ventures.

companies.name: Ragas
companies.description: Ragas is an open-source evaluation toolkit for Large Language Model applications, with particular depth on Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and agentic systems. Originally created under the Exploding Gradients organization on GitHub and now maintained by Vibrant Labs AI, Ragas is a Python library distributed on PyPI under the Apache 2.0 license. It moves teams from informal "vibe checks" to systematic evaluation loops by providing objective LLM-based and traditional metrics, automated test dataset generation, experiment tracking, and integrations with the broader LLM ecosystem including LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, Anthropic, and popular observability platforms. Ragas exposes a metrics library covering faithfulness, response relevancy, context precision and recall, factual correctness, semantic similarity, agent tool-use accuracy, SQL equivalence, Nvidia-defined RAG metrics, and general-purpose rubric scoring. The project ships a CLI (`ragas`) with quickstart templates such as `rag_eval`, and is consumed primarily as a `pip install ragas` library rather than as a hosted API service. Ragas is widely cited as a default evaluation harness for RAG applications and has grown a substantial community on GitHub and Discord.

The platform draws on signals from billions of global mailboxes to measure inbox placement, sender reputation, and deliverability across major mailbox providers. Return Path exposes no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or developer portal today; its capabilities are delivered through the Validity email-success platform.

companies.name: B2B Bank
companies.description: B2B Bank is a Schedule I Canadian bank, headquartered in Toronto and wholly owned by Laurentian Bank of Canada (Laurentian Bank Financial Group). It operates a business-to-business, intermediary-only model: rather than serving retail consumers directly, it manufactures and distributes banking products through a network of roughly 27,000 financial professionals — financial advisors and their dealerships, deposit and mortgage brokers and their firms, mutual fund and insurance manufacturers, and CIRO (formerly MFDA/IIROC) members. Its product lines include investment loans, RSP and TFSA loans, broker deposits (GICs and high-interest savings/investment accounts), broker mortgages, and investment and banking accounts. The bank became a Schedule I bank and adopted the B2B Bank name in 2012, consolidating predecessor trust businesses (North American Trust, Sun Life Trust), and its deposits are CDIC insured. On open finance, B2B Bank publishes no first-party developer portal or public API: developer.b2bbank.com and api.b2bbank.com do not resolve, and the public site exposes only gated advisor/broker applications (Advisor Access, EASE online loans, Group Access, Investor Access, online banking). Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework is legislated but not yet operational, and the bank documents no FDX participation, Interac data-sharing API, or aggregator program of its own — consistent with an intermediary bank whose digital surface is partner-gated rather than developer-facing.

It is a consumer-facing application and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

It guides implementation through buy-vs-build decisions and vendor recommendations, and runs a continuous monitoring loop that tracks progress and measures business impact. Doczen targets enterprises across financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, energy, technology, and transportation and logistics, and integrates with hundreds of tools. EasyHealth emphasizes reaching underserved and hard-to-reach populations, claiming roughly 40% member engagement versus traditional sub-10% rates. The company is backed by Anthemis and QED Investors and is profiled here as an API Evangelist network company. EasyHealth publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

Microhealth is a patient- and clinician-facing application platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

Unlike UK and Australian institutions bound by mandated open-banking contracts, and unlike US banks such as Capital One or Chase that publish first-party developer portals, Santander Bank N.A. exposes no public, first-party developer API for its US retail franchise: developer.santanderbank.com does not resolve, and the site publishes no developers/API/open-banking pages. Consumer-permissioned data access in the US is available today through aggregators rather than a direct API — Plaid supports "Santander - Personal" (Assets, Auth, Balance and Transactions). Santander's UK developer portal (developer.santander.co.uk) and the group's Corporate & Investment Banking API marketplace (apimarket.santandercib.com) are operated by separate legal entities and are not the US retail bank's surface. This record is an honest identity profile of a super-regional bank whose US open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated, with no documented first-party developer program.

companies.name: Security Service Federal Credit Union
companies.description: Security Service Federal Credit Union (SSFCU), headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative federally chartered and insured by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). It is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, serving members across Texas, Colorado, and Utah with consumer and business banking, deposit accounts, credit cards, auto and mortgage lending, and investment services through branches, online banking, and mobile apps. Its open-finance posture is the norm for a US credit union: there is no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification, and no public FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API is documented. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party aggregators, and any API capability is delivered through its core banking provider rather than a self-serve developer program.

companies.name: Solvo.ai
companies.description: Solvo.ai is a revenue-orchestration company building the decision layer for revenue management in container logistics. Its live pricing engine ingests market rates, capacity manifests, booking history, port congestion, customer behaviour and contract terms, then uses models trained on tens of millions of historical bookings to produce a ranked, capacity-aware rate recommendation per lane, equipment type and segment. Trade managers accept, adjust or override these recommendations on Solvo's Decision HUB, and every decision feeds back as training signal through a bidirectional integration with the carrier's commercial stack. Founded in 2021 and backed by Speedinvest, Solvo positions itself as the only proven, live pricing engine built specifically for container shipping, with one of the world's top carriers in production. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio company; Solvo currently publishes a marketing and insights site only, with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs or specifications.

companies.name: SouthState Bank
companies.description: SouthState Bank, National Association is an OCC-chartered national commercial bank headquartered in Winter Haven, Florida, and the principal subsidiary of SouthState Bank Corporation (NASDAQ: SSB). Formed through the 2020 merger of South State Corporation and CenterState Bank and redomiciled to Florida in 2025, it holds roughly $67 billion in assets and operates across the Southeast, Texas, Colorado, and Virginia. Like most US regional banks, SouthState runs no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definitions. Consumer-permissioned data access is delivered through third-party aggregators rather than a direct API: the Open Banking Tracker records SouthState reachable via Plaid only, with no documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) endpoint and no published CFPB Section 1033 data-access surface. Its open-finance posture is therefore aggregator-mediated, not a self-serve developer program.

companies.name: Sparkles
companies.description: Sparkles (sparkles.dev) is a San Francisco developer-tools startup in Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch building AI coding agents for a whole team, not just engineers. A technical owner connects the company's GitHub repositories and configures environment variables, after which any teammate on a company email address can describe a change and have an agent implement it inside an isolated sandbox and open a GitHub pull request for developer review. Positioned as "Lovable for existing projects," it lets marketers, designers, and operations staff ship safe code changes without needing to know Git or the command line. As of this profile Sparkles exposes only a marketing and product website plus legal pages; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, CLI, or OpenAPI, so this record captures verified company identity rather than an API surface.

companies.name: STAND+
companies.description: STAND+ is a Techstars-backed footwear company making biomechanically engineered "energy-recovery" shoes for people who spend long hours standing or walking - healthcare workers, frontline and workforce professionals, athletes, and everyday movers. Its proprietary midsole is designed to dissipate and disperse impact energy outward rather than returning it into the joints, which the company markets for fatigue and pain reduction. The product lineup includes the AntiGrav1, AntiGrav2, and AG3 recovery shoes, the Gales Pro and Gales Frontline workforce and healthcare lines, and standalone recovery insoles. STAND+ is APMA (American Podiatric Medical Association) certified and HSA/FSA eligible through a Truemed partnership. This is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand (standshoes.com) with no public developer API, SDK, or integration surface at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: StorSimple
companies.description: StorSimple was a Santa Clara, California hybrid cloud storage company founded in 2009 by Ursheet Parikh and Guru Pangal. Its appliances combined primary storage, tiered cloud archiving, deduplication, compression, and encryption behind iSCSI/SMB interfaces, backed by $31.5M from Index Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Ignition Partners, and Mayfield Fund. Microsoft acquired StorSimple in November 2012 and folded it into Azure as Azure StorSimple (8000 series physical and virtual arrays, plus the StorSimple Data Manager). The product is managed through Azure Resource Manager under the Microsoft.StorSimple resource provider and its REST API. Azure StorSimple reached end-of-life in December 2022 and is out of support; Microsoft directs customers to Azure File Sync and Azure Files.

companies.name: TeamViewer
companies.description: TeamViewer is a global provider of remote connectivity, remote access, and remote support software used by IT teams, MSPs, and enterprises to manage devices, deliver IT support, and connect operational technology across desktops, mobile devices, and IoT endpoints. The TeamViewer Web API is a RESTful API that uses OAuth 2.0 bearer token authentication and JSON to programmatically manage users, devices, groups, sessions, session reports, and meetings within a TeamViewer company account.

companies.name: The Atlas Marketplace
companies.description: The Atlas Marketplace (branded "The Atlas") is a free online community and knowledge marketplace for local government leaders. Officials and staff use it to learn from their peers about the smart, safe, and sustainable solutions working in their communities, browsing a searchable library of case studies, vendors, and civic-technology projects. The platform connects public-sector practitioners with the companies and partners behind proven municipal solutions across mobility, infrastructure, sustainability, and public safety. Backed by 500 Global, it operates as a content and community website rather than a developer/API product; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from its public web presence.

companies.name: Transposon Therapeutics
companies.description: Transposon Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing transformational therapies for neurodegenerative and aging-related diseases driven by LINE-1 retrotransposon activity. Its lead asset, TPN-101 (censavudine), is a potent oral inhibitor of LINE-1 reverse transcriptase in late-stage development for progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) / frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and Alzheimer's disease. The pipeline also includes follow-on novel nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) and Protein Kinase R inhibitors (PKRi) targeting pathways activated by LINE-1 and implicated in cognitive impairment. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a corporate marketing website only and no public API, developer, or machine-readable surface.

companies.name: truBrain
companies.description: truBrain is a Santa Monica, California nootropics and functional-beverage brand that makes "natural superfuels for performance" — drinkable nootropic shots (2,000mg of natural nootropics per 1oz bottle for focus and motivation), drinkable ketones (Ketone XL, 11g of pure ketones per shot for athletic energy and recovery), plus gummies, functional-mushroom blends, capsules, NAD+, hydration, and sleep supplements, packaged in recycled paper bottles. Founded by a team of neuroscientists and backed by 500 Global, the company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront and has run a Regulation A+ public equity offering. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. truBrain is a consumer packaged-goods company: it publishes no first-party developer API, documentation, or SDKs. The only machine-readable surface at its domain is Shopify's Customer Accounts OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 discovery metadata.

companies.description: Twingate is a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) platform that replaces legacy VPNs with software-defined perimeters, providing identity-based, least-privilege access to private resources without exposing them to the public internet. The Twingate Admin API is a GraphQL API authenticated via API key (X-API-KEY header) that enables programmatic management of remote networks, connectors, resources, users, groups, service accounts, devices, policies, and DNS filtering profiles.

companies.name: Tyra Biosciences
companies.description: Tyra Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company (NASDAQ: TYRA) based in Carlsbad, California, focused on developing next-generation precision medicines that address the emergence of tumor resistance and other challenges in existing treatment options. Tyra's proprietary in-house SNAP discovery platform combines advanced protein crystallography with structure-based drug design, producing full structural "SNAPshots" of the real-world interaction between a drug and its target in as little as seven days rather than weeks to months. This rapid, sequential structural iteration lets the team refine molecular designs to angstrom-level precision and design selective inhibitors intended to deliver deeper, more durable responses for patients, including in cancers where resistance mutations block first-generation drugs. Tyra was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a therapeutics company and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

companies.name: Unisub LLC
companies.description: UniSub is a recurring crypto-payments platform that lets merchants accept automated on-chain subscriptions and deposits directly from customer wallets (MetaMask, WalletConnect, Coinbase Wallet) in USDT, USDC, DAI, WBTC, WETH and other ERC20/Polygon tokens across EVM-compatible chains. Subscriptions are executed by audited smart contracts, and merchants integrate through an embeddable payment widget, checkout links, or per-merchant API/webhooks, with a hosted dashboard for subscribers and analytics. A 500 Global portfolio company based in Batumi, Georgia, UniSub also publishes its SubscriptionApp smart contracts and a The Graph subgraph on GitHub.

companies.name: Xalts
companies.description: Xalts (operated by Tokuten Pte Ltd) is an Accel-backed fintech building an AI agent platform for corporate treasury and finance teams — a copilot that automates trade finance operations (guarantees, trade payments, documentary credit and collections), liquidity management, and revenue operations. Task-specific agents learn internal processes and policies and integrate with ERPs, accounting systems, payment processors, and banks through the company's Omni Connect Protocol, which provides multi-bank connectivity via a single API. Xalts does not currently publish a public developer portal or API documentation; its connectivity APIs are offered to enterprise customers.

companies.name: Zwift
companies.description: Zwift is a Long Beach, California online fitness company that operates a multiplayer indoor cycling and running platform combining stationary smart trainers and bikes with a 3D virtual-world game client. Riders and runners use a smart trainer, smart bike (such as the in-house Zwift Ride), treadmill, or pod to drive an avatar through fictional worlds (Watopia, Makuri Islands) and licensed real-world routes, joining structured workouts, group rides, races, training plans, and 24/7 events alongside a global community of more than a million members. The platform pairs with smart trainers and heart-rate monitors over Bluetooth and ANT+, and the Zwift Companion mobile app provides in-game messaging, ride control, and route discovery. Zwift does not operate a general public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, or open-source SDK. Its developer surface is limited to a private, application-only Structured Training API for approved training partners (TrainingPeaks, TrainerRoad, Wahoo SYSTM, JOIN Cycling and similar coaching platforms) that lets external workout builders push custom workouts into a rider's Zwift account, plus one-way activity-export connections to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Garmin Connect, MapMyRide, MapMyRun, Adidas Running, Technogym, Fitbit, Wahoo, Apple Health, and Withings. There is no public REST surface, OAuth client registration, or partner self-service available to general developers — third-party tools (community libraries, ZwiftPower, Sauce for Zwift) interact with Zwift via reverse-engineered private endpoints, not a sanctioned API. Zwift is a paid consumer subscription business; revenue comes from monthly memberships and hardware sales (Zwift Ride, Zwift Cog, Zwift Click, Zwift Play).

It serves property management, home restoration, electrical / plumbing / HVAC trades, municipalities, home health and hospice, healthcare, legal, landscaping, and travel and hospitality clients. All City Communications is a service business and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

companies.description: AppliedVR is a virtual reality therapeutics company that combines immersive technology with proven cognitive behavioral and behavioral-science techniques to treat medical conditions, with a focus on chronic pain. Its lead product, RelieVRx, is the first FDA-authorized prescription VR device for chronic lower back pain, delivering automated, self-administered cognitive behavioral therapy in the patient's home. AppliedVR also offers the SustainVR and ITx immersive therapeutics platform and the AVR Pathway patient-support system, and validates its products through clinical academic research. The company operates as a regulated digital-therapeutics / medical-device business rather than a developer-facing API platform, so it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

The agents scope changes across integrated ERP, CRM, and HRIS systems, understand cross-system dependencies, implement and validate modifications, and keep a complete audit trail so teams can review agent work, approve modifications, and revert individual changes or restore a system to a prior state. Assemble is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company targeting IT and business-systems teams managing complex enterprise transformations. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or OpenAPI, so only its verified public identity and website properties are captured.

companies.name: Astrix Security
companies.description: Astrix Security is a cybersecurity company providing identity security for AI agents and non-human identities (NHIs) — the API keys, OAuth apps, service accounts, SSH keys, and MCP servers that fall outside traditional human IAM. Its platform lets enterprises discover a real-time inventory of every AI agent and NHI with business and risk context, secure them by remediating excessive privileges, misconfigurations, and abnormal or malicious activity, and deploy agentic AI safely via an Agent Control Plane that provisions short-lived, tightly scoped credentials. Founded by Alon Jackson and Idan Gour and headquartered in Boston, Astrix is backed by CRV, Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, F2, and Anthropic. The company was acquired by Cisco and ended standalone sales of new licenses effective June 30, 2026.

Users swipe to mark messages done or save them for later, compose replies by voice in their own writing style, receive smart notifications with email summaries, and search their mailbox with natural-language AI. Founded in 2024 by CEO Jonathan Unikowski and backed at seed stage by Bloomberg Beta and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Avec is a consumer productivity product rather than an API provider - it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

Commercial sellers and dealer groups can push inventory straight from their own systems into OPENLANE Sell via OPENLANE Connect, a lightweight dealer integration API with a dedicated test environment. companies.name: Baubap
companies.description: Baubap is a Mexican fintech offering instant personal microloans through an Android mobile app. Founded in 2018 in Mexico City by Roberto Salcedo and Luis Villarreal, it grants loans from $500 to roughly $9,000 MXN in minutes with no credit-bureau check and no income verification, using its own AI/ML-based alternative-scoring model to serve underbanked and no-credit-history borrowers. On-time repayment unlocks progressively larger amounts and helps users build a positive credit history. Baubap operates as a regulated SOFOM registered with CONDUSEF and supervised by CNBV, complying with Mexican data-protection and financial-security regulations. It has no public developer API; this profile captures the company's identity, its published /llms.txt, and its domain-security posture.

companies.name: Beeline Bikes
companies.description: Beeline Bikes (now operating as Beeline Connect) is a B2B software platform for the bicycle industry that links riders, retailers, and brands across North America, with roughly 3,300 participating retailers. The platform provides real-time service scheduling and 24/7 appointment booking, live market inventory management, test-ride booking, local bicycle assembly coordination, warranty submission and reimbursement tracking, an affiliate e-commerce sales channel with revenue sharing to local dealers, and a dynamic dealer locator. It supports both mobile and in-shop retail operations and serves established brands such as Aventon, Priority, Lectric, and Pedego. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or integration surface has been found at this time.

companies.name: BillTrim
companies.description: BillTrim is a consumer bill-management and negotiation service that helps households lower, monitor, and pay their recurring bills. Its team negotiates with providers on the customer's behalf (up to twice a year), watches for price increases before autopay processes, and can pay bills automatically from a connected bank account. BillTrim advertises support for 20,000+ service providers across internet, cable, phone, insurance, and other recurring household expenses. Backed by 500 Global, it operates as a consumer-facing web and mobile application; no public developer API or developer portal is currently published.

companies.name: Billtrust
companies.description: Billtrust is an AI-powered accounts receivable and B2B payments technology company that helps businesses accelerate cash flow by automating the order-to-cash cycle. Its platform spans automated invoicing and invoice delivery, B2B payment acceptance across multiple modalities, AI-driven cash application that matches payments to invoices, intelligent collections, credit decisioning, and a B2B eCommerce storefront. Billtrust connects to more than 40 ERP systems and 260+ accounts-payable portals, serving manufacturing, distribution, equipment, medical, retail, transportation, and business-services companies. This API Evangelist profile was seeded from the Bain Capital Ventures portfolio; Billtrust does not currently publish an open public developer portal or OpenAPI, so enrichment captures its identity, compliance program, and domain security posture from public surfaces.

companies.name: Bindery
companies.description: Bindery (Bindery Books) is a community-driven, influencer-led book publishing platform and marketplace founded by Matt Kaye and Meg Harvey. It pairs established book "tastemakers" — social-media book reviewers and BookTok / Bookstagram creators — with emerging authors, letting each tastemaker run their own micro-imprint (Ezeekat Press, Boundless Press, Skies Press, and others), acquire titles, weigh in on creative decisions, and promote them to their communities in exchange for a share of net earnings. Often described as "Patreon meets publishing," Bindery combines traditional trade distribution and marketing with paid membership communities, a bookshop, exclusive reviews and author interviews, and iOS and Android apps. The company is backed by Bloomberg Beta.

companies.name: Bloomy
companies.description: Bloomy (bloomylearning.com) is an AI-powered adaptive learning platform for K-12 students, founded by Alex Southmayd and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). The product diagnoses each student's knowledge gaps, builds a personalized standards-aligned learning path across English Language Arts, Math, and Writing, and delivers Socratic AI tutoring plus mastery-based practice, requiring 90%+ mastery before a student advances. It integrates third-party diagnostic/assessment data (i-Ready, NWEA MAP) and provides a real-time teacher dashboard. Bloomy serves traditional districts, charter schools, homeschools, and microschools, and sells to families via monthly or annual subscriptions (with ESA/EFA fund eligibility in some states). As of this profile Bloomy publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; this record captures its verified public identity and legal/account surface only.

companies.name: Bravo Sierra
companies.description: Bravo Sierra is an American personal care company founded in New York City in 2018, building high-performance, clean body care for the most active people. Its "military-native" line — deodorant, body wash, cleansing bars, body fragrance, hair styling paste, and antibacterial body wipes — is designed and field-tested with U.S. Special Operations Forces (starting with the 75th Ranger Regiment's 2nd Battalion) and manufactured in the USA. The direct-to-consumer brand runs on Shopify, offers subscriptions, and gives back a portion of every sale to programs supporting active service members, veterans, and their families. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; it publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures identity and the store's first-party well-known discovery and domain-security surface.

companies.name: Cera
companies.description: Cera is a United Kingdom-based digital-first home healthcare company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, that describes itself as Europe's largest provider of in-home care. Cera delivers home care, live-in care, nurse-led and complex care, extra-care housing, supported living, and specialist learning-disability and autism support, all wrapped around a proprietary digital platform that uses data analytics and machine learning so its network of carers can collect, monitor, and react to vital-sign and health-condition changes in real time. Cera positions this technology as a remote-monitoring and predictive layer that surfaces deterioration in health earlier and reduces hospitalisations across its United Kingdom home-care operations. As of this review Cera exposes no public developer portal, no self-serve REST API, and no HL7 FHIR endpoint or CapabilityStatement; its platform is an internal, operator-facing product delivered through consumer and carer mobile apps rather than a documented partner API. This profile is an honest identity-only stub recording the absence of a public API surface for a United Kingdom telehealth-adjacent home-care provider.

companies.name: Cheaf
companies.description: Cheaf is a mobile food-rescue marketplace that connects supermarkets, restaurants, bakeries, and food retailers holding surplus inventory with consumers who buy it as discounted "surprise packages" at pickup, cutting food waste while helping merchants recover value on stock that would otherwise be thrown away. Founded in Mexico in 2020, the consumer app operates across Mexico, Chile, and Argentina, has more than 3.5 million users, and reports millions of kilograms of food rescued and greenhouse-gas emissions avoided. Businesses list surplus through a merchant onboarding portal and pay a commission on sales; consumers browse and reserve packages through the mobile app. This API Evangelist profile tracks Cheaf's public web and developer surface; Cheaf is a consumer/merchant mobile platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation.

companies.name: Cherrypick
companies.description: Cherrypick is a London-based food-tech company (backed by Speedinvest) behind an all-in-one meal-planning and grocery-shopping mobile app. The app helps home cooks discover personalized recipes tailored to their dietary preferences, automatically plan their weekly meals, and turn those plans into a supermarket basket at real supermarket prices for home delivery or in-store pickup. Positioned as a lower-cost alternative to recipe-box subscription services, Cherrypick combines recipe discovery, meal planning, and grocery ordering into a single consumer experience aimed at saving people time and money while reducing food waste. Cherrypick is a consumer mobile application with no public developer, API, or partner-integration surface at this time; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a network entity rather than an API producer.

companies.name: Cimulate
companies.description: Cimulate is an AI-native commerce experience platform for intelligent product discovery, delivering context-aware search, adaptive browse, real-time recommendations, a conversational AI shopping assistant, and Commerce AEO (answer/agent engine optimization for visibility inside LLM surfaces like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude). The platform is architected API-first and headless-ready and advertises a proprietary Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for agentic commerce workflows. Cimulate became part of Salesforce in February 2026. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Sierra Ventures.

companies.description: Cooleaf is an employee engagement, recognition, and rewards platform built by ITA Group that helps HR and people leaders create lasting engagement across their organizations. companies.name: SNMP
companies.description: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is the foundational IETF standard for monitoring and managing network devices. SNMP defines a request/response protocol over UDP (ports 161 and 162) for retrieving and altering management variables exposed by agents on routers, switches, servers, UPSs, and other equipment, plus an asynchronous trap/notification channel for event delivery. The protocol family spans three major generations — SNMPv1 (RFC 1157), SNMPv2c (RFC 1901-1908), and the modular SNMPv3 architecture (RFC 3411-3418, extended by RFC 7860 for HMAC-SHA-2 authentication) — and is paired with the Structure of Management Information (SMI) and a vast catalog of MIB modules, most notably the IF-MIB (RFC 2863) for network interfaces. SNMP remains the lingua franca of network monitoring, consumed primarily by NMS platforms such as Nagios, Zabbix, PRTG, SolarWinds, LibreNMS, and Observium, and implemented in open source primarily by the Net-SNMP suite.
