companies.name: Blink Identity
companies.description: Blink Identity is an Austin, Texas company building a privacy-first facial-recognition identity platform for live entertainment venues, stadiums, and public spaces. Its "identify-in-motion" machine-vision system lets patrons enroll with a smartphone photo, then walk through touchless entry, pay-with-your-face concessions, and automatic loyalty recognition without stopping to scan a ticket. Facial images are converted into encrypted templates rather than stored as photos, and the company is a Techstars Music alumnus that has partnered with Live Nation / Ticketmaster on facial-recognition ticketing. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website; Blink Identity does not currently publish a developer-facing API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Braveheart Bio
companies.description: Braveheart Bio is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and related cardiac conditions. Its lead candidate, BHB-1893, is a selective cardiac myosin inhibitor (licensed as HRS-1893 from Hengrui Pharma) designed to reduce excessive heart-muscle contraction and improve cardiac performance in patients with obstructive and non-obstructive HCM. The San Francisco-based company launched in November 2025 with a $185M Series A led by a16z alongside Forbion, OrbiMed, Enavate Sciences, and Frazier Life Sciences, and filed for a Nasdaq IPO in July 2026. Braveheart Bio is a corporate/scientific organization and does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs.

companies.name: Brine (Tanx)
companies.description: Brine — now rebranded as tanX — is a cross-chain, self-custodial orderbook decentralized exchange (DEX) built on StarkWare's StarkEx Layer-2 scaling engine. It combines the trustless, non-custodial security of a DEX with the speed and low fees of a centralized exchange: gasless trading, rapid off-chain order execution with on-chain settlement, cross-chain deposits and withdrawals, and simple APIs for programmatic trading. The company is backed by Pantera Capital and is repositioning around "a secure and compliant future for crypto." This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Pantera Capital's portfolio and enriched by the pipeline; as of this pass the public REST API host is no longer reachable and the developer surface is limited to the GitBook documentation.

companies.name: CANbridge Pharmaceuticals
companies.description: CANbridge Pharmaceuticals (CANbridge Life Sciences Ltd.) is a global, China-based biopharmaceutical company founded in 2012 that focuses on the research, development, and commercialization of transformative therapies for rare diseases and rare oncology. The company in-licenses and develops differentiated drug candidates from around the world for the Chinese and global markets, with a portfolio of approved products and a gene-therapy and enzyme-replacement pipeline. Headquartered in Beijing with offices in Shanghai, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Suzhou, and Burlington, Massachusetts (USA), CANbridge is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming; CANbridge publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

Convoke serves biopharma teams working in business development, competitive intelligence, portfolio strategy, market research, and medical affairs. The company raised an $8.6M seed round co-led by Kleiner Perkins and Dimension. As of this profile, Convoke publishes a public marketing and company site but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Edge Markets
companies.description: EDGE Markets builds financial infrastructure for high-throughput gaming and trading environments, positioning itself as the "financial backbone for a new asset class." Its product line spans EDGE Boost, a high-limit debit platform (up to a $1,000,000 daily limit) with built-in responsible-gaming controls and activity tracking; EDGE Connect, a private payment rail and closed-loop settlement layer that replaces traditional consumer card networks to cut transaction costs and chargebacks; and EDGE Pro, a banking platform (in development) for market makers and institutional investors. The company has raised a $29.2M Series A and partners with gaming and betting operators. companies.description: Evox Therapeutics is an Oxford, United Kingdom based biotechnology company developing genetic medicines that expand the reach of gene therapy into the brain to transform the treatment landscape for severe neurodegenerative diseases. Evox is a venture backed life-sciences company (investors include GV) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes a corporate and scientific website but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Formation Bio
companies.description: Formation Bio is an AI-native pharmaceutical company building the pharma company of the future. Rather than applying AI to drug discovery, it focuses on drug development — acquiring and in-licensing clinical-stage drug candidates from pharma companies, universities, and biotech firms, then running them through clinical development far more efficiently than industry standards using its proprietary AI-native platform, data, and fine-tuned models. Led by CEO Benjamine Liu and CTO Linhao Zhang, the company raised a $372M Series D in 2024 led by a16z with participation from Sanofi, Sequoia, Thrive, Emerson Collective, and others, and partners with Sanofi and OpenAI on custom models for the drug development lifecycle. Formation Bio does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface.

companies.name: Genial Care
companies.description: Genial Care is a Brazilian healthtech network providing multidisciplinary, evidence-based care for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and atypical development up to roughly eight years of age. Founded in 2020 in Sao Paulo, it operates a network of clinics ("Casas Geniais") across Greater Sao Paulo delivering ABA (applied behavior analysis), speech-language therapy, and occupational therapy, alongside family assessments, in-person and online consultations, educational content, and a professional training academy. Care is coordinated through a proprietary mobile app that supports continuous monitoring and family engagement. The company partners with major Brazilian health plans (operadoras), which account for the majority of its revenue, and is backed by General Catalyst. Genial Care operates as a consumer/clinical care provider and does not publish a public developer API surface.

companies.name: Granza Bio
companies.description: Granza Bio is an early-stage biotechnology company reprogramming immunity for target-specific medicines. Founded in 2024 by Dr. Ashwin Nandakumar, Dr. Ashwin Jainarayanan, and Prof. Michael Dustin, the company builds on the discovery of "attack particles" — killing entities released by cytotoxic immune cells, characterized in Prof. Dustin's laboratory at the University of Oxford. Granza Bio is developing an engineered delivery-shell platform that directs therapeutic cargo to specific tissues, with the goal of advancing treatments for cancers, autoimmune disorders, and infections. The company raised $7.14M in seed funding co-led by Refactor Capital and Felicis, with participation from Pioneer Fund and Y Combinator. It is a research-stage life-sciences company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

companies.name: HomeLight
companies.description: HomeLight is a San Francisco–based real-estate technology company that matches home buyers and sellers with top-performing local real-estate agents and operates a stack of consumer-facing products that span the entire residential transaction: agent matching, Simple Sale cash-offer marketplace, Buy Before You Sell (BBYS) bridge financing, HomeLight Home Loans (NMLS #1529229), the HomeLight HELOC Card, and HomeLight Closing Services for title and escrow. The company ranks agents using historical performance data on home sales (price, speed, volume, geography, property type) and routes consumer leads to a curated network of agents, lenders, and cash-buyer investors. HomeLight exposes a private Partner API to lenders, brokerages, CRMs, and marketing partners (NerdWallet is its largest partner) for submitting leads (`/api/partner_lead/v2`), Simple Sale seller leads (`/leads/partner_simple_sale_lead`), and duplicate-lead checks (`/api/partner_dupe_lead_check`); credentials are issued on a per-partner basis via support@homelight.com. Beyond the Partner API, HomeLight has direct integrations with most major real-estate agent CRMs (Follow Up Boss, BoomTown, Sierra Interactive, Firepoint, Real Geeks, Brivity, Chime, LionDesk, KW Command). HomeLight has no public, self-service developer portal — the Partner API is gated by a commercial relationship, and there is no public OpenAPI spec, SDK, or open-source client published by the company.

companies.name: Kinro
companies.description: Kinro is an AI-powered commercial insurance brokerage for small businesses, founded in the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch and based in San Francisco. Its autonomous AI agents run the full broker workflow around the clock, from prospect identification and quote preparation through comparison, binding, and ongoing certificate and renewal servicing. Kinro targets the roughly 77% of the 36 million U.S. small businesses that are underinsured because traditional brokers cannot profitably serve low-premium accounts. It is licensed across 30 states, appointed by 15+ carriers with access to 50+ markets, and offers general liability, business owner's policies, workers' compensation, commercial auto and trucking, professional liability, cyber, and more. Kinro was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Mangata Finance
companies.description: Mangata Finance (Mangata X, since rebranded GASP) is a decentralized exchange built as a Substrate parachain in the Polkadot and Kusama ecosystem. It is designed for algorithmic traders and DeFi frontends, offering gas-free swaps, an omnichain ZK-rollup architecture, and a Proof-of-Liquidity consensus model where liquidity providers help secure the network. There is no REST or OpenAPI surface; developers integrate through a TypeScript SDK (@mangata-finance/sdk) that communicates with the Mangata Substrate node over Polkadot.js JSON-RPC/WebSocket, with published type-definition packages and open-source node, bridge, and dev-kit repositories under the gasp-xyz GitHub organization.

companies.name: Menten AI
companies.description: Menten AI is a biotechnology company pioneering generative AI for peptide drug design. Its MAUD 1.0 platform designs peptide macrocycles de novo for complex, previously undruggable targets by combining generative AI with physics-based models and quantum simulations, reporting nanomolar potency, oral bioavailability, cell permeability, and a greater-than-90% hit rate. The company operates through enterprise partnerships with pharmaceutical organizations rather than a public developer platform, and at the time of this profile publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation. The company builds AI-powered intelligent welding cells that automate metal fabrication for defense shipyards, utility and energy infrastructure, data centers, and heavy industry. Its core technology is Obsidian, a physical-AI reinforcement-learning agent trained inside Path's proprietary Weld World Model on tens of millions of welded inches; Obsidian runs at the edge of each cell and makes real-time, seam-by-seam welding decisions using a sensor stack of two cameras plus four lasers that deliver sub-millimeter 360-degree awareness around the torch. Path markets the cells with a CapEx-free consumption model and reports 97%+ first-pass yield, 4x productivity, and 30% lower welding costs across customers including HII (America's largest military shipbuilder), Saronic, LAD Services, Tycrop, Mine Rite Technologies, and Millerbernd. In April 2026 Path announced Rove, a mobile welding system mounted on a quadruped platform, extending its addressable geometry beyond fixed-cell applications. The company has raised approximately $271M across Seed through Series D from Drive Capital, Matter Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Addition, and Yamaha Motor Ventures, with the most recent $100M Series D closing in October 2024. Path Robotics has no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; its GitHub organization contains roughly 50 repositories that are almost entirely upstream open-source forks (ROS, protobuf, abseil, ceres-solver, pytorch3d, etc.) used as internal build dependencies rather than published developer artifacts. Revenue is earned through welding-cell deployments, services, and the consumable weld-output model — not API monetization.

Paradigm delivers radiation-free intraoperative measurement, per-vertebra registration, and structured surgical data capture, reducing radiation exposure while streamlining surgical workflows. Founded in 2016 and backed by DCVC, Proprio is commercializing surgical navigation, real-time surgical intelligence, and a growing surgical data registry. companies.name: Generate Biomedicines
companies.description: Generate Biomedicines is a Somerville, Massachusetts therapeutics company pioneering Generative Biology, a machine-learning-driven approach to de novo protein design across antibodies, peptides, enzymes, and gene therapies. Founded out of Flagship Pioneering and chaired by Noubar Afeyan, the company trains generative models on the full compendium of natural protein structures and sequences plus proprietary wet-lab data to design novel protein therapeutics computationally rather than by trial-and-error discovery. Its open-source flagship is Chroma, a programmable diffusion-based generative model for joint protein structure and sequence design published in Nature 2023 ("Illuminating protein space with a programmable generative model", doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06728-8) and released on GitHub under Apache 2.0 with pretrained weights available under a custom Chroma Parameters License (free for academic and nonprofit use). Chroma uses equivariant graph neural networks, diffusion modeling, and conditional random fields to sample all-atom protein structures with sub-quadratic complexity, supporting conditional generation via composable Conditioner modules for symmetry, substructure, shape, and secondary-structure constraints. The internal Generate Platform iterates on a "generate, build, measure, learn" loop that pairs in-silico design with high-throughput protein synthesis and characterization; the company reports having generated, built, and tested more than 42,000 proteins. Generate Biomedicines has platform collaborations with Amgen (six programs, January 2022) and Novartis (multiple programs, September 2024) and a CAR T collaboration with Roswell Park. Its clinical pipeline is led by GB-0895, a long-acting anti-TSLP antibody for severe asthma now in Phase 3 (SOLAIRIA study) with a parallel Phase 1 in COPD, plus preclinical programs GB-4362 (anti-free-MMAE for ADC oncology safety) and GB-5267 (MUC16 armored CAR T for ovarian cancer). The company priced its initial public offering in February 2026. Revenue derives from drug development, partner collaborations, and (for Chroma) commercial weights licensing; there is no public developer REST/HTTPS API or SDK for the Generate Platform itself — Chroma is consumed as a Python library installed via pip with model weights downloaded from chroma-weights.generatebiomedicines.com after registering for an API key.

Mindgard's platform combines AI Discovery and Recon (mapping the AI attack surface and shadow AI usage), continuous AI Red Teaming against evolving attacker techniques, AI Assessment, AI Runtime Protection, and Model Scanning, backed by a research-led attack library covering jailbreaks (ActorAttack, Crescendo, EvilConfidant, PersonGPT, DevModeV2, AsciiArtAttack, AntiGPT), prompt-injection techniques (Ascii85, AnsiEscaped, AnsiRaw and others), and policy/violation testing (MaliciousGeneration, PromptAlignment). Developers and security teams integrate Mindgard via a public REST API (projects, tests, multi-turn tests, datasets, findings, reconnaissance), a Python CLI (`pip install mindgard`), a Python SDK, a Burp Suite extension, and a GitHub Action for adding red-team checks to MLOps pipelines. The company also maintains and contributes to open-source security tooling including PyRIT integrations, an OpenAI-compatible LLM-Guard proxy, a chatbot API wrapper for testing web chatbots, and proof-of-concept vulnerability demonstrations (document RCE in LangChain agents, hidden audio jailbreaks, prompt-jailbreak demos). Mindgard's commercial model is enterprise SaaS with platform and services tiers; pricing is gated behind a sales conversation, and the platform is positioned for security, AppSec, and AI governance teams testing customer-facing or internally deployed AI systems.

companies.name: Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP
companies.description: Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP is a global Am Law 10 firm with approximately 2,200 lawyers and 39 offices across North America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. The firm provides corporate, transactional, litigation, and regulatory services across energy, financial services, healthcare, life sciences, retail and ecommerce, sports, technology, and transportation, with widely recognized depth in employee benefits and executive compensation, fintech and financial services regulation, intellectual property, and M&A. Morgan Lewis does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or machine-readable data product; its public technology surface is limited to its corporate website, an email-alert subscription managed through a Real Magnet (REACTION) marketing platform, and a portfolio of LexBlog-style practice blogs covering specific subject areas.

companies.name: Nectar Social
companies.description: Nectar Social is an AI "social operating system" for consumer brands — an AI-powered social teammate that manages online communities, performs real-time social listening and sentiment analysis, tracks influencers, and turns organic social engagement and DM conversations into measurable revenue across community, brand safety, commerce, influencer, social-selling, and analytics use cases. Founded in 2023 by Misbah and Farah Uraizee and based in Bellevue, Washington, the company raised $30M from Menlo Ventures, GV (Google Ventures), and True Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; as of this enrichment pass Nectar Social ships a SaaS web application (app.nectarsocial.com) but does not publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

companies.name: OctoAI
companies.description: OctoAI (formerly OctoML) was a Seattle-based AI inference platform founded in 2019 as a University of Washington Allen School spin-out of the Apache TVM project. The company originally focused on machine-learning model optimization and compilation across CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators, and in June 2023 launched a generative-AI SaaS inference platform that served open-source foundation models (Llama 2, Mixtral, SDXL, Stable Diffusion, Whisper) behind OpenAI-style REST APIs with Python and TypeScript SDKs. In January 2024 OctoML formally rebranded to OctoAI and in April 2024 unveiled OctoStack, a self-contained generative-AI production stack for deploying models inside customer VPC and on-premises environments across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and AWS Inferentia. NVIDIA acquired OctoAI in September 2024 for a reported $165M (down from a 2021 peak valuation of ~$900M), with CEO Luis Ceze and key staff joining NVIDIA. OctoAI sent customers a "Wind down of OctoAI Services" notice and terminated all hosted endpoints, accounts, and SDK access on 31 October 2024. The octo.ai domain now 301-redirects to nvidia.com and no public OctoAI product, API, dashboard, or developer portal remains; the technology has been absorbed into NVIDIA's internal AI inference stack and is not separately purchasable. This catalog entry is a historical record of the former OctoAI developer surface and the GitHub artifacts that remain.

companies.name: Paperplane
companies.description: Paperplane is an AI sales-productivity tool (Y Combinator W23, backed by Bloomberg Beta) that automatically takes notes on sales calls and keeps a rep's CRM up to date. It connects to a team's calendar and to conversational intelligence and call-recording tools such as Gong and Chorus, transcribes and analyzes each call, then writes the results back to Salesforce — updating opportunity fields, notes, and action items so sales teams spend less time on manual CRM data entry and stay on top of their deals. The product is organized around opportunities, calls, and notes, with integrations for Google Calendar, Gong, Chorus, and Salesforce. Paperplane is a hosted SaaS application; as of this enrichment pass it exposes a product documentation site (GitBook, with an llms.txt index) but no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or SDK.

companies.name: Piris Labs
companies.description: Piris Labs is a Y Combinator (W2026) deep-tech startup building the networking layer for AI. The company develops proprietary photonic interconnect technology paired with a vertically optimized software stack that moves data between AI accelerators at ultra-low latency, targeting the bottleneck where up to 80% of advanced AI compute sits idle waiting on slow networking. Piris Labs couples this optical fabric with a full-stack, low-latency inference offering and has reported some of the fastest inference speeds for large frontier models. Founded in San Francisco by Ali Khalatpour (CEO) and Keyvan Moghadam (President), the company currently exposes no public, documented developer API or SDK — its product is delivered as hardware plus a hosted inference stack behind an early-access waitlist. This profile tracks Piris Labs' identity in the API Evangelist network and any future API surface it publishes.

companies.name: Prewitt Ridge
companies.description: Prewitt Ridge builds SysGit, "the collaboration layer for complex hardware" — an enterprise platform that applies software development practices to systems engineering. SysGit provides Git-based version control for requirements and system models, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) workflows, AI-assisted systems engineering automation, and SysMLv2 compliance for open-standards adherence. The platform targets defense and aerospace teams, with customers including the US Air Force, GTRI, Leidos, and Anduril. Prewitt Ridge is a Techstars-backed company added to the API Evangelist network. companies.name: Primary
companies.description: Primary (Primary Kids, Inc.) is a direct-to-consumer children's apparel brand selling simple, slogan-free, mix-and-match clothing "in all colors, for all kids" — babies through age 14, plus adult sizes, swimwear, school uniforms and licensed Sesame Street collaborations. The company operates a Shopify-hosted online store at primary.com and is a portfolio company of Homebrew. Primary has no first-party developer API, but its storefront is agent-accessible: it serves a live hosted Shopify Storefront MCP server (catalog search, product lookup, cart, checkout, policy/FAQ lookup) and exposes Shopify's Customer Account API (OAuth2/OIDC) for customer-scoped operations, along with a published llms.txt agent-instructions document.

companies.name: Propagate Ventures
companies.description: Propagate (formerly Propagate Ventures) is a regenerative-agriculture company founded in 2017 that helps farmland owners, farmers, and investors design, plant, finance, and manage agroforestry and tree-crop systems. Its flagship SaaS product, Overyield, lets farmers, developers, and investors model tree-crop economics, choose crops, and design tree-crop systems that work alongside existing farm operations. Propagate pairs the software with technical assessments, site prep and planting services, improved tree genetics, and ongoing project monitoring, and is a partner in the USDA Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities. The company advises 30,000+ acres of agroforestry supporting over 760,000 trees and shrubs. Propagate publishes no public API or developer platform at this time.

companies.name: SiamSquared

StockRadars offers mobile apps (iOS and Android, including a paid StockRadars PLUS tier) and a web app for the Thai stock market, with features such as customizable screening "radars," Top100 rankings, income-statement views, shareholder tracking, volume analysis, real-time price alerts, and an in-house news feed (stockradars.news). The company is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass StockRadars publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation — it is a consumer-facing application, so most machine-readable API artifacts are not applicable and this profile captures identity plus a domain-security probe.

companies.name: Soria

The platform aggregates financial data from 125+ public and private sources into continuously updated financial models and delivers them through a terminal UI, an MCP server, an API, warehouse sync, and a research feed. Soria targets bulge-bracket banks, boutique research firms, and the largest hedge funds that specialize in the healthcare sector, turning fragmented healthcare and life sciences data into live, analyst-ready models. Backed by Y Combinator. Its public surface is a single-page marketing site; the API and MCP delivery channels are gated to customers and are not publicly documented.

companies.name: Synphony
companies.description: Synphony builds and deploys robots that work in the real world, combining AI, robotics, and human-in-the-loop systems so machines can perform practical physical tasks across agriculture, assembly, and inspection. Its platform trains AI models on real-world data, tests robot performance in realistic scenarios, and deploys systems into production. The company's first application is autonomous strawberry-harvesting robots plus farm software services (bed-level analytics, data-pipeline integration, and agentic solutions), targeting California's roughly $3B strawberry industry where labor is about 60% of costs. Founded in 2025 and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), Synphony runs a customer-facing platform at app.synphony.co but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK at this time.

companies.description: Tomo Guides is the home-buying guide and educational content produced by Tomo Mortgage (tomo.com), a consumer digital mortgage lender backed by a16z. Tomo offers home purchase mortgages and refinancing with $0 lender fees and rates advertised at roughly 0.25% below the market median, alongside its TrueRate tool that shows a fair rate before applying and state-by-state interest-rate pages. The "Guides" surface is Tomo's home-buying-guide blog content aimed at first-time and repeat buyers, not a developer product. companies.name: Transfix
companies.description: Transfix is a New York-based freight technology company that, since divesting its brokerage operation to NFI Industries in June 2024, operates as a SaaS and data company providing AI-powered Transportation Management System (TMS) software to freight brokers, third-party logistics providers (3PLs), shippers, and carriers across the United States. The Transfix TMS unifies pricing, planning, execution, and billing in a single platform, with feature areas covering Smart Pricing and Quoting, RFP Management and Collaboration, Coverage and Carrier Management, Streamlined Scheduling, Operations and Automation, Invoicing and Payments, and Reporting and Insights. Core AI capabilities include the Custom Rate Prediction Suite for spot and contract pricing across Dry Van, Reefer, and Flatbed equipment, and the RFP Workflow with a Smart Upload feature that structures bid data from heterogeneous file formats. Transfix markets integrations with existing TMS, carrier networks, and data sources, and references freight API integrations in marketing material, but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or open-source repositories. NFI Industries is the platform's anchor third-party customer following the brokerage divestiture.

companies.name: TutorABC
companies.description: TutorABC (formerly iTutorGroup) is a Taiwan-headquartered online language-learning platform offering live one-on-one and small-group English and Chinese instruction to learners worldwide. Courses span conversational and business English, Mandarin Chinese, certification-exam prep, and study-abroad advising, delivered through a proprietary web and mobile classroom with matched tutors and partnerships with institutions such as Oxford and Cambridge. The company runs consumer learning sites alongside separate portals for tutor recruitment, learning consultants, and interviewer/onboarding workflows. TutorABC is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company identity, its agent-facing llms.txt, and its domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: United States Africa Command
companies.description: United States Africa Command (AFRICOM) is a unified combatant command of the United States Department of Defense responsible for military operations and coordination in Africa. AFRICOM's primary mission is to advance U.S. national security interests and promote regional stability through security cooperation, military assistance, and joint training exercises with African partner nations. AFRICOM is headquartered at Kelley Barracks in Stuttgart, Germany and maintains relationships with 53 African nations. The command is led by a four-star general and conducts operations spanning humanitarian assistance, counter-terrorism, peacekeeping support, and capacity-building activities across the continent.

companies.description: Werner Enterprises is a leading transportation and logistics company providing truckload transportation services, logistics solutions, and supply chain management throughout North America. Founded in 1956 and headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, Werner operates one of the largest fleets in the United States and offers freight brokerage, dedicated carriage, intermodal, and final-mile delivery services through its Werner Bridge℠ digital freight platform.

companies.name: Whole Surplus

It prevents waste at its source and recovers surplus products back into the circular economy with maximum environmental, social, and economic benefit across the entire supply chain from producers to consumers. Its platform combines an AI-powered analysis tool that identifies the optimal recovery path for each product with services including Fazla Market (discounted resale), donations to food banks, animal-feed conversion, recycling, a smart-scale detection system, and sustainability consultancy. Fazla is the first B Corp certified waste-management company in Turkey and is supported by the UN Development Programme (UNDP). The company operates a customer web application (app.fazla.com) but publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specification at this time.

companies.name: Wonderful
companies.description: Wonderful is an applied-AI company building an enterprise AI platform for critical, high-volume workflows. It combines an AI platform (run any model, any modality, any use case, fully governed) with local deployment teams and a strategic partnership model to help large organizations accelerate AI adoption. Wonderful powers agentic automation for enterprises such as national telecom operators, energy providers, and financial-services firms, covering customer-service containment, collections across millions of clients, internal IT automation, and end-to-end billing resolution, with reported outcomes like a 91.5% containment rate across millions of customers. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and IVP. Wonderful sells an enterprise platform with deployment services rather than a self-serve public developer API; its developer documentation is login-gated.

companies.name: Alan
companies.description: Alan is a Paris-based digital health insurance and wellness company founded in 2016 by Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve and Charles Gorintin. It was the first independent health insurance provider licensed in France in over fifty years and offers an integrated product combining complementary health insurance ("mutuelle"), prevention, and care delivery through a single mobile and web experience. Alan's product surface includes group and individual health plans (Alan Santé), retirement plans (Alan Dolce Vita), public-sector and self-employed offerings, an HR/benefits admin dashboard for employers, an in-house telehealth and chat-care service (Clinique Alan) staffed by salaried clinicians, a gamified prevention and step-tracking program (Alan Play / Alan Mind), and vision/optical benefits with zero out-of-pocket pricing. The company reports over one million members and roughly 33,000 client businesses, operates in France, Belgium, and Spain, and reached a reported €5B valuation in its 2026 Series F round. Engineering and product practice is documented publicly on the Alan Product and Technical Blog at medium.com/alan, and a small portfolio of internal-tools and design assets (most notably react-native-fast-shadow and the Alan Sans typeface) is open-sourced on github.com/alan-eu. Alan does not publish a public-facing developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; all member and employer interactions happen through Alan's first-party apps and the HR/benefits dashboard.

companies.name: CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog)
companies.description: CHANGELOG.md is a community convention for a human-readable, Markdown- formatted file at the root of a project that records notable changes between versions. The leading specification is "Keep a Changelog" by Olivier Lacan, which defines a stable, opinionated set of section headings (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security) and recommends pairing with Semantic Versioning (SemVer). The format is widely adopted across open source and enterprise projects as the de facto way to document API and software releases in a way that is readable by humans and parseable by tooling.

companies.name: Compass
companies.description: Compass is a New York City headquartered, tech-enabled residential real estate brokerage founded in 2012 by Robert Reffkin and Ori Allon. The company operates the largest residential real estate brokerage in the United States by sales volume, supporting roughly 36,890 agents and $267 billion in gross transaction value across approximately 250,360 transactions in fiscal year 2025, on $6.96 billion in revenue. Compass builds and operates a proprietary, end-to-end agent platform — an integrated cloud-based suite spanning CRM, marketing center, transaction management, listings, market analytics, the Compass One client dashboard, Compass Lens, AI-powered comparative market analysis, AI-generated video, virtual agent services, and a voice-activated AI assistant — custom-built for residential brokerage workflows. The company has invested over $100 million per year in technology and runs a 500+ person Product and Engineering organization, with engineering hubs that have included Seattle. Compass completed its merger with Anywhere Real Estate on January 9, 2026, combining two of the largest residential brokerage operators in the United States. The Compass platform is internal-facing: it is offered as the operating system for Compass agents and their clients, not as a developer product. There is no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or third-party developer portal for the Compass real estate platform; the company's GitHub presence at github.com/urbancompass publishes a handful of internal-tooling open source projects (e.g. Snail, Mussel, hnvm, bazel-toolchain) rather than product APIs.

companies.name: EnviCore
companies.description: EnviCore is a Calgary, Alberta based sustainability and materials-technology company, backed by Techstars, that produces low-carbon supplementary cementitious materials for the mining and construction industries. Its low-temperature process repurposes industrial waste, mine tailings, clays, and pozzolans into valuable cement replacements, reducing CO2 emissions and supporting a circular economy. EnviCore does not publish a developer API, but its public website exposes an agentic surface: a published llms.txt and a live Wix Site MCP endpoint for AI-agent access to public site content.

companies.name: Rally Network
companies.description: Rally Network (RLY Protocol, stewarded by the RLY Network Association) is a permissionless, open-source, multi-chain web3 mobile toolkit for developers. It provides natively embedded, self-custodial wallets and gasless (gas station / ERC-2771 relayer) transactions so mobile apps can let users create wallets, transfer tokens, claim NFTs, and deploy or call smart contracts without handling gas or seed phrases. The toolkit ships as first-party SDKs for React Native/Expo, Flutter, and Unity plus TypeScript libraries and a hosted dashboard for API keys and configuration. Rally Network is the successor to the original rally.io social-token platform (creator coins), which decentralized in 2021 and wound down its consumer sidechain in early 2023; the RLY Network Association now maintains the open protocol and developer tooling.

companies.name: RoomRaccoon
companies.description: RoomRaccoon is an all-in-one hotel management software platform for independent hotels, B&Bs, guesthouses, hostels, and small chains, founded in 2017 by Tymen van Dyl and Nadja Buckenberger and headquartered in Breda, Netherlands with major operations in Cape Town, South Africa, plus offices in Valencia, Spain and Lisbon, Portugal. The platform bundles a cloud Property Management System (PMS), a Channel Manager that synchronises rates, availability, and restrictions across 200+ OTAs, metasearch engines, GDSs, and bedbanks, a commission-free Booking Engine for direct website bookings with bookable add-ons, RaccoonPay for integrated, multi-currency guest payments, and RaccoonRev for competitor insights and revenue management. RoomRaccoon advertises 400+ integrations with partners such as Booking.com, Expedia, Lightspeed, and Sage, and was named World's Best Hotel Channel Manager at the 2023 World Travel Tech Awards. A connectivity / partner API exists at api.roomraccoon.com (e.g. POS endpoint at /api/?type=POS&version=2) but is access-controlled: prospective integrators must request an API key and Hotel ID by emailing connectivity@roomraccoon.com, and no public OpenAPI specification, public SDKs, or public GitHub organisation are published.

companies.description: Western & Southern Financial Group is a Fortune 500 diversified family of financial services companies headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio. companies.name: Agrostar
companies.description: AgroStar (Ulink Agritech Private Ltd) is a leading Indian agri-tech company on a mission to help farmers grow more and earn more, sustainably. Founded in Pune, it operates India's largest digital farmer network and agri-inputs platform, serving millions of farmers across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh through its Kisan (AgriDoctor) mobile app. AgroStar builds a connected ecosystem across the agricultural value chain — farm advisory, quality agri-inputs, omnichannel retail access and global market linkages — backed by data and agronomy expertise, with a focus on climate-smart agriculture, water conservation and reducing food waste. It is a portfolio company of Accel. AgroStar's public corporate site is Wix-powered and exposes a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint plus an /llms.txt for agentic AI access to public site content; it does not publish a developer-facing product API.

companies.name: Amblea
companies.description: Amblea is a French mission-driven ("entreprise à mission") healthcare-logistics platform that centralizes and optimizes patient (medical / sanitary) transport across the French health system. Formed in 2023 from the merger of Ambler (founded 2018) and Sanilea (2013), it operates a marketplace connecting healthcare establishments (hospitals, clinics, EHPADs, day-care centers) with licensed transport providers (ambulance companies and medical taxi services). The platform handles centralized booking and digital prescription management, shared-transport optimization (grouping patients per trip), real-time tracking, budget and contract management, and automated billing between facilities and transporters. Amblea reports 800+ healthcare establishments, 6,300 transport partner companies, and roughly 8,000 daily trips, making it one of France's largest healthcare-transport coordination platforms. It exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; access is via its web application and direct business arrangements.

The controller exposes a comprehensive REST API with first-party Python, Go, and Java SDKs, a Terraform provider, and Ansible automation for intent-based, self-service application services across VMware, AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, and bare-metal environments.

CN transports goods across an integrated network linking the Atlantic and Pacific coasts with the Gulf of Mexico. CN offers shipper APIs, EDI integration, the eBusiness portal, and the CN ONE mobile app for shipment tracking, ordering, billing, and rate management.

companies.name: commandbar
companies.description: CommandBar is a product-adoption and in-app user-assistance platform that helps SaaS teams onboard, guide, and support users directly inside their web applications. Its embeddable widget bundles a command palette / universal search (Spotlight), an AI copilot, contextual help (HelpHub), nudges and product tours, checklists, and in-app surveys, all driven by a JavaScript SDK (npm `commandbar`) that boots against an organization ID. CommandBar was founded in 2020, backed by Insight Partners among others, and acquired by Amplitude in 2024; the product is now delivered as Amplitude Guides & Surveys. The standalone commandbar.com developer surface (SDK reference, REST API, changelog) has been retired and redirects to Amplitude, though the npm SDK remains published.

companies.name: convergence
companies.description: Convergence AI was a London-based artificial-intelligence startup founded in 2024 by Marvin Purtorab (CEO) and Andy Toulis (CTO) building Proxy, a personal AI agent designed to complete open-ended administrative and web-browsing tasks across domains. Its approach centered on long-term memory and continual learning via a new class of models it called Large Meta Learning Models (LMLM). Convergence raised a $12M pre-seed led by Balderton Capital with participation from Salesforce Ventures and Shopify Ventures, and was acquired by Salesforce in May 2025 to strengthen Agentforce. Its lasting public surface is the convergence-ai GitHub organization, which open-sourced proxy-lite (a mini open-weights web-browsing agent), the proxy-lite-3b vision-language model on Hugging Face, the LM2 memory-model paper repo, and the WebGames agent benchmark.

companies.name: DealerSocket

companies.name: Sturdy
companies.description: Sturdy is a decentralized liquid money market protocol for on-chain lending and borrowing. Sturdy V2 uses a two-tier architecture: a base layer of risk-isolated lending pairs, where each siloed market consists of a single lending asset and a single collateral asset, and an aggregation layer on top that lets lenders choose acceptable collateral types while avoiding liquidity fragmentation. The protocol is oracle-agnostic (using RedStone, API3, and eOracle feeds depending on the market), is governed by the $STRDY token and the Sturdy DAO, and has been audited by Zellic, ChainSecurity, Spearbit, Certik, Code4rena, and Quantstamp. Sturdy is an on-chain smart-contract protocol rather than a hosted REST API: its developer surface is the published smart contracts, oracle integrations, and the Sturdy Subnet, with no first-party web API, SDK, or OpenAPI. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital.

Tahoe's Mosaic platform makes in vivo, single-cell-resolution data generation scalable. Backed by General Catalyst and Wing Venture Capital, Tahoe publishes no commercial REST API; its programmatic surface is open-source models, datasets, and the first-party tahoe-x1 Python library.

The company also exposes a memory API for connecting internal agents to a governed evidence layer. Osseus (Y Combinator S2026) was founded by Anish Mariathasan and Ayush Patel and serves R&D teams across aerospace, automotive, robotics, electronics, pharma, and biotech.

companies.description: Ossus builds AI-native intelligence for cultural institutions, starting with libraries. Its flagship product is Ossus ILS, a modern integrated library system that unifies cataloguing, circulation, acquisitions, analytics, and patron discovery in one interface, with an AI copilot that drafts MARC records, subjects, and classifications for librarian approval. A lighter product, Librar, targets school libraries with fast mobile setup. AI add-ons cover camera-based shelf inventory, vendor comparison for purchasing, and grant finding. Ossus emphasizes privacy-first design: it does not train on or sell customer data and works only with catalogue metadata rather than borrower records. PolyXLabs currently publishes no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.description: "TypeScript-first GraphQL schema builder with a plugin system for Prisma, Relay, federation, simple objects, and code-first type-safe schema construction without code generation."

companies.name: Salus
companies.description: Salus provides runtime validation and governance for AI agents. It sits between an agent and its tools as a policy-aware proxy that intercepts each action before it executes, then clarifies, rewrites, escalates for human review, or blocks it against organizational policies — managing commit-time risk on financial transfers, appointment changes, and data modifications before they alter customer data, finances, or records. Integration requires only an endpoint URL change (no agent rewrite), and Salus works across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, Retell, Vapi, and custom tools. Capabilities include evidence-based validation, PII detection, budget and loop protection, idempotency checks, human-in-the-loop escalation, self-repair of blocked actions, and integrated evals and observability. Salus is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in San Francisco.

companies.name: Tenzai

Founded in 2025 by Guardicore founders Pavel Gurvich and Ariel Zeitlin together with Ofri Ziv, Itamar Tal, and Aner Mazur, the Tel Aviv-based company launched out of stealth in November 2025 with a $75M seed round (one of the largest in cybersecurity) led by Greylock Partners, Battery Ventures, and Lux Capital at a reported $330M valuation. Tenzai targets the penetration-testing market with continuous, AI-driven offensive validation. As of this profile the company exposes a marketing site, a research blog, careers, and a SOC 2 Type 1 trust center, but no public developer or API surface.

companies.name: The Human Utility

Operating in Detroit, Baltimore, and dozens of other cities, it has helped thousands of households avoid water shutoffs. The Human Utility runs a public-facing web application for donors and recipients rather than a developer-facing API product; its source code lives in the humanutility GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched with identity and link details; no public API surface was found.

companies.name: ALICE Technologies
companies.description: ALICE Technologies is a Menlo Park, California construction technology company that builds an AI-driven generative scheduling and construction optioneering platform. The product simulates millions of possible construction sequences for a project — varying crews, equipment, methods, and constraints — to find optimal schedules, accelerate timelines, recover delayed projects, and de-risk capital project delivery. ALICE's suite includes ALICE Optimize (generative scheduling from imported Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project schedules), ALICE Plan (a 2D visual planning canvas overlaid on drawings), ALICE Model (BIM-driven schedule generation from 3D models), and the Schedule Insights Agent (an LLM-powered conversational interface for analysing and recommending schedule changes, including automated DCMA 14-point schedule quality scoring). The platform is sold as SaaS to general contractors, owners and developers, and consultants working on industrial (data centres, energy, semiconductors), infrastructure (rail, highway, tunnels), and commercial projects, with reported impacts including up to 17% reduction in project duration and 14% labor cost savings. ALICE was founded in 2015 by René Morkos (Stanford PhD) and is backed by Merus Capital, Foundamental, Future Ventures, Lightspeed, Blackhorn Ventures, and Brick and Mortar; in 2026 it announced a formal alliance with McKinsey to deploy generative scheduling on capital projects. ALICE integrates by importing from Primavera P6, Primavera Cloud, Microsoft Project, and BIM/drawing formats, but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository — integration is delivered via the product's import/export surface and customer-success engagements.

companies.name: AutoGen Studio
companies.description: AutoGen Studio is a low-code / no-code developer GUI from Microsoft Research for rapidly prototyping, composing, and debugging multi-agent AI workflows built on the AutoGen framework. Shipped as the `autogenstudio` Python package and launched with `autogenstudio ui`, it serves a FastAPI + React (Gatsby) web app on localhost that exposes four primary interfaces — Team Builder, Playground, Gallery, and Deployment — backed by a SQLModel persistence layer (SQLite by default; any SQLAlchemy-compatible backend such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, MSSQL via `--database-uri`). The Team Builder offers drag-and-drop and JSON authoring of teams, agents, models, tools, and termination conditions fully aligned with AutoGen AgentChat's declarative component spec; the Playground streams live inter-agent messages and renders the control transition graph; the Gallery imports community components; and the Deployment view exports a team to Python, exposes it as an endpoint, and packages it for Docker. AutoGen Studio is built on AutoGen AgentChat / Core / Extensions and supports any OpenAI-compatible model endpoint (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, local vLLM/Ollama, etc.) via declarative `model_client` configuration, plus MCP tool integration. Authentication is experimental (GitHub OAuth + JWT only). Microsoft explicitly positions AutoGen Studio as a research prototype — not production-ready — and encourages teams that need authn/z, multi-tenancy, sandboxing rigor, or hardened deployment to build directly on the AutoGen framework instead. Companion to the broader AutoGen multi-agent framework, distributed under the Microsoft microsoft/autogen monorepo (CC-BY-4.0 docs, MIT code).

As Evergy, the company continues to serve approximately 1.6 million customers in Kansas and Missouri with a focus on grid modernization, smart metering (AMI) through its Gridstream Connect IoT platform, and clean energy transformation including wind power and demand response programs.

companies.name: Windward
companies.description: Windward is a Maritime AI company headquartered in London and Washington D.C. delivering mission-grade, multi-source maritime intelligence for defense agencies, law enforcement, customs, energy and commodity traders, marine insurers, shippers, and financial institutions. Founded by CEO Ami Daniel, Windward fuses AIS data, remote sensing (EO, SAR, RF GEOINT), proprietary behavioral analytics, and generative AI into a single Maritime AI platform covering vessel screening, ownership and entity resolution, sanctions exposure, deceptive shipping detection, ship-to-ship transfer analysis, IUU fishing detection, smuggling detection, container tracking, and maritime infrastructure protection. Windward exposes its intelligence through the API Insights Lab, a unified GraphQL API at developer.windward.ai providing programmatic access to vessel risk scores, Organization Defined Risk (ODR), ultimate beneficial ownership, early detection signals, tracked shipments, carriers, and detention & demurrage data, along with webhooks and workflow automation. The company has no public REST/OpenAPI surface, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub org — its API is GraphQL-only with managed onboarding and expert-led implementation support.

companies.name: Campbell's
companies.description: Campbell's (Campbell Soup Company, now The Campbell's Company) is the consumer brand trusted for generations to provide authentic, flavourful, and readily available soups, meals, and recipes. Alongside its consumer website, Campbell's has historically operated a Campbell's Kitchen Developer API that let developers embed Campbell's, Swanson, Pace, Prego, and Pepperidge Farm recipes, products, and nutrition data into their own web and mobile experiences.

companies.name: Climavision
companies.description: Climavision is a Louisville, Kentucky weather intelligence company that combines a proprietary nationwide supplemental network of low-altitude X-band, dual-polarization gap-filling weather radars with AI-driven numerical weather prediction (NWP) to deliver enterprise-grade forecasts and observational data. Its Horizon AI product line includes Horizon Point for site-specific forecasts, Horizon Global for ground-to-high- altitude global models, Horizon HI-RES for custom high-resolution local forecasting, and Horizon S2S for subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction. Climavision exposes a Weather API hosted at point-forecast-api.climavision.com with 1,800+ parameters, 15-day forecasts, and bearer-token authentication, plus a separate Radar Status API and Radar-as-a-Service offering that supplies Level II files, NetCDF, and GeoTIFF radar data products (reflectivity, velocity, dual-pol-derived QPE at 1km, precipitation type, tornado debris detection) for coverage below 4,000 feet where NEXRAD cannot see due to Earth curvature. The company integrates its radar feed into MRMS and has provided supplemental data into the National Weather Service's AWIPS software. Climavision processes 1.5+ billion datasets daily, serves customers across agriculture, aviation, commodity trading, drones and Advanced Air Mobility, energy and utilities, government, insurance and reinsurance, media, and transportation and logistics, and raised a $100 million strategic investment from TPG's Rise Fund. API access is gated through a sales-led contact process; no public sandbox or open-source SDKs are published, and the Climavision GitHub organization (github.com/Climavision) currently has only two minor public repositories (an archived Azure Table Storage helper and a GeoServer Helm chart fork).

companies.description: Dealogic is a global provider of content and software for the capital markets, including deal-management, analytics, league-table, and compliance solutions used by investment banks, sales/trading desks, and investment managers. Dealogic delivers data and connectivity primarily through its Cortex platform, Dealogic Connect, and Analytics products rather than a self-service public developer API; integrations are contracted with customers and accessed under license rather than from a public developer portal.

companies.name: Legora
companies.description: Legora is a Stockholm, Sweden-based collaborative AI workspace for lawyers, founded in 2023 as Leya by Max Junestrand (CEO), Sigge Labor (CTO), and August Erséus, and rebranded to Legora in 2025. The platform delivers an agentic operating system, Legora aOS, that helps law firms and in-house legal teams execute document review, legal research, drafting, advisory work, and regulatory monitoring at scale. Core product surfaces include Agent (end-to-end execution of complex legal work), Monitors (regulatory change tracking), Lists (workflow organization), Tabular Review, Workflows, Legal Research, Portal, Editor, a Word Add-in, an Outlook Add-in, and a mobile app, with practice-area solutions spanning M&A, litigation, banking, tax, and insurance. Legora is built on Azure OpenAI Service, holds ISO 42001, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 Type II certifications, operates under GDPR with EU and US data residency options, supports BYOK encryption, and commits not to train AI models on customer data. The company closed a $550M Series D led by Accel in March 2026 at a $5.55B valuation. Legora's commercial model is enterprise SaaS sold to law firms and in-house teams; there is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GitHub organization, or open-source release for the Legora platform.

companies.name: Let's Do This
companies.description: Let's Do This is an endurance-events marketplace where participants discover and register for mass-participation sport — marathons, road races, trail runs, triathlons, obstacle races and cycling events — across the United Kingdom and the United States. The platform covers event discovery, entry purchase and entry management, team entries, memberships, referral credits and discount codes, and it works with event organisers and charity partners who list and sell places through it. Backed by EQT Ventures. As of July 2026 Let's Do This publishes no public API program: there is no developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDK or webhook surface. A live but undocumented GraphQL endpoint backs the consumer marketplace with introspection disabled.

companies.name: MisterSpex
companies.description: Mister Spex SE is a European online-first eyewear and optical retailer selling prescription glasses, sunglasses, and contact lenses across more than 100 premium, luxury, independent, and private-label brands. Founded in Berlin in 2007 and listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, the company serves more than 8 million customers online in five countries and operates 65 stores in Germany plus a network of over 300 partner opticians. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public consumer or developer API, so this profile captures corporate identity and security-surface artifacts derived from live probes rather than an API catalog.

companies.name: Open mHealth
companies.description: Open mHealth is a nonprofit, community-driven initiative that develops open standards and open-source software for making patient-generated health data interoperable across mobile apps, wearables, clinical systems, and electronic health records. Its core contribution is a library of clinically validated JSON Schema data point schemas — covering physical activity, sleep, heart rate, blood pressure, body weight, blood glucose, and other vital signs — with the sleep, physical-activity, and metadata schemas now superseded by IEEE 1752.1, the IEEE standard for Mobile Health Data co-shepherded by the Open mHealth community. Around the schemas Open mHealth ships a stack of Apache-2.0 reference implementations: Shimmer (a Java/Spring server that pulls health data from Fitbit, Google Fit, iHealth, Misfit, RunKeeper, and Withings APIs and normalizes it into Open mHealth or IEEE 1752.1 data points), omh-dsu-ri (a Data Storage Unit reference implementation exposing an OAuth 2.0-secured Data Point REST API on top of MongoDB and PostgreSQL), Granola (an Objective-C library that serializes Apple HealthKit samples into Open mHealth JSON), a web visualizations library built on D3 and Plottable.js, the OMH-on-FHIR mapping that aligns Open mHealth data points to HL7 FHIR resources, and a sample-data-generator. Open mHealth operates as the steward of the standard, the schema and unit registry at registry.openmhealth.org, and a developer community of thousands of developers and health organizations including Cornell Tech, Kaiser Permanente, Stanford School of Medicine, UC Davis, and UCSF. The project has no commercial API, no paid tier, and no hosted SaaS — all artifacts are open source under Apache 2.0 and the standard itself is openly published.

companies.name: Perl
companies.description: Perl is a highly capable, feature-rich programming language with over 37 years of development. It is best known for text processing, system administration, web development, and rapid scripting, supported by the Comprehensive Perl Archive Network (CPAN) with more than 25,000 open source extension modules and a global community of developers, blogs, and local user groups. The Perl Foundation supports ongoing development of Perl and its sister language Raku.

companies.name: Rational
companies.description: Rational (rational.to) is a Y Combinator (S26) company building AI employees, or "AI coworkers," for accounting and finance teams. Its AI agents onboard themselves to a firm, build a company "brain," and perform recurring accounting work — accounts payable, AR collections, bookkeeping, bank reconciliation, document collection, expense review, and month-end close — while keeping postings, payment release, and policy-sensitive decisions behind explicit human approval gates with an inspectable review history. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco by Jibril Moinuddin and Christ Xu, Rational targets accounting firms and finance teams facing a structural capacity and labor shortage. As an early-stage company it currently exposes a marketing and agent-discovery surface (llms.txt, ai-discovery.json, RFC 9116 security.txt) rather than a public developer API; this profile captures that surface and will be enriched as a developer platform ships.

companies.description: Addus HomeCare is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Addus HomeCare API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Agile Loop L.L.C.
companies.description: Agile Loop L.L.C. is a London-founded enterprise AI company (founded 2023, backed by 500 Global) building Large Action Models — action-first foundation models trained on thousands of software interfaces so AI agents can operate any user interface and execute multi-step workflows end-to-end from natural-language instructions. Its product suite spans Sector Fusion (telecom network analytics), an Intelligent Evaluation Platform (AI scoring and fraud detection), LLM Ops (governance for LLM applications), an Aviation Ops Suite, and SAM-X (natural-language Excel automation), alongside the open-source Synapse Copilot toolkit for connecting LLMs to APIs and an embeddable Copilot widget for SaaS products. Agile Loop publishes no public OpenAPI, developer portal, or versioned client SDKs at the time of this profile.

companies.name: Aliro Quantum
companies.description: Aliro Quantum (branded "Aliro, The Quantum Networking Company") is a Boston-based, Harvard spin-out building full-stack software for entanglement-based quantum networks. Its platform unifies three core products: the Aliro Simulator for physically accurate, optical-level modeling and validation of heterogeneous quantum networks before any hardware is deployed; AlirOS, a vendor-agnostic control-plane operating system that runs on quantum end-nodes and quantum repeaters across multiple hardware modalities; and the Aliro Orchestrator, a centralized single-pane-of-glass management system that configures, monitors, and operates quantum nodes and services through the full network lifecycle. These are packaged commercially as AliroNet — described by Aliro as the world's first end-to-end entanglement-based quantum network solution — delivered in three modes (Emulate, Pilot, and Deployment) and also available as AliroNet Quickstart, a bundled hardware-plus-software starter package that pairs third-party photon sources, detectors, memories, repeaters, and routers with Aliro's orchestration, control, and data operations software. The company markets Quantum-Powered Security as its anchor use case (Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later mitigation for telcos, utilities, financial services, and defense), alongside quantum-computing interconnects (clustered and blind quantum compute for cloud providers), networked quantum sensors for positioning/navigation/timing, and quantum position verification. Customers and design partners disclosed publicly include EPB of Chattanooga, Boeing, Cisco, the US Air Force, Brookhaven National Laboratory, Stony Brook University, and Noblis. Aliro is backed by deep-tech investors including Cisco Investments and Accenture Ventures, reports more than 50 third-party quantum networking devices already integrated with its stack, and operates with hardware-agnostic positioning across photonic, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and diamond-defect node technologies. There is no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or open-source repository — the AlirOS APIs referenced in Aliro's product materials are vendor-facing integration interfaces consumed under commercial engagement, and Aliro's GitHub organization carries no public repositories.

companies.name: Apex.AI
companies.description: Apex.AI is an embedded and autonomous software company whose tagline is "software that moves," focused on safe, real-time, software-defined systems (SDx) for automotive, robotics, and other safety-critical embedded platforms. Its product line includes Apex.Grace (deterministic embedded execution framework, an automotive-grade evolution of ROS 2), Apex.Ida (high-speed fault-tolerant middleware for sensor, compute, and cloud connectivity), Apex.OS for V&V (data recording and replay for validating autonomous systems), and Apex.Alan (automated tooling and CI/CD workflows for safe software development at scale). Apex.AI also provides technical assessment, architecture, embedded and cloud software development, CI/CD pipeline, and ROS 1 to ROS 2 migration services. The company is a maintainer of substantial ROS 2 and embedded middleware open source. It is backed by Canaan Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Apex.AI publishes no public developer REST API at this time.

companies.name: Asylon
companies.description: Asylon Robotics is an American-made robotic security company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Norristown, Pennsylvania, that automates physical perimeter security with autonomous drones, ground robots, software, and AI. Its flagship products include the Guardian automated security drone (the most widely used automated security drone system, with tens of thousands of patrol and alarm-response missions completed), the DroneDog quadruped ground robot built on Boston Dynamics Spot with the Asylon DogHouse charging enclosure and PupPack cellular PTZ payload, and DroneIQ, the Robotic Security Operations Center (RSOC) and software platform that coordinates robotic assets, fixed surveillance, and human operators. DroneIQ exposes an open-architecture integration layer for third-party alarms and sensors (radar, smart fences, Bosch alarm panels, gun-detection computer vision, Genetec), but the company publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; API and integration access is arranged directly with Asylon. Asylon raised a $26M Series B in July 2025 led by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Augmenta
companies.description: Augmenta is a Toronto-based generative AI company building the Augmenta Construction Platform (ACP), a Spatial AI system that automates building design — starting with electrical raceway routing and expanding into mechanical and plumbing (MEP). ACP ingests Revit models, accepts conduit run schedules, fly/no-fly zones, and project specifications, then generates clash-free, constructable 3D conduit routes in the cloud and exports them back into Revit as system conduit ready for detailing and prefabrication. The platform combines computational geometry, advanced optimization, and machine learning to handle data-center, hospital, and school-scale electrical builds, and is marketed to VDC teams and electrical contractors as a way to cut BIM time by roughly two-thirds. Augmenta was founded by veterans of generative design for advanced manufacturing, won EC&M 2026 Product of the Year, was named to the 2026 Global Cleantech 100, and signed a five-year strategic partnership with E-J Electric Installation Co. The product is delivered as a SOC2-certified Revit add-in with a cloud back-end; there is no public REST API, SDK, or open-source release.

companies.name: Barnes & Noble
companies.description: Barnes & Noble is the largest retail bookseller in the United States, operating physical bookstores and an e-commerce site selling books, magazines, gifts, and educational products. Barnes & Noble also operates the Nook e-reader platform and offers affiliate and publisher partner programs. No public developer API is currently offered; the company operates primarily through retail channels and affiliate marketing programs.

companies.name: Binaris
companies.description: Binaris was a fast, low-latency Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) platform for running production Node.js workloads in the cloud. Founded in 2017 and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, its developer surface centered on the `bn` command-line tool and Node.js SDK (published to npm as `binaris` and to Docker Hub as `binaris/bn`), which let developers scaffold, deploy, invoke, and inspect serverless functions in seconds. Authentication was via a Binaris API key (`BINARIS_API_KEY`). The company later explored a "Shift" programming model (`@binaris/shift-fetch-runtime`). The hosted platform at binaris.io / binaris.com is no longer in service, but the first-party client packages and a 42-repository GitHub organization remain publicly available and are captured here.

companies.name: Bindbridge
companies.description: Bindbridge is an AI-driven molecular discovery company founded in 2025 and based in Cambridge, UK, developing next-generation crop protection through targeted protein degradation. Its BRIDGE platform uses AI to discover and design molecular glues and targeted protein degraders with novel modes of action against weeds and crop diseases, combining AI candidate generation, computational docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and free-energy binding calculations to accelerate agricultural R&D across herbicides, insecticides, and fungicides. The company raised $3.8M to help reduce billion-dollar crop losses and is backed by Speedinvest. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; it publishes no public API or developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: C++
companies.description: C++ is a general-purpose, statically typed, compiled programming language created by Bjarne Stroustrup as an extension of C. C++ supports object- oriented, generic, and functional programming and is widely used in systems programming, game engines, embedded systems, scientific computing, finance, and high-performance services. The language is standardized by ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG21 with current revisions including C++20 and C++23. C++ does not expose a network/HTTP API; this index captures the language home, standards process, reference documentation, and ecosystem resources.

companies.name: Compose
companies.description: Compose (Compose, Inc., compose.io) was a database-as-a-service (DBaaS) provider that offered production-ready, auto-scaling, hosted deployments of open-source databases — MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch, RabbitMQ, RethinkDB, ScyllaDB, etcd, MySQL, and Disque — each provisioned with high availability, automated backups, and a REST API for programmatic management. Founded in 2010 as MongoHQ and rebranded to Compose in 2014, the company was backed by DCVC (Data Collective) and was acquired by IBM in 2015, after which the offering was folded into IBM Cloud as "IBM Compose" / IBM Cloud Databases. The standalone Compose service and its developer surface (compose.com, compose.io, apidocs.compose.com) have since been deprecated and taken offline. This profile documents the surviving, verifiable first-party artifacts — the archived GitHub organization at github.com/compose, the official Go SDK (gocomposeapi) wrapping the Compose REST API, and the official command-line tools (bach, cocli).

companies.name: Concord Systems
companies.description: Concord Systems was a Brooklyn, New York stream-processing company founded in December 2014 by Alexander Gallego and Emilio Del Tesoro, and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It built a high-performance distributed stream processing framework written in C++ on top of Apache Mesos, aimed at letting application developers and data scientists write real-time streaming computations ("operators") in the language of their choice — Python, Ruby, Go, Java/Scala, Node.js or Haskell — with Kafka and Amazon Kinesis connectors and a CLI for deploying topologies. Akamai Technologies acquired the company in an all-cash transaction in September 2016 and folded the technology into its IoT edge data platform for real-time messaging and log processing. The company is discontinued: concord.io is parked and the documentation site is gone. Its interface was a Thrift-based operator driver API rather than an HTTP/REST API, so there is no OpenAPI or event surface to catalog; the surviving first-party developer artifacts are the github.com/concord organization and the client libraries still published on PyPI, RubyGems and pkg.go.dev.

companies.name: Continual
companies.description: Continual was an operational-AI / MLOps platform for the modern data stack, founded by Tristan Zajonc (previously Sense, acquired by Cloudera) and Tyler Kohn (co-founder of RichRelevance). It let data and analytics teams declaratively build, deploy, and continuously maintain production predictive models directly inside cloud data warehouses — Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery — using SQL and dbt as the primary interface rather than bespoke ML pipelines. The company raised a seed round led by Amplify Partners and a $14.5M Series A in 2022. The product is now dormant: continual.ai is a parked single-page shell, the documentation host redirects to the homepage, and the last release of the first-party Python CLI + SDK on PyPI was in March 2023. This profile captures the verifiable public artifacts that remain — the PyPI package, the GitHub organization, and a live domain-security posture.

companies.name: DNN Software
companies.description: DNN Software is the company behind DNN Platform (formerly DotNetNuke), a leading open-source web content management system (CMS) and web application framework built on Microsoft ASP.NET and C#. Originally created by Shaun Walker in 2002, DNN provides a modular platform for building websites, intranets, and web applications, extended through custom modules, providers, and skins. For developers, DNN ships a first-party set of .NET libraries on NuGet (DotNetNuke.Core, DotNetNuke.WebApi, DotNetNuke.Web, and related packages) plus a DotNetNuke Web API (ASP.NET Web API) services framework for building authenticated REST endpoints inside a DNN site. The open-source DNN Platform is developed in the open on GitHub under an MIT license, with community documentation, forums, and Discord maintained by the DNN Community.

companies.name: Entocycle
companies.description: Entocycle is a London-based insect farming technology company building industrial-scale, controlled-environment facilities that use black soldier fly bioconversion to turn organic waste streams into insect protein for animal feed and organic fertilizer (frass). Its platform combines modular climate-controlled farm infrastructure, real-time AI-driven insect monitoring that counts and tracks insects across their lifecycle, and fully automated production systems to standardize output across deployments worldwide. Entocycle partners with waste management companies, agricultural producers, insect companies, and offtake buyers to develop and operate circular-economy insect farms. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: Ionic Security
companies.description: Ionic Security was an Atlanta, Georgia data-protection and dynamic-authorization company whose Machina platform let developers add data access, control, and protection to any application with a small amount of code. Machina provided an API-driven service layer for just-in-time enforcement of data-access policies — evaluating user, device, service, environment, and data attributes to allow or deny each request — backed by client SDKs for Java, C, C++, C#, Objective-C, Python, and JavaScript, a Machina CLI, and cloud-storage integrations for AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Storage. Ionic was venture-backed (GV, Kleiner Perkins, Ten Eleven Ventures) and was acquired by Twilio in April 2021 for roughly $30.2 million to accelerate Twilio's data-security capabilities. The company's developer domains (ionic.com, dev.ionic.com, api.ionic.com) are no longer live, but the first-party SDKs and CLI remain published on Maven Central, PyPI, and the IonicDev GitHub organization.

companies.name: Kinvey
companies.description: Kinvey was a mobile Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS / mBaaS) platform providing app developers with hosted data storage, user management and authentication, file storage, push notifications, caching/offline sync, and serverless business logic through its Flex (FlexData / FlexFunctions) services. It shipped first-party client SDKs for web, Node.js, iOS/macOS (Swift), Android/Java, Xamarin/.NET, NativeScript, Angular/Ionic, and Cordova/PhoneGap, plus a command-line utility for managing apps, environments, and Flex microservices. Kinvey was acquired by Progress Software; the standalone developer surface has since been retired (kinvey.com redirects into Progress and the GitHub organization was archived in February 2025), though the published SDKs and CLI remain available on their package registries.
