companies.name: Muon Space
companies.description: Muon Space is a Mountain View, California-based end-to-end space systems company that designs, builds, and operates mission-optimized satellite constellations to deliver Earth Intelligence and enable real-time compute and decision-making in space. Founded in 2021 by veterans of Skybox, NASA, and SpaceX, the company's core product is Muon Halo, an integrated technology stack composed of MuSim (constellation simulation and digital twin), MuOS (IP-based software-defined network middleware connecting space, ground, and cloud), MuCore (software-configurable instrument core), Condor (modular Condor-M and Condor-XL spacecraft platforms), and MuDash (cloud-based tasking, scheduling, and operations dashboard). Muon Space's flagship public mission is FireSat, a purpose-built wildfire detection and monitoring constellation developed with the Earth Fire Alliance, Google Research, and the Gordon & Betty Moore Foundation; FireSat carries a high-dynamic-range multispectral IR instrument capable of detecting 5x5 meter fires across a 1,500 km swath with a 50 m nadir ground sample distance, with revisit times targeted to twenty minutes once the full constellation is operational. The Protoflight satellite produced its first-light imagery in June 2025, with the first block of three additional satellites launching in 2026 and full operational capacity targeted for 2030. Other Muon Space missions support the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force for next-generation weather monitoring, Hydrosat for thermal geospatial intelligence in climate and agriculture, and global security applications including missile-defense architecture. Muon Space's revenue model is mission contracting, spacecraft and constellation delivery, and hosted data services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Halo platform or FireSat data feed.

companies.name: One More Game
companies.description: One More Game is a fully remote game development studio founded by veterans behind titles such as Warcraft, Diablo, StarCraft, and Guild Wars. The team builds delightful, social online games designed to be played with friends, emphasizing fast iteration and a mission to help players have more fun. One More Game was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. The studio publishes a consumer gaming website, a company blog, careers listings, and a GitHub organization (PlayOneMoreGame) of game-development tooling and forks, but does not currently operate a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Open Souls
companies.description: Open Souls is an open-source framework and philosophy for building "AI souls" — agentic, embodied digital beings with personality, drive, and ego, built on top of large language models. The Soul Engine framework (distributed as the soul-engine npm package and CLI) models agency, memory, emotion, and goal-setting through WorkingMemory, cognitiveSteps, and MentalProcesses abstractions, describing itself as "NextJS + Vercel for the minds of digital beings." The project is now legacy: the opensouls.org site is parked and the hosted Soul Engine cloud service is no longer operating, but the open-source framework and npm packages remain published under the opensouls GitHub organization. Open Souls was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Per Vices
companies.description: Per Vices Corporation is a Toronto-based company that designs and manufactures high-performance software defined radio (SDR) platforms, where signal tuning is handled in hardware while the remaining radio functionality runs in software so a single application-agnostic platform can serve many markets. Its product line includes Cyan (up to 16 independent radio chains, near-DC to 18 GHz), Crimson TNG (4 Rx / 4 Tx, near-DC to 6 GHz), Chestnut (near-DC to 9 GHz on an Intel Stratix 10 FPGA), and Calamine (receive-only, near-DC to 40 GHz). Per Vices ships open-source host software and firmware built on the UHD (USRP Hardware Driver) framework rather than a public web API; developers program the radios through the UHD C++ driver, GNU Radio integration, and example applications published on its GitHub org, with full integration support provided directly to customers. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with company identity and a security probe; it publishes no public REST/OpenAPI web API surface.

companies.name: PHP
companies.description: PHP is a widely-used server-side scripting language especially suited for web development and embedded in HTML. It powers a large portion of the web including platforms like WordPress and Drupal, and provides extensive database support, framework options, and a mature ecosystem. PHP itself is a language and runtime, not a hosted API service.

companies.name: Quantive (fka Gtmhub)
companies.description: Quantive (formerly Gtmhub) is a strategy-execution and OKR (Objectives and Key Results) SaaS platform, historically backed by Insight Partners. The company and its "Quantive Results" product have since been acquired and folded into WorkBoard — quantive.com now redirects to workboard.com and the developer portal (developer.quantive.com) has been decommissioned. The public REST API and OpenAPI reference are no longer reachable, but first-party developer tooling remains published on public registries: the @gtmhub/sdk extensibility SDK on npm (for building marketplace plugins and insights) and the gtmhub-cli command-line client (distributed via Homebrew, Chocolatey, and GitHub releases). This profile captures the surviving developer surface.

companies.name: Rubric Labs
companies.description: Rubric Labs is an applied AI lab based in Canada that helps companies build and ship intelligent, agent-powered applications. companies.name: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
companies.description: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is the de-facto repository file used by open-source projects on GitHub, GitLab, and similar platforms to declare community standards, acceptable behavior, and enforcement procedures for project participants. The most widely adopted text dropped into this file is the Contributor Covenant, currently at version 2.1, maintained by the Organization for Ethical Source. GitHub surfaces a CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md located in the repo root, .github/, or docs/ directory in its Community Standards checklist and links to it from issue templates. The file is plain Markdown and has no machine-readable schema, but it is structurally consistent across the dominant template (Contributor Covenant) and a small number of alternatives (Citizen Code of Conduct, Django Code of Conduct, Mozilla Community Participation Guidelines).

companies.name: CODEOWNERS
companies.description: CODEOWNERS is the file format originally introduced by GitHub and later adopted by GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Gitea, and Azure Repos that lets a repository declare which individuals or teams are responsible for a path or pattern within the codebase. Platforms use it to auto-request reviews on pull/merge requests, enforce required approvals via branch protection or push rules, and route pings on issues. The file is plain text with one rule per line - a glob pattern followed by one or more owner handles (`@username` or `@org/team`) or email addresses. Comments start with `#` and the last matching pattern wins.

It builds action cameras, the M1 mirrorless camera, smart home/security cameras, dash cams and in-car rearview systems, VR cameras, and handheld gimbals, and now positions itself around computer vision, edge intelligence, and edge computing solutions for smart mobility, smart home, smart retail, smart parks, and smart communities, selling through JD and Tmall storefronts. Surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment - the developer subdomain (dev.xiaoyi.com) returns 502, api.xiaoyi.com serves only a placeholder page, and no API documentation, OpenAPI specs, official GitHub organization, or first-party registry packages were located.

companies.name: yesmro
companies.description: YESMRO (易买工品), operated by Shanghai Sheti Information Technology Co., Ltd. and founded in April 2016, is a self-operated Chinese B2B e-commerce platform for MRO (maintenance, repair and operations) and factory-automation parts. It carries millions of SKUs across mechanical components, industrial control (PLCs, HMIs, servos, drives), sensors, low-voltage electrical, pneumatics, tools, safety and factory consumables from 800+ brands, targeting the small and medium-sized end factories that make up the long tail of industrial demand. The company runs automated (AGV) warehouses in Shanghai, Hefei and Dongguan and 10+ regional offices, and in 2020 launched an open platform for upstream suppliers. It is backed by Qiming Venture Partners, Matrix Partners China and Sequoia Capital China. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming; no public developer API, open-platform docs, or specification surface was found during enrichment.

companies.name: Big O Notation
companies.description: Big O Notation is a mathematical notation used in computer science to describe the performance or complexity of algorithms, providing a way to classify algorithms by how their runtime or space requirements grow as input size grows. It is foundational to algorithm design, API performance benchmarking, and software engineering education.

companies.name: Binary Format
companies.description: Binary format refers to data encoding and serialization methods that use binary rather than text representations, including formats like Protocol Buffers, MessagePack, Avro, Thrift, CBOR, and others used in APIs and data storage systems for efficiency. Binary formats offer significant advantages over text-based formats in terms of size, parsing speed, and type safety.

companies.name: Cabot Oil & Gas
companies.description: Cabot Oil & Gas was an independent oil and gas company engaged in the development, exploitation, exploration, production, and marketing of natural gas and oil properties in the United States. In 2021 it merged with Cimarex Energy to form Coterra Energy, which operates across the Permian Basin, Marcellus Shale, and Anadarko Basin.

companies.name: Centric Brands
companies.description: Centric Brands LLC is a New York-headquartered global lifestyle brand management and product-development platform formed in October 2018 when Differential Brands Group (NASDAQ: DFBG) acquired Global Brands Group's $1.2B North American licensing business. The company designs, sources, markets, and distributes apparel, accessories, footwear, beauty, and entertainment-licensed products across men's, women's, kids', accessories, and entertainment segments. Its mission is "to be a leading global apparel & accessories company with a portfolio of iconic licensed and owned brands that delight retailers and consumers of all ages." Centric filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on May 18, 2020 and emerged in October 2020 under control of secured creditors led by Blackstone's GSO Capital Partners, Ares Management, and HPS Investment Partners. The company is led by CEO Jason Rabin (since 2018) and operates ~20 global offices across New York (HQ), Los Angeles, Greensboro, Montreal, London, Amsterdam, Hong Kong, and multiple cities in China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, and Vietnam. Owned brands include Hudson Jeans, Buffalo Jeans, Robert Graham, Joe's Jeans, Hervé Léger, Favorite Daughter, and AllSaints; licensed apparel brands include Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, Nautica, Spyder, IZOD, Van Heusen, Kate Spade New York, Coach, Michael Kors, Frye, Timberland, Lucky Brand, Juicy Couture, Under Armour, and Off-White; the entertainment licensing portfolio spans 70+ properties including Disney, Marvel, Warner Bros., DC, Nintendo, Hasbro, Mattel, Nickelodeon, Netflix, Pokémon, Sanrio, Paw Patrol, and the NFL/MLB/NBA/NHL via Sports & Entertainment Licensing. Centric Brands operates "11 end-to-end Ecommerce sites," a 3D design and art studio in Greensboro, and a New York City photo/video studio. The company has no public developer program, no documented public APIs, and no public source code repositories; its two namesake GitHub organizations (centric-brands, Centricbrands) are private placeholders with zero public repos.

companies.name: Django
companies.description: A high-level Python web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design. Django follows the model-template-views architectural pattern and includes an ORM, automatic admin interface, robust template system, and quick internationalization support. The current release line is Django 6.0, supported by the non-profit Django Software Foundation, and it powers some of the busiest websites globally.

companies.name: Forter
companies.description: Forter is a New York City-headquartered ecommerce fraud prevention and digital identity platform founded in 2013 by Michael Reitblat and Alon Shemesh. The company operates an AI-powered decision platform for digital commerce that helps merchants approve more legitimate transactions while blocking fraud, account takeover, payment abuse, policy abuse, and return/refund abuse. Forter's products include Fraud Management, Payment Optimization (3DS, card vaulting, network uplift, payment orchestration, predictive routing), Dispute / Chargeback Recovery, Account Protection (sign-up, login, session), Abuse Prevention (checkout and post-purchase), Element for Payment Service Providers, and an Agentic Commerce suite for AI-agent-initiated transactions. The platform is built on what Forter describes as the world's largest first-party identity network, derived from real consumer interactions across hundreds of leading retailers, marketplaces, and food-delivery brands such as Adidas, eBay, Instacart, Nordstrom, Priceline, Sephora, and Wayfair. Forter exposes a public Core API (orders, 3DS, disputes, accounts, merchants, compensation, data privacy) and an Evidence API documented at docs.forter.com, alongside prebuilt integrations for Magento/Adobe Commerce, Salesforce B2C Commerce, commercetools, Adyen, Braintree, Checkout.com, Paysafe, Worldline, Worldpay, and others. Forter is also the sponsor of the open-source Trusted Agentic Commerce Protocol, a secure authentication and data-encryption protocol for AI agents, merchants, and merchant vendors. The company has raised approximately $525M in venture funding from Sequoia Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, NEA, and others, and has been valued at roughly $3B at last public reporting.

companies.name: Integrated Development Environment
companies.description: Integrated Development Environment (IDE) is a software application that consolidates the core developer workflow into a single interface, typically combining a source code editor, build automation tools, debugger, version control integration, intelligent code completion, refactoring, and language server protocol (LSP) support. Modern IDEs increasingly integrate AI coding assistants, agentic tooling, remote development containers, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients to extend the surface area beyond local file editing.

companies.name: Integration Patterns
companies.description: Integration Patterns are design patterns and best practices for integrating different software systems and applications, including messaging, data transformation, and service orchestration approaches. Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIP), as cataloged by Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf, provide a technology-independent vocabulary and visual notation harvested from proven solutions to recurring integration problems, organized into Messaging Channels, Message Construction, Message Routing, Message Transformation, Messaging Endpoints, and System Management.

companies.name: Irreducible
companies.description: Irreducible is a cryptography company accelerating the zero-knowledge (ZK) revolution by turning advanced proof systems into cost-efficient, production infrastructure. The company invented and leads Binius, a state-of-the-art zero-knowledge SNARK built on towers of binary fields that natively handles bitwise operations to deliver order-of-magnitude speedups over prime-field systems on ordinary CPUs, GPUs, mobile devices, and custom FPGA hardware. Irreducible operates its own FPGA-based proof-generation service and publishes Binius as open-source Rust crates. Target applications include self-sovereign identity, on-chain privacy, content provenance for AI-generated media, and verifiable supercomputing. Irreducible was backed by a Series A co-led by Paradigm and Bain Capital Crypto. This profile was seeded as a Paradigm portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company exposes an open-source developer surface (crates + docs) rather than a public REST API.

companies.name: Mips
companies.description: MIPS is a processor IP and compute company building embedded and edge AI silicon for automotive, robotics, and mission-critical systems. Its portfolio spans the MIPS RISC-V CPU families (M8500, I8500, P8700, S8200), the ARC processor and NPX/VPX accelerator lines, and development tooling such as MIPS Atlas Explorer virtual platforms and the ASIP Designer / ASIP Programmer toolchains. MIPS frames its offering around a "Sense, Think, Act, Communicate" signal chain for real-time autonomy — what it calls Physical AI at the edge. MIPS is a semiconductor IP licensor rather than a public web-API provider; this profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched with identity and probed security posture.

companies.name: Protect AI
companies.description: Protect AI is an AI/ML security company building defensive tooling and open-source security research for the model supply chain, large language model (LLM) applications, and runtime AI workloads. The commercial platform is anchored by three products — Guardian (AI model security and third-party model scanning across PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Keras, Pickle, GGUF, Safetensors, and 35+ formats with Hugging Face, SageMaker, MLflow, S3, Git, and Artifactory integrations), Recon (scalable AI red teaming with an attack library of 450+ known attacks against LLM applications mapped to OWASP LLM Top 10), and Layer (runtime AI security with 27 turnkey policies, eBPF and SDK collection, and DataDog/Splunk/Elastic/PagerDuty integration). Protect AI also stewards a portfolio of widely used open-source AI security projects on GitHub including LLM Guard (input/output scanner toolkit for prompt injection, PII, toxicity, secrets, and data leakage detection), ModelScan (model serialization attack scanner), Rebuff (prompt injection detector, archived May 2025), NB Defense (Jupyter notebook security), AI Exploits (real-world AI/ML vulnerability demonstrations), and Vulnhuntr (LLM-driven autonomous vulnerability discovery), plus the huntr bug bounty platform for AI/ML with over 17,000 security researchers. Protect AI was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in 2025 and is being integrated into the Prisma AIRS AI security platform. No public, programmatic developer API or OpenAPI specification is published for Guardian, Recon, or Layer at the time of this profile — integration is performed via product CLIs, SDKs, eBPF agents, and platform connectors documented behind Palo Alto Networks customer accounts.

companies.name: Ratify
companies.description: Ratify is a CNCF Sandbox open-source verification framework for container images and other supply chain artifacts in Kubernetes environments. It enables policy-driven artifact ratification by coordinating any number of pluggable verifiers (signatures, SBOMs, scan results, attestations) against a given policy, integrating with Kubernetes admission webhooks via the Gatekeeper policy engine. Ratify is developed by the ratify-project GitHub organization (originally a Microsoft open-source project), written in Go, and distributed as a CLI tool, Go library, and Kubernetes admission webhook server. It supports OCI-compliant artifact stores including Azure Container Registry, Amazon ECR, and Docker Hub. Ratify exposes an internal HTTP verification API (v2alpha1) consumed by its webhook server but does not publish a public-facing REST API or OpenAPI specification.

companies.name: React Foundation
companies.description: The React Foundation is a Linux Foundation project announced in February 2026 that supports React, React Native, and supporting components after Meta contributed the React project to the Linux Foundation. It ensures the continued open governance, neutral stewardship, and long-term development of the React ecosystem used by millions of front-end and mobile developers worldwide. The Foundation does not currently expose a public, programmatic REST API; engagement with the project happens primarily through GitHub repositories and documentation channels.

companies.name: Seed Club
companies.description: Seed Club is a web3 accelerator and community focused on consumer crypto, helping founders build "a dramatically more interesting internet" where the value created by online communities is captured by people rather than platforms. It runs a cohort-based accelerator (currently SC07: Consumer Crypto), a ventures/investment arm, and a portfolio program, alongside a broader community of builders, creators, and token communities. Seed Club operates as a community-owned organization and publishes a public Community Handbook, a blog, and open-source dApp code (Farcaster frames, crowdfunding smart contracts). It is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. Seed Club is a program and community brand rather than an API provider — it exposes no public developer platform, REST/GraphQL API, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface at this time.

companies.name: Sinclair, Inc.
companies.description: Sinclair, Inc. (Nasdaq: SBGI), formerly Sinclair Broadcast Group, is a diversified media company and one of the largest U.S. local television broadcasters. The company operates 177-185+ TV stations across roughly 79-86 markets affiliated with all major broadcast networks (Fox, NBC, CBS, ABC, MyNetworkTV, The CW), owns Tennis Channel, holds a stake in YES Network, and runs digital multicast networks Comet, Charge!, Roar, and The Nest. Sinclair Ventures houses the company's non-broadcast operations, including ad/martech units (AMP, Drive Auto, Free State, Digital Remedy/Compulse) and broadcast technology subsidiaries (Dielectric, ONE Media Technologies, Bitpath, CAST.ERA, Broadspan Wireless). In 2019 Sinclair acquired the Fox Sports regional sports networks for ~$9.6 billion through a Diamond Sports Group joint venture; Diamond was rebranded Bally Sports in 2021, filed Chapter 11 in March 2023, exited bankruptcy in January 2025 as Main Street Sports Group, rebranded again as FanDuel Sports Network, and is winding down operations in mid-2026. Sinclair publishes no public developer APIs.

companies.name: Theta EdgeCloud
companies.description: Theta EdgeCloud is a distributed, hybrid AI and video cloud built on the Theta Network blockchain, offering on-demand GPU compute for AI model training, fine-tuning, inference, video transcoding, and live streaming. EdgeCloud aggregates GPU capacity from data-center hyperscaler partners and a global community of Edge Nodes (consumer and enterprise GPUs) into a single dispatchable compute layer addressable via REST, JSON-RPC, and SDK clients. Core services include EdgeCloud AI Services (on-demand model inference APIs for LLMs, image, audio, and multimodal models such as Llama, Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and Whisper; agentic RAG chatbots; GPU-backed Jupyter notebooks; dedicated GPU pod deployments; and AI training with GPU clusters), EdgeCloud Video Services (the Theta Video API for upload, transcoding, livestream ingestion, DRM, NFT-gated playback, and webhooks), EdgeStore (decentralized object storage), and the EdgeCloud Client (an installable node that earns TFUEL for contributing GPU and bandwidth). Developers authenticate with x-api-key tokens issued from the EdgeCloud dashboard, manage deployments programmatically through api.thetaedgecloud.com and the Node.js SDK @thetalabs/theta-edgecloud, and access on-demand model endpoints (also distributed through RapidAPI). The Theta blockchain layer is EVM-compatible with an Ethereum RPC adaptor, supports TNT-20 tokens and NFTs, and underwrites EdgeCloud's payment, rewards, and staking economy through the THETA governance token and TFUEL gas token. Theta operates as Theta Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California.

companies.name: Audi Connect / myAudi
companies.description: Audi Connect is the connected-vehicle services platform from Audi AG, the Ingolstadt, Germany-based luxury automaker and member of the Volkswagen Group. Delivered to drivers through the embedded MMI infotainment system and the myAudi companion app for iOS and Android, Audi Connect spans remote vehicle control (lock/unlock, remote start, climate pre-conditioning, EV charge management), safety and security (Emergency Call/eCall, Audi Service Request, stolen-vehicle locator, geofencing, speed alerts), and in-car infotainment (real-time traffic, satellite map imagery, parking and fuel information, weather, news, natural voice recognition, Amazon Alexa, Amazon Music, Wi-Fi hotspot, and an in-vehicle app store with Disney+ and passenger gaming on supported models). Services are packaged as Audi connect CARE (included for ten years on new U.S. Audis), Audi connect NAV (navigation and live traffic), and Audi connect PLUS (premium streaming and Wi-Fi). For EVs and PHEVs, Audi Connect adds charging-station search, remote charge monitoring, and cabin pre-conditioning. Audi does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, OAuth program, or partner SDK for myAudi/Audi Connect; programmatic access today is brokered by third-party connected-car aggregators (Smartcar, High Mobility, Enode, Mojio) under Audi's commercial agreements, and community projects reverse-engineer the mobile-app endpoints. Audi has publicly discussed an internal OpenAPI-driven API management strategy (with Nagarro) but the surface remains private to Audi, VW Group brands, and authorized partners.

companies.description: Bassetts Ice Cream is a Philadelphia ice cream brand founded in 1861 and self-described as "America's oldest ice cream brand." The company is family-owned across six generations of the Bassett / Strange family, retails out of a single counter at Reading Terminal Market in Center City Philadelphia, and operates a wholesale frozen-dessert distribution business serving restaurants, hotels, country clubs, dipping parlors, supermarkets, and caterers within a 40-mile radius of Philadelphia (with distributor partners in the New York metro and Florida). Bassetts also exports to China (since 2008), South Korea (2017), and Taiwan (2020), and ships pints nationwide via Goldbelly. The corporate office is at 1211 Chestnut Street, Suite 410, Philadelphia, PA. The bassettsicecream.com website is hosted on Wix and exposes no public API, no developer portal, and no machine-readable product catalog.

companies.name: CarbonChain
companies.description: CarbonChain is a London- and New York-based carbon accounting platform founded in 2019 that is purpose-built for the highest-emitting, hardest-to- track commodity supply chains — metals and mining, energy, manufacturing, and agriculture. Its AI-assisted platform builds asset- and transaction- level emissions pictures using activity-based emission factors, and packages those calculations into modules for supply-chain emissions, corporate carbon footprints (Scope 1, 2, 3), product carbon footprints, scenario analysis, and regulatory compliance. The flagship CarbonChain Comply release ships a Carbon Reporting Hub aligned with EU CSRD, UK SECR, US SEC, and CDP, along with EU/UK CBAM declaration validation, automated CBAM XML generation, and a Supplier Engagement Module for collecting and validating supplier emissions data. CarbonChain Connect links producers and importers through shared installation-level CBAM infrastructure. The company is a CDP Accredited Provider (2024), is ISO 27001 certified, and is backed by Y Combinator, Union Square Ventures, Voyager VC, and Aera VC, with $10M Series A funding (2023). CarbonChain serves manufacturers, commodity traders, banks, and procurement teams, and offers system-to-system API integration for delivering activity data in and pulling gold-standard emissions calculations out — but it does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source client library. API access is offered as part of customer integration projects rather than as a self-serve developer surface.

companies.name: Conifer
companies.description: Conifer (YC S26) builds Sage, a local-first AI runtime and workspace that runs models entirely on your own machine. Its inference engine is written from scratch in Rust, reaching up to 60% faster decode than llama.cpp on Apple Silicon, and pairs an editor, integrated terminal, file viewers, and an agent runtime inside a kernel-level sandbox so tool calls only touch what you allow. Conifer routes each request to the cheapest capable model, starting with free on-device inference and falling back to cloud only when needed, cutting AI spend by up to 80%. The desktop app ships as Juniper for macOS, Windows, and Linux with no accounts, no telemetry, and no cloud dependency. Conifer is proprietary and distributed as compiled binaries; it currently exposes no public web API.

companies.name: dopl technologies
companies.description: Dopl Technologies is a Seattle-based data and AI company (founded 2022, Techstars-backed) democratizing access to diagnostic exams and interventional procedures through telerobotic ultrasound. Its Dopl Traverse platform and SonoFlex app let a remote sonographer operate an ultrasound probe over a network from significant distances, extending specialist-level imaging into rural and workforce-constrained regions. Field testing in rural Washington hospitals has reduced patient wait times by over 90 percent. The company cites 50M+ missed ultrasound exams annually and $19.5B in lost revenue from unequal imaging access, and expects FDA clearance in 2027 before expanding into minimally invasive procedures. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation; this record is a network stub maintained for discovery and future enrichment.

companies.name: Dwight Capital
companies.description: Dwight Capital LLC is a leading commercial real estate finance company in the United States, with a loan servicing portfolio exceeding $15 billion across all affiliates. The firm originates Balance-Sheet Bridge and New Construction Loans, FHA/HUD Insured Loans, C-PACE Financing, Mezzanine Financing, and Preferred Equity for multifamily, healthcare, and mixed-use commercial real estate. Headquartered in New York City with an additional office in Sunny Isles Beach, Florida, Dwight is consistently ranked among the top FHA/HUD multifamily lenders in the country and operates as a privately held business specializing in bridge-to-HUD execution for commercial real estate sponsors.

companies.name: Gas POS
companies.description: Gas Pos is a North Little Rock, Arkansas technology company (founded 2015) that builds cloud-based point-of-sale systems and EMV-certified fuel dispensers for gas stations and truck stops across the United States. Delivered as equipment-as-a-service with no upfront hardware cost, the platform pairs touchscreen POS terminals, barcode scanners, and back-office inventory and pricing tools with PCI-compliant, EMV-certified payment processing at both the register and the pump. It accepts major fleet cards including Comdata, Comchek, EFS, T-Chek, Voyager, and Fleetone, and lets operators manage item pricing and inventory remotely from a phone. Backed by 500 Global and Pioneer Fund. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface has been located to date.

The company recruits and interviews real people matching a client's ideal customer profile, then models each participant as an always-on AI avatar grounded in that interview data. Teams use the resulting synthetic audience to test surveys, messaging, ad creative, pricing, and product flows and retrieve population-scale quantitative results plus qualitative commentary in minutes rather than the weeks traditional market research takes. Auxos is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company founded by Ashton Daniel, Jerry Wu, and Kerry Lu, targeting marketing, product, and research teams. Co-founded by Stanford materials scientist Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue refined the orbital nickel-hydrogen cell into a grid-scale "Energy Storage Vessel" (ESV) targeting a 30-year, 30,000+ cycle service life with 100% usable depth of discharge, ~90% round-trip efficiency, an operating range of -20 C to +60 C, no thermal runaway risk, and no active thermal management. The ESV's aqueous metal cell (AMC) uses a nickel hydroxide cathode, a nickel-alloy anode, an alkaline electrolyte, and hermetically sealed hydrogen gas storage built from steel, nickel, fiberglass, resin, and water — no lithium, cobalt, or rare earths. EnerVenue is scaling manufacturing through a one-million- square-foot gigafactory in Shelby County, Kentucky (1 GWh phase one, scaling toward 20 GWh per year with ~$1B of follow-on investment) plus a high-volume line in Changzhou, China (250 MWh by Q3 2026, 1 GWh in 2027). Customer commitments exceed 7 GWh and include Pine Gate Renewables (2.4 GWh, multi-year), Green Energy Renewable Solutions (Nicon Industries), Sonnell Power Solutions, and VedantaESS. The company closed a $300M Series B in 2026 to fund the gigafactory build-out. EnerVenue sells hardware, EPC-integrated storage systems, and long-duration service warranties — it does not publish a developer API, SDK, public OpenAPI specification, or open-source repository.

companies.name: Defer
companies.description: Defer was a Paris-based, Y Combinator-backed (W23) zero-infrastructure background jobs platform for Node.js and TypeScript developers, founded in 2022 by Bryan Frimin and Charly Poly. The product converted regular JavaScript/TypeScript async functions into managed background jobs with configurable retries, throttling, concurrency controls, scheduled crons, multi-environment support, alerting, and a hosted dashboard — removing the need for developers to operate their own queues, workers, and Redis-style infrastructure. Defer shipped client SDKs and framework integrations (Next.js, RedwoodJS) and a CLI/build pipeline that uploaded function bundles to the Defer cloud for execution. The company appears to have wound down its hosted service in 2024 — the defer.run domain now 301-redirects to digger.tools, no end-of-service post-mortem is publicly linked from the homepage, and the GitHub organization (github.com/defer-run) last saw meaningful activity in July 2024 with the final defer.client release v2.3.0 cut on 2024-03-06. The open source client libraries remain available but are effectively unmaintained and the hosted backend they depended on is no longer operational. This catalog entry preserves the historical footprint of Defer as part of the 2022-2024 wave of "zero-infrastructure" background-job and durable- execution startups (Inngest, Trigger.dev, Hatchet, Temporal Cloud, Restate) so the design pattern and the players who pursued it remain discoverable in the API Evangelist network.

In March 2022, Swedish pulp and paper group BillerudKorsnäs (now Billerud) completed its acquisition of Verso for $825 million in cash, taking the company private and rebranding it as Billerud Americas Corporation. The Verso standalone brand, ticker, and corporate web presence have been retired; ongoing North American operations, paper grades, and customer relationships now sit inside Billerud's global business.

companies.name: Vista

Its FDA-cleared Vista AI Scan product lets technologists of varying skill levels perform high-quality, standardized MRI exams across multiple hospital sites without on-site specialists, claiming faster scan times, more available scan slots, and reduced imaging backlogs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a product/marketing website only — there is no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer surface to catalog.

companies.name: Zet

Its core product is a fixed-deposit-backed (FD-backed) secured credit card starting at very low deposits, requiring no income proof or prior credit history, alongside credit-score monitoring and improvement tools, UPI payments, cashback rewards, a ZET Plus subscription tier, and a ZET Fixit credit-report error-resolution service. Backed by General Catalyst and Sequoia Capital, Zet operates as a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) and, as of this enrichment pass, exposes no public developer platform, API, OpenAPI, or documented developer surface.

companies.name: 42 Floors
companies.description: 42Floors was a Y Combinator- and 500 Global-backed commercial real estate search platform founded in 2011 by Jason Freedman to make it easy to discover and lease office, coworking, retail, industrial, and warehouse space across top U.S. markets. It aggregated a large listings database (the "42Floors MLS") that brokers and tenants searched online. The company was acquired by Knotel in 2018, and the 42floors.com domain and listings service were later taken over by Yardi, which folded them into CommercialCafe — 42floors.com now redirects there. The only surviving developer surface is the first-party `mls` RubyGem, a client for the (now-decommissioned) 42Floors MLS API at mls.42floors.com.

companies.name: Anki
companies.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

companies.name: Atomic Finance
companies.description: Atomic.Finance was a non-custodial, Bitcoin-native financial platform based in Toronto, Canada (founded 2018) that built options-trading and hedging products directly on Bitcoin using Discreet Log Contracts (DLCs) — with no custody, no wrapping, and no swapping. Rather than a hosted REST API, the company's public developer surface is a body of open-source Bitcoin and DLC tooling published to GitHub (the atomicfinance organization, 34 repositories) and to npm under two first-party scopes: @atomicfinance/* (the Bitcoin Abstraction Layer SDK) and @node-dlc/* (a Node.js implementation of the DLC and Lightning wire protocols). The company is reported out of business, but the libraries remain published and implement DLC, BIP-340 Schnorr/adaptor signatures, and BOLT Lightning standards.

companies.name: BetaList

Startups gain exposure through the BetaList website, daily email newsletter, and social media channels. No public developer API has been identified; startup discovery and submission are handled through the web interface.

companies.name: Bloom
companies.description: Bloom was a decentralized identity, credit-attestation and verifiable-credentials company backed by Pantera Capital, built on Ethereum and IPFS around three products: BloomID (identity attestation), BloomIQ (a credit registry) and BloomScore (credit risk scoring). Its stated aim was to let traditional and digital-currency lenders serve people who cannot obtain a bank account or a credit score, and it announced a TransUnion partnership in 2020 for consumer credit monitoring. Bloom is wound down. Its integration SDKs were archived on GitHub in 2021, its API, documentation and status hosts no longer resolve, bloom.co now redirects to a domain-broker sale listing, and Bloom HoldCo LLC filed a Form 15-12G on 2025-08-14 terminating Exchange Act registration of its BLT token with holders of record stated as "none". What survives is open source: 40 public repositories under github.com/hellobloom and 19 unmaintained but installable npm packages under the @bloomprotocol scope implementing the W3C and DIF decentralized-identity stack (Verifiable Credentials, DIDs, Presentation Exchange, Credential Manifest, WACI).

companies.name: Bloomsbury
companies.description: Bloomsbury AI was a London-based natural-language-processing startup, backed by Seedcamp, that built Cape — an API making it easy to build software that answers questions about the contents of documents (machine reading / document question answering). Bloomsbury AI was acquired by Facebook in 2018; the hosted Cape API is terminated and bloomsbury.ai now serves only a farewell page. The team open sourced the Cape stack (web services, document QA, machine reader, and clients) under the bloomsburyai GitHub organization, which remains publicly available as archival source. This API Evangelist profile preserves that identity and the open-source footprint.

companies.name: Bug Labs
companies.description: Bug Labs is a New York City enterprise software company founded in 2006, first as one of the earliest open-source modular hardware makers and later as an enterprise IoT platform provider serving Fortune 500 customers including Verizon, Comcast, VMware, Ford, Charter and Orange. Its current flagship product, Signalpattern, targets workflow fragmentation by mapping and connecting dispersed enterprise systems, automating cross-system tasks, and letting users interact with APIs directly without writing code. Bug Labs previously operated the well-known public IoT APIs dweet.io, dweetpro.io and freeboard.io; all three are decommissioned and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation or public API today. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital and Court Square Ventures.

companies.name: cargo.one
companies.description: cargo.one is a Berlin-headquartered digital freight platform that operates as an AI-native operating system for air and ocean freight logistics. The platform unifies freight forwarder operations by centralizing rates, partners, and systems on a single end-to-end surface shared between human teams and AI agents. For freight forwarders, cargo.one provides air e-booking with 76+ integrated airlines (300+ total network), ocean freight rate management with 10+ liner integrations, multimodal quoting across air, ocean, road, and local charges, a Rate Management System for buy/sell/internal rates, a branded 24/7 self-service Customer Portal, analytics dashboards, a 24/7 Global Network for cross-timezone quoting, and an API Suite with native TMS integrations for CargoWise, Cargospot, and Descartes. For carriers, cargo.one delivers a market-intelligence and customer-access platform spanning the end-to-end commercial cycle. AI workflows are offered in three deployment modes — Co-pilot (approval-based), Supervised (autonomous with escalation), and Autonomous — covering rate management, rate procurement, quoting, booking, and customer support automation, backed by retrieval-augmented generation and a cargo.one MCP Server for custom solutions. Notable customers include Lufthansa Cargo, Kuehne+Nagel, DSV, Maersk, CMA CGM, Hellmann, and Rhenus Logistics. cargo.one's API and TMS integrations are partner / enterprise offerings — there is no public self-serve OpenAPI specification, developer sandbox, or open-source SDK published outside of customer onboarding.

companies.name: Chef Robotics
companies.description: Chef Robotics is a San Francisco, California physical-AI company building AI-enabled robots for high-mix food production. Its core product is an NSF-certified food-assembly robot that picks, scoops, and deposits a wide range of ingredients — fresh, cooked, IQF, sauces, leafy greens, mixed vegetables, and discrete piece items — into trays, burritos, wraps, pizza bases, and other containers on conveyor lines. The robots are powered by ChefOS, a proprietary Generalized Food Manipulation Model trained on tens of millions of real-world servings and tens of thousands of hours of production data, combining vision, decision-making, and robot control across a See / Think / Act stack with continuous Fleet Learning. Chef Robotics sells via a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that bundles hardware, software updates, 24/7 monitoring, and customer success. Deployed customers include Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice, and Chef Bombay, with the fleet having produced 98+ million servings across the US, Canada, and Europe. The company is venture-backed (Kleiner Perkins, Avataar Ventures-led $43M Series A, Bloomberg Beta, Construct Capital) and serves frozen meals, fresh meals, co-manufacturing, D2C meal delivery, medically tailored meals, meatpacking, airline catering, and foodservice verticals. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for ChefOS — the platform is operated as a closed, fleet-managed service on Chef-owned hardware deployed inside customer facilities.

companies.name: Cloudcoreo
companies.description: CloudCoreo was a Seattle-based cloud security startup (founded 2016, seed round led by Madrona Venture Group) that built a cloud configuration and vulnerability-assessment platform to identify and remediate misconfigurations across public multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP). VMware acquired CloudCoreo in February 2018 and folded the team and product into VMware Cloud Services, where it became the basis of CloudHealth Secure State. The standalone CloudCoreo service and developer surface have since been retired: cloudcoreo.com is now a parked/for-sale domain and there is no live public API. The CloudCoreo GitHub organization remains, hosting the now-deprecated first-party CLI. This profile is a historical/lineage record, not an active API provider.

companies.name: Codex Protocol
companies.description: Codex Protocol was a blockchain startup (founded 2018, backed by Pantera Capital) that built a decentralized registry for unique physical assets — fine art, wine, watches and other collectibles — on Ethereum, using ERC-721 Codex Records and an ERC-20 Codex Coin (CODX) token, plus a Codex Viewer dapp and a Codex Registry REST API. The company is now defunct: its API and dapp repositories are archived, its documentation host no longer resolves, and its original marketing domain (codexprotocol.com) has been repurposed by a third party and redirects offsite. The surviving, verifiable first-party artifacts are the codex-protocol GitHub organization (13 repositories of smart contracts, services, and tooling) and four @codex-protocol npm packages. This profile was surfaced as a Pantera Capital portfolio company and is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical / defunct record.

companies.name: Computable
companies.description: Computable (Computable Labs) was a Pantera Capital-backed crypto startup that built the Computable Protocol, a decentralized data-market and "Datatrust" system letting participants create Fair, Free-Access (FFA) markets to pool, price, and share datasets on Ethereum. The project shipped developer client libraries (computable.js for JavaScript, computable.py for Python), a Datatrust API reference implementation, Computable Improvement Proposals (CIPs), and a protocol specification ("The Computable Book"). The GitHub organization and its repositories are archived and inactive (last activity 2022-2023) and the company's websites (computable.io and computablelabs.com) no longer resolve to a live property, so this profile documents the surviving open-source developer surface rather than a running service.

companies.name: CRED
companies.description: CRED is an Indian consumer fintech that started with premium credit-card bill payments and rewards and has expanded into peer-to-peer payments (Scan & Pay, Tap to Pay, RuPay credit card on UPI), short-term credit (CRED Cash, CRED Mint), wealth (CRED Money), e-commerce (CRED Store), and travel. CRED's surface area is overwhelmingly consumer-app and the company does not publish a public, self-service developer portal. Its engineering organisation contributes to the broader ecosystem via the engineering.cred.club tech blog and open-source repositories under the CRED-CLUB GitHub org. B2B integrations (merchant acceptance, issuer partnerships, etc.) are negotiated directly with the partnerships team.

companies.name: Datalogue
companies.description: Datalogue was a self-service data integration and preparation startup founded in 2015 that used machine learning to automatically classify, transform, and standardize data from disparate sources for analytics teams. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company was acquired by Nike in February 2019 and its standalone product was discontinued; the datalogue.io domain now serves an unrelated blog. This profile is retained for the API Evangelist network as a historical/portfolio record. The only surviving first-party developer artifacts are the company's public GitHub organization and an unmaintained Python SDK ("datalogue") still published on PyPI.

companies.name: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.)
companies.description: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.) was a pioneering social data platform that provided real-time and historical access to social media firehoses (Twitter, Facebook Topic Data, and more) through its CSDL filtering language and its Push, Historics, and Managed Sources REST APIs. Founded in 2007 and backed by Insight Partners and others, the company was acquired by Meltwater in 2019; the datasift.com domain now redirects to meltwater.com and the standalone DataSift developer platform and APIs have been discontinued. Official first-party client SDKs for Python, Ruby, PHP, Java, and Node.js remain published on public package registries under the datasift GitHub organization as historical artifacts.

companies.name: Deci AI
companies.description: Deci AI was a deep-learning development company (founded 2019, Tel Aviv) whose platform helped teams build, optimize, and deploy computer-vision and NLP models in production. Its stack combined the AutoNAC neural-architecture-search engine, the Infery inference runtime, and the open-source SuperGradients PyTorch training library — the home of the YOLO-NAS object-detection architecture. Deci was acquired by NVIDIA in 2024; deci.ai now redirects to NVIDIA and there is no live standalone hosted API or developer console. companies.name: Dharma Labs

This profile captures those honest historical artifacts; the provider ships no maintained API today.

companies.description: File formats define how information is encoded for storage in a computer file, spanning images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF), audio (WAV, MP3, OGG, FLAC), video (MP4, MOV, MKV), documents (PDF, HTML, DOCX, ODT), data serialization (JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, Parquet, Avro), archives (ZIP, TAR, GZIP), and executables. File formats are central to API and data interoperability, identified via filename extensions, magic numbers, MIME types, and IANA media-type registrations.

Plugins connected editors to shared Floobits workspaces where multiple developers edited the same files and terminals in real time over a synchronizing backend (built on a diff-match-patch model). companies.name: Getaround
companies.description: Getaround is a peer-to-peer car-sharing marketplace and connected-car technology company founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, with significant European operations across France, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Norway, and the United Kingdom. The platform pairs private and professional vehicle owners with renters who book cars by the hour or day, unlocking and starting vehicles from a mobile app rather than meeting the owner to exchange keys. The keyless experience is enabled by Getaround Connect, a proprietary in-car telematics device that the company designs and installs in shared vehicles to handle remote lock/unlock, ignition, GPS tracking, mileage reporting, fuel level monitoring, and trip event recording. Getaround acquired Drivy in 2019 to consolidate the European car-sharing market and acquired the HyreCar rideshare-driver rental marketplace in 2022. The company went public on the NYSE via a SPAC merger in December 2022 at a valuation of roughly $1.2 billion, was delisted from the NYSE in July 2024 and transferred to OTC Pink under the ticker GETR after its market capitalization collapsed to roughly $24 million. On February 11, 2025, Getaround announced it was ceasing all United States operations — including HyreCar — while preserving its European business, which continues to operate in major EU cities under the same Getaround Connect platform. Getaround has never published a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; partner integrations with insurers, fleet operators, and automotive OEMs have historically been delivered through private, contract-bound APIs rather than a self-service developer surface. The company's GitHub organization hosts primarily forks of generic open-source libraries (Braintree SDKs, iOS testing frameworks, logging libraries) rather than first-party API artifacts.

companies.name: Heyzap
companies.description: Heyzap was a mobile-game advertising, discovery, and monetization company. It began as a social game-discovery network and pivoted into a mobile ad mediation platform, offering iOS, Android, Unity, Cordova, and Adobe AIR/ANE SDKs that let game developers serve and mediate ads across networks such as AdMob, AppLovin, Vungle, Chartboost, AdColony, and Facebook Audience Network. Heyzap was acquired by Fyber (RNTS Media) in 2016 and its brand was later folded into Digital Turbine. Heyzap never published a public REST API; its developer surface was the mobile ad-mediation SDKs distributed via GitHub (github.com/Heyzap) and package registries. The heyzap.com domain is now parked/for-sale and the developer documentation site no longer resolves; this profile preserves the historical, first-party SDK artifacts that remain publicly available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

companies.name: HTTP/2
companies.description: HTTP/2 is the second major version of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol, defined by the IETF in RFC 7540 and standardized in 2015. It optimizes use of network resources and reduces perceived latency by introducing a binary framing layer over a single TCP connection, with full request and response multiplexing across independent bidirectional streams. HTTP/2 uses HPACK header compression to eliminate redundant header data, credit-based flow control via WINDOW_UPDATE frames, stream prioritization through dependencies and weights, and server push via PUSH_PROMISE frames to proactively deliver anticipated resources. Core frame types include DATA, HEADERS, PRIORITY, RST_STREAM, SETTINGS, PUSH_PROMISE, PING, and GOAWAY, with the protocol preserving the existing HTTP semantics of methods, status codes, and headers while transforming how they are transported on the wire.

companies.name: Immunio
companies.description: IMMUNIO was a Montreal-based application security company (founded 2013) that built a real-time RASP (Runtime Application Self-Protection) platform to detect and block attacks against web applications and APIs without requiring code changes. Its product shipped as language-native agents for Ruby on Rails, Python (Django/Pyramid/Flask), Node.js/Express, Java, PHP, Scala and .NET, covering the OWASP Top 10 including Cross-Site Scripting and SQL Injection. The company raised roughly $8M from Bloomberg Beta, WhiteStar Capital, Real Ventures, Hoxton Ventures and BDC, and was acquired by Trend Micro in November 2017, where the technology was folded into Trend Micro's hybrid cloud and container security for the DevOps lifecycle. The immun.io and docs.immun.io properties have since been retired; the durable public surface today is the first-party agent libraries on RubyGems, PyPI and npm and the IMMUNIO GitHub organization.

companies.name: Impira
companies.description: Impira was a document-AI / intelligent-document-processing company that let business users turn unstructured content — documents, invoices, images, PDFs and webpages — into structured, queryable data by building and training extraction models without code. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Impira was acquired by Figma in early 2023 and its standalone product domains (impira.com, impira.io) no longer serve. Its GitHub organization (github.com/impira) survives, along with two first-party open-source Python libraries still published on PyPI: the official Impira Python SDK and DocQuery, an MIT-licensed document question-answering library. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record; there is no live API, developer portal, or hosted documentation surface remaining.

companies.name: Interana
companies.description: Interana was an event-based behavioral analytics platform for interactively querying large-scale event data (clickstream, product usage, and time-series data) at full resolution. Founded around 2013 in Redwood City, California by former Facebook engineers, it was used at scale by companies including Microsoft Bing. The company's team and technology were acquired by Twitter in March 2020; the standalone product was spun out and continued as Scuba Analytics (scuba.io), and the interana.com domain now redirects to its successor lineage. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical / defunct company record — there is no live public API surface, developer portal, or hosted documentation remaining. The only surviving first-party developer surface is the open-source Interana GitHub organization.

companies.name: iRobot
companies.description: iRobot Corporation is a Bedford, Massachusetts consumer robotics company best known for the Roomba robot vacuum and the Braava and Braava jet robot mop product lines. Founded in 1990 by MIT roboticists, iRobot pioneered the home cleaning robot category and has sold tens of millions of units worldwide. Its current portfolio includes the Roomba Max, Roomba Plus, and Roomba 100/200 series vacuums and combo (vacuum + mop) models, along with AutoWash and AutoEmpty docks, the iRobot Home App for scheduling and mapping, and a cleaning accessories and trade-in program. The proposed acquisition by Amazon was abandoned in January 2024 after regulatory pushback from the European Commission, after which iRobot underwent a major restructuring and layoffs. iRobot's revenue model is direct robot and accessory sales plus recurring consumables; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification, and its homesupport documentation explicitly notes that Wi-Fi connected Roombas do not have an open API. A community of unofficial reverse-engineered libraries (dorita980, rest980, pyirobot) exists but is not endorsed by iRobot.

companies.name: iZotope
companies.description: iZotope is a Cambridge, Massachusetts audio software company founded in 2001 that builds professional plugins for music production, audio repair, mixing, and mastering, with deep investments in AI-assisted and machine-learning-driven audio processing. Its flagship products include RX (audio restoration and dialogue repair widely used in film, TV, and podcast post-production), Ozone (mastering suite with Master Assistant), Neutron (mixing suite with Mix Assistant and Track Assistant), Nectar (vocal processing with Vocal Assistant), Tonal Balance Control (cross-session referencing), and the Music Production Suite bundle. iZotope's assistive technologies analyze incoming audio and propose starting-point chains, EQ curves, dynamics settings, and spectral repairs — historically among the first widely adopted AI features in the professional audio plugin market. iZotope was acquired by Native Instruments in 2024 and now sits inside Soundwide, the Francisco Partners- backed group that also includes Native Instruments, Plugin Alliance, Brainworx, iZotope, and others. Distribution is via desktop plugin formats (VST3, AudioUnit, AAX) for DAWs such as Pro Tools, Logic, Ableton Live, Cubase, Studio One, and Reaper; there is no public REST/HTTP developer API or SaaS developer platform. iZotope does license its DSP and ML-based audio algorithms to OEM partners as embedded SDKs (historically delivered to partners like Sony, Adobe, and Microsoft) and ships a small set of public GitHub repositories that are primarily internal C++/Lua tooling, embedded Linux Yocto layers for iZotope hardware, and accompanying code for academic audio research papers rather than a developer API surface.

companies.name: Kano Computing
companies.description: Kano Computing is a London-based technology company founded in 2013 by Alex Klein, Saul Klein and Yonatan Raz-Fridman that began by shipping build-it-yourself computer and coding kits designed to teach STEM and creative computing to children on top of Raspberry Pi hardware. Its catalog spanned the Kano Computer Kit, motion-sensor and Harry Potter / Star Wars coding wands, the Windows-based Kano PC built with Microsoft, and the Stem Player and Stem Video Projector consumer devices. Kano paired the hardware with Kano Code, a block-to-text creative-coding platform, and Kano World, an online making and sharing community. The company entered administration in 2023 and its assets now trade under the Stem brand; its developer footprint survives as open-source tooling in the KanoComputing GitHub organization and the npm @kano scope rather than a hosted API.

companies.name: Kik (Kin)
companies.description: Kik (Kin) refers to the Kin cryptocurrency created by Kik Interactive, the messaging company, as a blockchain-based digital currency for use inside consumer applications. Kin originally launched on a fork of the Stellar network and later migrated to Solana, shipping first-party developer SDKs (JavaScript/Node and Python) under the kinecosystem GitHub organization and a developer program at developer.kin.org. The Kin project is now defunct: the developer surface no longer resolves, every kinecosystem repository is archived, the published SDKs are deprecated, and Kik itself was acquired by MediaLab AI Inc. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and is retained as a historical record of a wound-down crypto developer surface.

companies.name: LaunchKit
companies.description: LaunchKit was a set of web-based tools for mobile app developers, built by Cluster Labs, Inc. in San Francisco and backed by GV. Its products included Screenshot Builder for App Store screenshots, Review Monitor for App Store review alerts, a Sales Reporter, hosted App Websites, and Super Users and Cloud Config delivered through the LaunchKit iOS SDK. LaunchKit joined Google in 2016 and the codebase was released as open source under Apache 2.0. Atropos has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; GENEVA OS, TQL, ACE, ChatRWD, and the Evidence Agent are proprietary enterprise software delivered under contract to health-system and life-sciences customers, and the company's public GitHub org contains only forks (FAISS, HELM, security-policy-templates, terraform-aws-github-runner) and a small number of internal research notebooks rather than any shippable client library.

It operates an open, crowdsourced delivery network of more than one million rider partners serving supermarkets, pharmacies, fresh-food and restaurant merchants across thousands of counties and cities, alongside merchant fulfillment products such as the Haibo in-store logistics system and the Dada Youjian picking service. DFDL was developed by the Open Grid Forum (OGF) and is also published as ISO/IEC 23415:2004. Apache Daffodil is the reference open-source implementation, with the latest release being version 4.1.0.

Within an API context, flowcharts are used to model workflows, integration patterns, retry logic, authentication flows, and the orchestration of services. This index links to the canonical specifications and documentation for the protocol; no OpenAPI is generated because FTP is not an HTTP API.

A stability pool absorbs liquidations and rewards depositors with discounted collateral, while a Peg Stability Module and a multi-source oracle (Pyth Network primary, Switchboard fallback) keep USH near its peg. Hedge is an on-chain protocol rather than a hosted REST API; its documentation, whitepaper, and audited Solana program are its public surface. companies.name: Midas
companies.description: Midas is an onchain asset-management protocol that brings institutional-grade investment strategies onchain as tokenized real-world assets (RWAs). Investors mint and redeem Midas tokens directly against the underlying assets, and the resulting ERC-20 tokens can be used as collateral and as building blocks throughout the onchain economy. API and EDI access is not self-service: prospective integrators must submit a Direct Integration request, and fees may apply.

Its lead program, AU-409, is a first-in-human Phase 1 candidate for liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma), with additional pipeline work in heart-safe chemotherapy and other oncology indications. Auransa is a DCVC / DCVC Bio portfolio company, also backed by Lux Capital, 11.2 Capital, and Harmonix Fund. companies.name: Incandor
companies.description: Incandor is a San Francisco based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building behavioral intelligence infrastructure for fraud and abuse detection. Rather than relying on identity verification at account creation, Incandor constructs a behavioral map of every user on a platform from how they physically interact with an app or website — mouse dynamics, keystroke timing, scroll patterns, and on mobile how a device is held. It requires no fraud labels and no enrollment period, working from the first session. At the individual level it identifies account takeovers with greater than 99 percent accuracy; at the population level it separates out coordinated fraud rings, mule operators, shared operators, bots and agents, and coerced or duress sessions. Incandor is delivered as a programmable API and a client-side telemetry SDK rather than a black-box risk score, letting fraud teams combine behavioral signals with their own transaction history, customer records, and business rules. It collects only behavioral signals — not what users type, read, or view — keeping user data private by design. The company was founded by Matthew Yekell (CEO) and Luc Rosenzweig (CTO), both Stanford CS graduates. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; the developer platform is currently early access.

companies.name: Fixed Format
companies.description: Fixed format (also known as fixed-width) is a data interchange approach where every field has a predefined column width and is space-padded as needed. companies.name: HTML
companies.description: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language for creating web pages and web applications. Maintained as a Living Standard by WHATWG and developed in close coordination with the W3C, HTML defines the structure and semantics of web content alongside CSS for presentation and JavaScript for behavior. The current specification covers semantic elements, multimedia (audio, video, picture, track), the canvas API, forms with rich input types and validation, web storage, custom elements, the dialog and popover patterns, and a broad set of DOM and document conformance rules. This index covers HTML-related standards, specifications, references, and resources relevant to API designers and web developers building on top of HTTP.

companies.name: HTML5
companies.description: HTML5 is the fifth major version of the HyperText Markup Language used for structuring and presenting content on the web. Standardized by the W3C in 2014 and now maintained by WHATWG as the HTML Living Standard, HTML5 introduced semantic elements (article, section, nav, header, footer, aside), native multimedia via the audio and video elements, the canvas drawing surface, web storage (localStorage and sessionStorage), geolocation, drag-and-drop, offline application support, Web Workers for background processing, and richer form input types with built-in validation. HTML5 remains the foundation for modern web applications and the substrate that HTTP-based APIs ultimately render and consume on the client.

Tractable reached unicorn status in June 2021 and secured a $65M investment from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 in July 2023, scaling to over 300 employees across offices in London, Warsaw, Paris, Milan, Spain, Romania, New York, Toronto, Tokyo, and Bangkok. The product is delivered through flexible desktop and API integrations with FNOL, estimatics, and claim review systems, but the developer surface is gated to enterprise partners — there is no public developer portal, self-service API key, OpenAPI specification, SDK release, or open-source repository, and no publicly published authentication, endpoint, pricing, or rate-limit documentation.

The app combines public transit (bus, rail, metro, tram, ferry), micromobility (bike share, scooter, e-bike), ride-hail, walking, and driving into multi-modal routes with real-time arrivals, disruption alerts, step-by-step navigation, fare comparisons, and journey-saving features such as Get Me Somewhere, Go, and Citymapper CLUB (its paid premium subscription). In March 2023 Citymapper was acquired by Via Transportation, the New York-based TransitTech company that supplies on-demand transit, paratransit, and network-planning software to cities and transit agencies; Via integrates Citymapper as the rider-facing layer of its end-to-end transit platform alongside Remix (network planning) and Via's own on-demand operations software. Citymapper additionally offers a B2B advertising platform (ads.citymapper.com) targeting urban commuters. Citymapper previously published a self-service Directions API, a Navigation SDK (iOS, Android, Web), and Travel Time / Routing endpoints, but discontinued all self-serve developer products on 23 June 2023; remaining transit-data and routing integrations are now delivered under enterprise contracts through Via Transportation rather than via a public developer portal. There is no current public OpenAPI specification, self-serve API key, or open-access developer documentation for Citymapper.

companies.name: Collegevine
companies.description: CollegeVine is a Cambridge, Massachusetts company, backed by Menlo Ventures, that has repositioned itself as "the AI operating system for universities." Its platform pairs automated ingestion of data from campus systems (a Data layer) with a unified Ontology of institutional operations and an AI Operations layer of agents, applications, and ML models that connect directly to a university's CRM and admissions workflows. CollegeVine also operates a large consumer-facing college-admissions guidance property (chancing engine, essay guidance, and an AI counselor) at collegevine.com and blog.collegevine.com. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or published SDK for its product; engagement is enterprise sales and demo driven. It does maintain an active public GitHub organization of open-source PureScript, Haskell, and TypeScript libraries.

companies.name: Conagra Brands
companies.description: Conagra Brands is a leading North American branded consumer packaged goods (CPG) food company headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. Its portfolio of iconic frozen, refrigerated, and shelf-stable brands includes Marie Callender's, Healthy Choice, Slim Jim, Reddi-wip, Hunt's, Banquet, Birds Eye, Duncan Hines, and Orville Redenbacher's. Conagra internally describes itself as API-first across its digital estate, but does not publish any public developer APIs at this time. Partner integrations such as foodservice, retail, and supplier portals are managed via direct B2B agreements rather than a public developer surface.

companies.name: Confluence Labs
companies.description: Confluence Labs is a San Francisco AI research company (Y Combinator Winter 2026, backed by Paul Graham) focused on learning efficiency — building machine learning systems that learn from limited data and few experiments. Founded by Brent Burdick and Niranjan Baskaran, the lab works on hypothesis generation (using AI to design maximally informative experiments) and data-efficient modeling (combining large language models with discrete program search) to accelerate breakthroughs in data-sparse domains such as drug design, materials engineering, hardware, and physics discovery. The team reported state-of-the-art performance on the ARC-AGI-2 reasoning benchmark using LLM-driven program synthesis and open-sourced their solver on GitHub. Confluence Labs currently publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; this profile captures verified company identity for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Discovery Communications
companies.description: Discovery Communications was a global media company providing original and purchased programming across multiple distribution platforms before merging with WarnerMedia in 2022 to form Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), a leading global media and entertainment company whose portfolio spans HBO Max, Discovery Channel, CNN, Warner Bros. film studios, DC, Food Network, HGTV, and other television, film, and streaming brands. No public developer APIs are documented at the corporate level; technical and partnership inquiries are handled at the individual brand or business-unit level.

companies.name: Domtar
companies.description: Domtar is committed to turning responsibly sourced wood fiber into essential products like paper, pulp, recycled packaging, tissue, and lumber. No public developer-facing APIs have been identified at this time; this index will be updated if any are made available.
