companies.name: Duetto
companies.description: Duetto is a San Francisco–headquartered hospitality technology company providing a cloud-based Revenue and Profit Operating System (RP-OS) for hotels, casinos, resorts, and independent properties. Duetto's platform combines dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, group business optimization, benchmarking, and reporting to help hospitality operators optimize room rates, profitability, and total revenue performance. Core products include GameChanger (real-time dynamic pricing engine), ScoreBoard (forecasting and reporting dashboard), BlockBuster (group business optimization), Advance (AI-powered demand forecasting), HotStats (profitability benchmarking), and GameTime (select-service hotel revenue management). Duetto serves over 7,500 properties in more than 100 countries, with customers including Meliá, Sonesta, Virgin Hotels, and Sandman Hotel Group. Duetto integrates with major property management systems (PMS), central reservation systems (CRS), booking engines, and channel managers including Cloudbeds, Oracle OPERA / OHIP, Mews, Sabre, Amadeus, SiteMinder, and Infor. Duetto exposes an Open API for technical integration partners but does not publish a public, self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification — API access is partner-only and gated through a structured onboarding process with a self-testing toolkit. Revenue is generated through SaaS subscriptions to its revenue management products.

companies.name: eBPF Foundation
companies.description: The eBPF Foundation is a Linux Foundation project that advances eBPF technology by guiding upstream development, promoting its benefits, and enhancing its security and reliability. eBPF enables programmable kernel functionality for networking, observability, tracing, and security without changing kernel source code. The Foundation itself does not operate a public API; it stewards the technology and community.

companies.name: Ericsson
companies.description: Ericsson (Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson) is a Swedish multinational networking and telecommunications equipment vendor headquartered in Kista, Stockholm. Founded in 1876, the company supplies mobile and fixed network infrastructure to communication service providers worldwide and operates across three product areas: Networks (5G RAN, 5G Core, Cloud RAN, transport), Cloud Software & Services (OSS/BSS, orchestration, billing, charging, analytics), and Enterprise Wireless Solutions (private 5G via Cradlepoint). Ericsson holds more than 60,000 granted patents and operates 21 R&D centers, with networks that carry roughly 40 percent of the world's mobile data traffic. In 2024 Ericsson and twelve major operators — AT&T, Bharti Airtel, Deutsche Telekom, KDDI, Orange, Reliance Jio, Singtel, Telefonica, Telstra, T-Mobile, Verizon, and Vodafone — closed Aduna, a 50:50 joint venture that aggregates CAMARA-aligned network APIs (SIM Swap, Number Verification, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Device Reachability, Scam Signal, Call Forwarding Signal, Connectivity Insights, OTP SMS) and exposes them through hyperscaler and CPaaS channel partners (Microsoft Azure Marketplace, Google Cloud, Vonage, Sinch, Infobip). Ericsson also owns Vonage (acquired 2022), which operates the public-facing developer portal for many of these network capabilities, and runs the Ericsson Intelligent Automation Platform (EIAP) for ORAN-aligned rApp development. Ericsson does not publish a single consolidated developer portal or canonical OpenAPI catalog at ericsson.com — its programmable surface is delivered indirectly through Aduna, Vonage, and channel partners, and most of its public GitHub presence is research tooling and infrastructure software (CodeChecker, CodeCompass, ecchronos) rather than developer-facing APIs.

companies.name: Exxon Mobil
companies.description: Exxon Mobil Corporation is one of the world's largest publicly traded international energy companies, exploring for, producing, and refining oil and natural gas and manufacturing petroleum and chemical products. This repository tracks any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with Exxon Mobil.

companies.name: Filmgrail
companies.description: Filmgrail is an Oslo, Norway based software company offering an AI-powered digital platform for cinema operators. Its product suite bundles a cinema content management system (CMS), native iOS and Android mobile apps, branded cinema websites, and marketing and analytics tooling into a single managed offering, with a loyalty system, festival platform, push notifications, and a planning tool layered on top. Filmgrail markets these capabilities as a way to automate cinema operations and grow digital ticket sales and moviegoer engagement, and describes API-based integration between its platform and cinema point-of-sale systems, websites, and mobile apps. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from Oslo, Norway and Delaware, USA. Filmgrail does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

companies.name: Fox Corporation
companies.description: Fox Corporation is a U.S. media company whose portfolio includes Fox News Media, Fox Sports, Fox Entertainment, Fox Television Stations, and the ad-supported streaming service Tubi. Fox is a Fortune 500 consumer of cloud, AI, and media technology APIs (notably AWS as preferred AI cloud provider) but does not publish a public developer portal at the corporate level.

companies.name: Hawk-Eye Innovations
companies.description: Hawk-Eye Innovations is a Basingstoke, UK-headquartered sports technology company and part of the Sony Group, specializing in precision optical tracking, electronic officiating, video replay, and performance analytics across 25+ professional sports in 100+ countries. Founded in 2001 by Paul Hawkins and acquired by Sony in 2011, Hawk-Eye operates alongside Pulselive and Beyond Sports within Sony's sports division. The company is the standard for ball-tracking in tennis (Electronic Line Calling, now used in place of human line judges at the major tours), goal-line technology and semi-automated offside in football (Premier League, FIFA), video replay in cricket (DRS), NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, rugby, and PGA Tour shot-tracking. Core product platforms include SMART Replay, SMART Track, SMART Insight, HawkAR, iHawk, HawkREPLAY, HawkNEST, HawkVISION, SkeleTRACK, Electronic Line Calling, Goal Line Technology, Semi-Automated Offside Technology, and VAR systems. Revenue comes from long-term contracts with leagues, federations, and broadcasters; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hawk-Eye products. All integrations are bespoke and delivered through Sony Sports Business / Hawk-Eye operations teams.

companies.name: Headgum
companies.description: Headgum is an American comedy podcast network founded in 2015 by Marty Michael, Amir Blumenfeld, and Jake Hurwitz, with studios in Los Angeles and New York. It produces and distributes premium comedy and entertainment podcasts including Doughboys, Not Another D&D Podcast, Dead Eyes, Hey Riddle Riddle, and Why Won't You Date Me?, and operates Gumball, a host-read podcast and YouTube advertising marketplace that lets brands buy ads directly from creators. Headgum is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Headgum publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: Helion Energy
companies.description: Helion Energy is an Everett, Washington fusion power company building commercial fusion electricity generators using a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed configuration (FRC) approach burning deuterium and helium-3. Helion forms two FRC plasmas at opposite ends of its machine, accelerates them toward each other, merges them, and uses pulsed magnetic compression to drive them to fusion conditions; the expanding plasma pushes against the confining magnetic field and induces current directly back into the machine's capacitor bank via Faraday's Law, recapturing electricity without a steam cycle. Founded in 2013 by David Kirtley, John Slough, Chris Pihl, and George Votroubek, Helion is chaired by Sam Altman and has progressed through seven generations of prototypes (IPA, Venti, Trenta, and most recently Polaris) on its way to commercial generators. Polaris, brought online in late 2024, is the company's seventh-generation machine and the first privately developed fusion device to demonstrate measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, reaching 150 million degrees Celsius in February 2026. In May 2023, Helion signed the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement, committing to deliver 50 MWe to Microsoft starting in 2028, with the Orion plant planned for the Malaga, Washington area; a subsequent agreement with Nucor targets a 500-MWe facility. Helion is funded by Sam Altman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Nucor, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and others, with a reported $5.4B valuation as of early 2025. The company's revenue model is fusion electricity sales under long-term PPAs; Helion has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source software product, and its public GitHub organization (Helion-Energy) contains only forks of plasma-physics simulation tools (WarpX, FerroX, pyamrex, maestrowf).

companies.name: HiddenLayer
companies.description: HiddenLayer is an Austin, Texas-based AI security company founded in March 2022 by Chris Sestito (CEO), Tanner Burns (Chief Scientist), and Jim Ballard (CIO) — former Cylance researchers who encountered a real-world attack on production ML models. HiddenLayer builds an AI Security Platform that protects machine learning and generative AI systems across their entire lifecycle, comprising four integrated modules: AI Discovery (catalogs AI assets and eliminates shadow AI), AI Supply Chain Security (Model Scanner inspects models, weights, and pickle/RDS files for malicious payloads and backdoors), AI Attack Simulation (continuous adversarial red-teaming for agentic and generative systems), and AI Runtime Security / AIDR (a real-time detection-and-response firewall using deterministic classifiers that sit outside the model inference path to detect prompt injection, jailbreaks, indirect attacks, data leakage, and malicious tool calls in agentic and MCP systems). The platform exposes native connectors for CI/CD, MLOps, SIEM/SOAR, API gateways, and major data and cloud platforms, plus guardrail integrations for OpenAI Agents, LangChain, AWS Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework, Azure APIM, and a GitHub Action for Model Scanner. HiddenLayer publishes Python, TypeScript, and Java/Kotlin SDKs and research-grade tooling such as HiddenPickle (Python pickle disassembler/patcher) and HiddenPromise (R .rdx/.rdb/.rds disassembler). The company has raised $56M total ($50M Series A in September 2023 led by M12 / Microsoft's Venture Fund and Moore Strategic Ventures, with Booz Allen Ventures, IBM Ventures, Capital One Ventures, and Ten Eleven Ventures participating) and serves Fortune 500 enterprises, financial services, and US Federal agencies. The HiddenLayer SaaS console and REST API are gated behind enterprise sales and not publicly self-serve, placing this profile in Tier-3 (enterprise-gated) coverage.

companies.name: Humans
companies.description: humans& is a human-centric frontier AI lab founded in 2025 and publicly announced on January 20, 2026, building large-scale AI models centered on people and their relationships rather than raw autonomy. Its research spans long-horizon and multi-agent reinforcement learning, memory, and user understanding, tightly integrating science and product so that AI acts as connective tissue that strengthens organizations and communities. The founding team comes from frontier industry and academic labs including xAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, Reflection, AI2, Stanford, and MIT. Its seed round is led by SV Angel and co-founder Georges Harik, with investors including NVIDIA, GV (Google Ventures), Emerson Collective, Forerunner, S32, DCVC, and Jeff Bezos. As a pre-product research lab it publishes no public API yet; this profile captures its verified public identity surfaces.

companies.name: Iambic Therapeutics
companies.description: Iambic Therapeutics is a San Diego, California AI-driven drug discovery company founded in 2019 by Thomas Miller (CEO) and Fred Manby (CTO) that designs small-molecule therapeutics for oncology and other indications. Iambic builds proprietary AI models for drug discovery, including Enchant, a multimodal transformer that predicts clinical properties (pharmacokinetics, cellular and biochemical activity) of candidate molecules from early discovery data, and NeuralPLexer (now NeuralPLexer3), a flow-based generative model for protein-ligand complex structure prediction used to identify cryptic pockets and guide structure-based design. Both lines of work have been published at venues including NeurIPS 2025. The company's internal pipeline is oncology-led: IAM1363, a brain-penetrant selective HER2 / HER2-mutant inhibitor, completed Phase 1/1b dose escalation in 2025 and is in dose optimization with clinical activity reported at ESMO 2025; IAM-K1 (KIF18A) and IAM-C1 (CDK2/4) are preclinical, alongside undisclosed neurology, gastrointestinal, and inflammation discovery programs. In February 2026 Iambic announced a discovery and technology collaboration with Takeda worth up to ~$1.7B plus royalties, following a $100M+ private financing in November 2025 and total disclosed funding of approximately $334M. The company has been named to the CNBC Disruptor 50 list in 2025 and 2026 and has signaled intent to access public markets, including via a SPAC. Iambic's public GitHub footprint is limited to np-bench, a BSD-3 benchmark library for 3D biomolecular structure prediction; the underlying NeuralPLexer and Enchant models are proprietary and there is no public developer API, SDK, or commercial platform offering.

companies.name: IDEX Corporation
companies.description: IDEX Corporation (NYSE: IEX) is a global engineered products company that designs and manufactures pumps, flow meters, valves, fluidics systems, precision components, and fire and safety equipment. IDEX serves health, science, water, energy, semiconductor, aerospace, fire and safety, and industrial markets through three segments: Fluid and Metering Technologies, Health and Science Technologies, and Fire and Safety / Diversified Products.

companies.name: Imbue
companies.description: Imbue is a San Francisco AI research lab building agentic foundation models for reasoning and the human tooling around them, with a stated mission of AI that is loyal to its user. The team trains large reasoning models in-house (including a 70B model trained from scratch with open-sourced tooling and evaluation datasets) and publishes research on agent and reasoning architectures, reinforcement learning, data generation, and the scientific theory of deep learning. Imbue ships practical tools that emerge from the research, including Sculptor and mngr for orchestrating parallel coding agents, Bouncer for filtering social feeds, and Blueprint and Vet. There is no public commercial inference API; integration happens through open-sourced repositories, model artifacts on Hugging Face, and research releases.

companies.name: Insilico Medicine
companies.description: Insilico Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company applying generative AI and robotic automation to drug discovery and development. Its Pharma.AI software suite includes PandaOmics (target discovery from multi-omics data), Chemistry42 (generative chemistry with retrosynthesis, property prediction, and ADMET), Generative Biologics, inClinico (clinical trial outcome prediction), Science42 DORA (research assistant), Nach01, and PreciousGPT-family models for life sciences. The company runs its own therapeutic pipeline spanning oncology, fibrosis, and inflammation, with programs targeting TNIK, USP1, QPCTL, PHD, MAT2A, TEAD, ENPP1, KAT6 and others through Phase II. Insilico monetizes through Pharma.AI software licensing, partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies, and progression of its in-house assets. Pharma.AI tools are commercial SaaS products accessed via web UI; the company publishes open-source research code on GitHub (GENTRL, fcd_torch, BiAAE, DD-VAE, DORA) but does not expose a public commercial API.

companies.name: iPrice
companies.description: iPrice Group is a Southeast Asian e-commerce aggregator and price-comparison platform headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It aggregates billions of live product offers and thousands of coupons from more than a thousand retail partners, letting shoppers compare prices, discover deals, and make more informed purchases across seven markets: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Hong Kong. Backed by 500 Global as part of the Asia Venture Group portfolio, iPrice serves tens of millions of monthly visitors and is known for its large SEA e-commerce dataset. As of this profile, iPrice does not publish a public consumer or partner API, developer portal, or OpenAPI; this record is a company profile in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: J.C. Penney
companies.description: J.C. Penney Company, Inc. (JCPenney) is an American department store chain offering apparel, accessories, beauty, jewelry, footwear, and home goods. The company emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in late 2020 and continues to operate hundreds of department stores across the United States and Puerto Rico.

companies.name: Jumbo Privacy
companies.description: Jumbo (Jumbo Privacy) was a mobile-first consumer privacy and security assistant founded in 2019 by Pierre Valade, the co-founder of the Sunrise calendar app acquired by Microsoft. The iPhone/Android app helped everyday users take control of their online privacy by automatically hardening privacy settings across services like Google, Facebook, Twitter/X, Amazon, and LinkedIn, cleaning up old social posts, monitoring data breaches, and bundling identity-theft insurance. It was explicitly designed to process user data locally on-device with no server-side processing, so it never exposed a public developer API, SDK, or documented integration surface. Jumbo was backed by investors including Balderton Capital and Thrive Capital before being acqui-hired by cyber-insurer Coalition in 2023; the standalone consumer app was wound down and fully discontinued by 2024. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record - there is no active API to enrich.

companies.name: Kyndryl
companies.description: Kyndryl is a Fortune 500 IT infrastructure services company spun off from IBM in 2021. The company designs, builds, manages, and modernizes mission-critical technology systems across cloud, mainframe, networking, digital workplace, security, applications, data, and AI. Kyndryl operates the Kyndryl Bridge integration and observability platform, runs the Kyndryl Vital design studios, and partners with hyperscalers including AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and SAP. No public developer API has been documented.

companies.name: Leidos
companies.description: Leidos, a Fortune 500 digital and mission innovator, delivers solutions at the intersection of national security, health, and critical infrastructure. With a global workforce of approximately 47,000, the company is executing its NorthStar 2030 strategy focused on five growth engines: space and maritime, energy infrastructure, digital modernization and cyber, mission software, and managed health. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified.

companies.name: Magic
companies.description: Magic (magic.dev) is a San Francisco frontier AI research lab building frontier-scale code models - an "AI coworker" for software engineering, and ultimately a path to safe AGI - rather than a shipping developer product. It has raised roughly $515M from Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, CapitalG, Elad Gil, Sequoia, Jane Street, and Eric Schmidt, and has published research on ultra-long-context models (LTM-1 at a 5M token context window, and the unreleased LTM-2-mini research prototype claimed to handle up to 100M tokens). As of this review Magic does not publish a public, self-serve developer API, API reference, SDK, or waitlist; its website and careers pages describe mission, research, and open roles only, with no product access model, pricing, or documented endpoints. Its GitHub organization (magicproduct) hosts research tooling (e.g. hash-hop, a long-context evaluation harness) and infrastructure forks, not an API client or SDK.

companies.name: Monell Chemical Senses Center
companies.description: The Monell Chemical Senses Center is "the world's only independent, non-profit scientific institute dedicated to interdisciplinary basic research on the senses of taste and smell." Founded in 1968 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Monell conducts chemosensory research organized around three strategic themes: Healthy Senses and Happy Lives, Senses for a Thriving Planet, and Nourishing Our Future. The center runs postdoctoral training, the Dr. Charis Eng Monell Science Apprenticeship Program, the Monell Science Entrepreneurship Program, an Academic Partnership Program, and the Monell Insiders corporate partnership program. Monell does not publish a public developer API surface; its "product" is knowledge disseminated through scholarly publications and conferences.

companies.name: Moxion Power
companies.description: Moxion Power was a Richmond, California-based mobile battery energy storage (BESS) company founded in 2020 that designed, manufactured, and deployed large-scale mobile lithium-iron-phosphate battery units (the MP-75 and related platforms) intended to displace diesel generators across construction sites, film and television production, live events, utility work, and emergency response. The company built a 40,000 square-foot factory in Richmond, raised approximately $100 million in a Series B at a reported $1.5 billion valuation led by Tamarack Global with participation from Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund and Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, and signed a multi-year fleet partnership with Sunbelt Rentals. After delivering 400+ units it announced cessation of operations on July 29, 2024, laid off its entire workforce, and filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware in August 2024 with approximately $201,980 in cash on hand and estimated liabilities of $100M–$500M. In September–October 2024, Viridi Parente acquired Moxion's Richmond facility, battery inventory, intellectual property, patents, and the Sunbelt Rentals relationship through the bankruptcy auction for approximately $7 million. Moxion Power had no public developer API, SDK, or open source release; its GitHub organization (github.com/moxion-power) contains zero public repositories. This profile is preserved for historical reference.

companies.name: Muro AI
companies.description: Muro AI is an early-stage construction-technology startup building PrecOS, a pre-construction operating system marketed as a pre-con manager's AI assistant that carries general contractors from scoping through handover. The platform applies domain-adapted large language models, image models, agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, and document/plan parsing (OCR and computer vision) to automate bid comparison, estimation, bill-of-materials, and budget updates for teams that still run on spreadsheets. Muro is backed by Techstars and integrates with industry tools such as Procore. As of this profiling the company publishes a marketing site, a blog, and careers pages, but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so this record captures identity and a domain-security probe rather than an API surface.

companies.name: National Institute of Food and Agriculture
companies.description: The National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) provides leadership and funding for programs that advance agriculture-related sciences. NIFA invests in and supports initiatives that ensure the long-term viability of agriculture, partnering with land-grant universities and the broader agricultural research community.

companies.name: Nestlé
companies.description: Nestlé S.A. is the world's largest food and beverage company by revenue, headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland. Its product portfolio spans coffee (Nescafé, Nespresso), water, pet food (Purina), baby and infant nutrition (Gerber, Cerelac), confectionery (KitKat), dairy, and health science. No public developer portal or external API offering has been identified for Nestlé; integrations with retailers and partners are handled through private B2B systems rather than a self-serve developer program.

companies.name: Operand
companies.description: Operand is an AI-enabled pricing and commercial strategy platform for consumer retail, founded in 2024 and backed by Felicis, Y Combinator, SV Angel, and Soma Capital. It applies proprietary AI systems — an autonomous "agent swarm" — to set pricing and promotion strategy for mid-market and enterprise brands and retailers managing thousands of SKUs, volatile demand, and thin margins, running simulations to benchmark margin, revenue, and inventory-turn objectives before automating price changes. Operand is delivered as a managed platform with expert support and request-a-quote pricing rather than a public developer API; it currently publishes no OpenAPI, developer portal, or self-serve SDKs. An earlier Operand product at operand.ai offered an embeddings / semantic-search API with Python, Go, and TypeScript SDKs, now discontinued.

companies.name: Pachama
companies.description: Pachama is a San Francisco–based climate technology company founded in 2018 that built a satellite- and machine-learning-powered platform for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of nature-based carbon projects — including forest conservation, reforestation, afforestation, and improved forest management. Pachama combined satellite imagery, LiDAR, remote sensing, and deep-learning models to measure aboveground biomass, detect deforestation, and track project performance against verified baselines, surfacing that intelligence through an online marketplace where corporate buyers (including Microsoft, Shopify, Salesforce, Flexport.org, Mercado Libre, Boom Supersonic, and Nespresso) could discover and purchase high-integrity carbon credits. In November 2025, Pachama was acquired by Carbon Direct, and its proprietary digital MRV platform and forest-carbon science team were folded into Carbon Direct's science-backed carbon management offering; pachama.com now redirects to carbon-direct.com. Throughout its life as an independent company Pachama operated a buyer marketplace and discussed plans for a partner API to embed project selection and retirement data into third-party products, but never shipped a public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification — its GitHub organization contains only forks and archived internal tooling.

companies.name: Physical Intelligence
companies.description: Physical Intelligence (often styled "Pi" or "π") is a San Francisco-based research company building general-purpose foundation models for robotics with the stated goal of producing learning algorithms that can control any robot to do any task. The company has published a continuing line of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: π0 (October 2024, first generalist multi-task multi-robot policy), π0-FAST (autoregressive variant via Real-time Action Chunking / FAST tokenization), π0.5 (April 2025, open-world generalization), π*0.6 (November 2025, reinforcement-learning from experience), and π0.7 (April 2026, steerable model with emergent capabilities). Physical Intelligence releases significant work as open source: the openpi repository (~12K stars) is the canonical home for π0 weights and code, with companion repos including real-time-chunking-kinetix, pi-data-sharing, aloha, augmax, and rlds_dataset_builder. The company does not yet offer a hosted commercial API; access to the platform is via open-weight models and research collaborations.

companies.name: Pony.ai
companies.description: Pony.ai is a global autonomous-mobility company founded in Silicon Valley in 2016 and dual-headquartered in Guangzhou and Fremont. Its core technology is the Pony "virtual driver", a Level 4 autonomous driving stack deployed across three business lines: Robotaxi (PonyPilot+ ride-hailing service operating in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen, plus pilots in California and Arizona), Robotruck (autonomous heavy-duty trucking in China), and Personally Owned Vehicle (POV) intelligent driving software for production passenger cars. The company is publicly listed on NASDAQ under PONY and reports more than 32 million kilometres of autonomous road testing. Pony.ai does not publish a traditional public developer API; its public GitHub presence includes infrastructure tooling such as pony_aim (experiment tracker) and bazel-buildfarm rather than the AV stack itself. This profile captures the company surface and any developer-relevant artifacts.

companies.name: Props
companies.description: Props (Props Project, operated by Props PBC / Open Props, founded by YouNow's Adi Sideman) was a blockchain-based loyalty and rewards network that let consumer apps grant users a shared crypto token (the Props Token) as a stake in the networks they helped grow. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Borderless Capital, Venrock and Comcast Ventures, it raised ~$2M and was the first Regulation A+ consumer token qualified by the SEC, reaching over three million users across its app network. In August 2021 the team announced it would wind down commercial operations at year end, citing the regulatory constraints of running a qualified security, and open-sourced the Props Protocol contracts on GitHub. The propsproject.com domain no longer resolves; there is no live developer portal, API, documentation, or maintained SDK. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record.

companies.name: Protocol Labs
companies.description: Protocol Labs is an open-source research and development company founded in 2014 by Juan Benet, best known for creating foundational decentralized web protocols including IPFS (the InterPlanetary File System), Filecoin (a decentralized storage network), libp2p (a modular peer-to-peer networking stack), and IPLD (a data model for content-addressed systems). Since its founding it has grown into an innovation network connecting more than 750 startups, funds, accelerators, foundations, and open-source projects working across web3, AI, robotics, cryptography, and neurotechnology. Protocol Labs itself (protocol.ai) is a research and venture organization rather than a commercial API provider — it publishes no first-party REST API; its developer surfaces (IPFS HTTP APIs, Filecoin JSON-RPC, libp2p) live in their own separate open-source projects and GitHub organizations.

companies.name: Qphox
companies.description: QphoX is a Delft, Netherlands-based quantum technology company founded in 2021 and spun out of Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). It develops quantum networking hardware to tackle the scaling challenges of quantum computing, centered on its Quantum Transducer, described as the first quantum interface between single optical and single microwave photons, enabling optical interconnects between superconducting quantum processors. Alongside the transducer, QphoX offers an Optical Control System for delivering RF signals into extreme cryogenic environments and a CryoSwitch Control Module for use with Radiall's cryogenic latching actuator. The company publishes open-source Python instrument-control libraries (QCoDeS drivers) on GitHub for operating its hardware. QphoX is backed by Speedinvest. QphoX exposes no public web API or developer portal.

companies.name: Realtor.com
companies.description: Realtor.com is a real estate listings website operated by Move, Inc., a subsidiary of News Corp, headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The platform is the official site of the National Association of REALTORS (NAR) under a long-term operating agreement and is one of the largest U.S. property search portals, serving home buyers, sellers, renters, and real estate professionals. Realtor.com aggregates for-sale, for-rent, and off-market listings sourced primarily from Multiple Listing Services (MLSs) via Move's listings distribution subsidiary ListHub, and surfaces them through consumer web and mobile apps alongside neighborhood, school, mortgage, and market data. The professional side of the business sells lead-generation and marketing products such as Connections Plus, ReadyConnect Concierge, and Market VIP to agents and brokers, while ListHub provides MLS-to-portal syndication, broker reporting, and listing feed management. Adjacent Move properties include Doorsteps, Moving.com, and SeniorHousingNet, and the company publishes a public economic research arm at realtor.com/research that releases monthly housing market reports and downloadable historical datasets. Realtor.com does not publish a first-party public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; programmatic access to listing data is gated through MLS membership and ListHub's broker/vendor agreements, while the only widely available HTTP APIs branded as Realtor.com are unofficial third-party scrapers hosted on RapidAPI and Apify.

companies.name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals
companies.description: Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) is a Salt Lake City-based AI-enabled drug discovery company that operates the Recursion Operating System (Recursion OS), a vertically integrated platform combining automated wet-lab cellular phenomics, transcriptomics (Trekseq), proteomics, ADME, chemistry, and patient data with machine learning to map biology and design drug candidates. The platform runs on BioHive-2, a NVIDIA-built supercomputer ranked among the top global systems and dedicated to biopharma workloads, and is fed by 50+ petabytes of proprietary biological and chemical data. In November 2024 Recursion completed the acquisition of Exscientia, folding Exscientia's generative AI chemistry, Centaur Chemist, and clinical pipeline into the combined company; Recursion now runs more than 10 clinical and preclinical programs (REC-4881 for FAP, REC-3565 MALT1 inhibitor, REC-1245 RBM39 for biomarker-enriched solid tumors and lymphomas, REC-617 CDK7 inhibitor, REC-994 for cerebral cavernous malformation, REC-2282 for NF2- mutated meningiomas, REC-4209 for IPF, REC-7735 for HSD obesity), 10+ advanced discovery programs, and 10+ partnered programs across Roche (Genentech), Bayer, Sanofi, and Merck KGaA (Darmstadt). Recursion does not currently expose paid commercial APIs to external developers; assets and data access are delivered through licensing, scientific collaborations, and the MapApp web product. Externally, Recursion ships substantial open tooling: the RxRx family of open phenomics datasets (RxRx1, RxRx2, RxRx3, RxRx3-core, RxRx19a, RxRx19b) hosted at rxrx.ai and Hugging Face, the OpenPhenom-S/16 foundation model (released on Hugging Face and Google Cloud's Model Garden, with Phenom-Beta on NVIDIA BioNeMo), the MolE molecular foundation model, the gflownet library for graph and molecular generative modeling, SynFlowNet/synflownet-boltz for retrosynthesis-aware molecular design, maes_microscopy (NeurIPS 2023 spotlight masked autoencoders for cell microscopy), and rxrx1-utils for the NeurIPS 2019 CellSignal competition. The combination positions Recursion as a Tier-2 AI drug discovery provider with no commercial API surface but a meaningful open-source and open-model presence aimed at the computational biology research community.

companies.name: Reniac
companies.description: rENIAC Inc. is a Santa Clara-based data acceleration company whose flagship product, the rENIAC Data Engine (rDE), is a drop-in accelerator for open source and NoSQL databases such as Apache Cassandra. Combining FPGAs with proprietary software, rDE speeds storage, network, and compute operations and can be deployed as a hardware-optimized cache, a transparent data-acceleration proxy, or a scalable storage engine on-prem, hybrid, or in the cloud (including early availability on AWS). rENIAC targets ultra-low-latency, real-time workloads — AI/ML, fraud prevention, payment processing, electronic trading, and recommendation engines — claiming up to 10x throughput, 13x lower latency, and significant TCO and CPU reductions. rENIAC ships an infrastructure/hardware acceleration product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe.

companies.name: Sportlogiq
companies.description: Sportlogiq is a Montreal, Quebec-based sports analytics company that applies patented computer vision and machine learning to broadcast video to generate high-resolution player tracking, event, and performance datasets across ice hockey, soccer/global football, American football, and youth sports. Founded in 2015 by Olympic figure skater Craig Buntin and computer-vision PhD Mehrsan Javan, the company is led by CEO Mitchell Wasserman and employs roughly 75 people, including a research team of ~13 AI scientists with 180+ patents and publications. Sportlogiq describes itself as the global leader in hockey analytics, with adoption across the majority of NHL franchises, 150+ professional and amateur hockey clubs worldwide, international hockey federations and leagues (SHL, PWHL, IIHF), NCAA hockey programs, NFL franchises, and global football organizations — collectively serving 220+ clients. In November 2024 Sportlogiq acquired 8BY8, a sports video infrastructure platform that combines multi-angle video, data streams, and audio for officiating, coaching, and player health workflows. In January 2026 Sportlogiq was itself acquired by Teamworks, where it continues to operate as the AI analytics layer of Teamworks' broader operating system for sport. Sportlogiq exposes its tracking and event data to teams, leagues, broadcasters, and analytics partners through a private partner API and bulk data feeds; there is no public developer portal, no self-service signup, no published OpenAPI specification, and no public SDKs or open-source repositories. Access is sold as part of commercial contracts and integrated directly into partner workflows.

companies.name: TerraPower
companies.description: TerraPower is a Bellevue, Washington-based advanced nuclear innovation company founded in 2006 with Bill Gates as founder and chair. Its flagship product is the Natrium reactor, a 345 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor co-developed with GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy and paired with an integrated molten salt energy storage system that can boost output to 500 MWe for up to five-plus hours to follow renewable grid load. TerraPower broke ground in 2024 on the first commercial Natrium demonstration plant in Kemmerer, Wyoming under the U.S. Department of Energy's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP), a 50/50 cost-share with up to $2 billion in federal funding. The company's second business line, TerraPower Isotopes (TPI), produces research-grade actinium-225 — an alpha-emitting radionuclide used in targeted alpha therapy for cancer — from DOE thorium-229 stockpiles in partnership with Isotek, with a lab in Everett WA and a cGMP manufacturing facility under construction in Philadelphia's Bellwether District. TerraPower has no commercial developer API, SDK, or public partner integration platform; its revenue model is reactor sales, plant operation, and isotope supply contracts with pharmaceutical partners including Aktis Oncology, Advanced Accelerator Applications, Cardinal Health, and Point Biopharma. The company does maintain a meaningful open-source nuclear engineering footprint on GitHub — most notably ARMI (Advanced Reactor Modeling Interface), an Apache 2.0 Python framework for nuclear reactor design and analysis automation used internally to design Natrium and made available to the wider reactor engineering community.

companies.name: Traverse
companies.description: Traverse is a San Francisco data research lab, founded in 2025 by Lance Yan and backed by Y Combinator (W26) along with angel investors from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and Meta. Traverse partners with frontier AI labs to solve "non-verifiable" work: the ambiguous, taste-dependent, long-horizon tasks in domains like law, healthcare, sales, and writing where reinforcement learning lacks the clean deterministic feedback loops it has in math and coding. The lab captures real human expert behavior in highly controlled settings and turns judgment, taste, and reasoning into high-fidelity training environments for frontier models. As of mid-2026 Traverse is an early-stage research lab with no public API, developer platform, SDKs, or product documentation — its public surface is a manifesto-style website, a blog, careers pages, and a contact CTA for prospective lab partners.

companies.name: Trella
companies.description: Trella is a Cairo-headquartered B2B trucking marketplace and digital freight platform that connects shippers with carriers across the Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan (MENA-P). Founded in 2019 by Omar Hagrass, Ali El Atrash, and Pierre Saad and backed by Y Combinator, Trella runs a digital load marketplace, a carrier mobile app, and a shipper web dashboard that together replace the traditional broker-driven, paper-based long-haul trucking workflow. Core platform services include load posting and carrier matching, instant quoting, GPS tracking and live shipment visibility, electronic proof of delivery (ePODs), load insurance, a control-tower operations layer for carrier quality and performance, and integrated payments and invoicing between shippers and carriers. The network spans 30,000+ carriers and operates from major freight hubs including Cairo, Alexandria, Port Said, Damietta, Sokhna, Jeddah, Dammam, Riyadh, and Dubai, serving industries such as FMCG, construction, manufacturing, agriculture, mining, e-commerce, retail, electronics, ceramics, and freight forwarding. Trella's revenue model is marketplace take-rate and value-added logistics services; there is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks catalog, or open-source platform release for the Trella marketplace.

companies.name: Triblio
companies.description: Triblio is an account-based marketing (ABM) platform now owned by Foundry, the marketing services and data unit of International Data Group (IDG). Originally founded in Reston, Virginia, Triblio was acquired by IDG/Foundry in June 2020 as the cornerstone of a multi-year strategy to combine first- party publisher data, third-party intent signals, and ABM advertising, web personalization, and sales acceleration into a single platform. The product combines account-based advertising, intent-driven audience segmentation, website personalization, and a Smart Score that ranks accounts using behavioral signals from first-party web visits, third-party intent providers (notably Bombora Company Surge and G2 intent), CRM data, and Foundry's own publisher network. Triblio integrates with major CRMs and marketing automation systems including Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics 365, SugarCRM, Marketo, Pardot, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Analytics, and Slack. Foundry positions Triblio as the engine behind its broader Sales Acceleration and Foundry ABM offerings, with intent data feeds from Bombora ingested weekly and G2 intent ingested nightly. Triblio does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI specification, or open-source SDKs; the GitHub organization at github.com/triblio was archived in January 2026 with no public repos. Customer integrations are delivered through pre-built CRM and MAP connectors, an Apps Marketplace, and platform-internal automation rather than a self-serve developer API.

Wing also co-founded the InterUSS Platform open-source UTM project, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. Wing's revenue comes from per-delivery fees charged to merchant partners and from drone-as-a-service operations rather than from public developer APIs; the Delivery Platform API and OpenSky API are not openly published and there is no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at the time of profiling.

companies.description: CTRL Therapeutics (cTRL Tx) is a Chicago-based preclinical biotechnology company developing next-generation cell therapies for solid tumors. companies.name: Mantis
companies.description: Mantis (Mantis Biotech) builds predictive digital twins of individual people, aggregating personal data streams — wearables, digital activity, and clinical records — into high-fidelity models by combining large language models with physics-based simulation. The company positions itself as a neutral intermediary for personal predictive models — an "OAuth for identity" or "Plaid for banking" layer — letting individuals grant scoped, revocable access to their twin to healthcare providers and third-party builders. Applications include pre-symptomatic infection detection, cognitive baseline monitoring, heart-failure decompensation forecasting, medication-adherence prediction, post-operative recovery trajectories, psychiatric relapse early warning, and running trials on twins. Mantis is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company; as of this profile it publishes a marketing site and manifesto but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Manulife Bank
companies.description: Manulife Bank of Canada is a Schedule I federally chartered bank and a wholly-owned subsidiary of The Manufacturers Life Insurance Company, part of Manulife Financial Corporation. Launched in 1993 as Canada's first branchless (direct) bank — and the first federally regulated bank opened by an insurance company in Canada — it operates entirely through online banking, a mobile app, and telephone banking, with no physical branches. It is best known for the Manulife One all-in-one account, the Advantage Account, GICs, mortgages, and lines of credit that connect everyday banking and borrowing with long-term financial planning. Manulife Bank publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; no developer.manulifebank.ca host resolves, and the public site is bot-protected. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework — legislated in Budget 2024 and the Fall Economic Statement 2024, with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer — is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer financial data access today is voluntary and occurs through financial-data aggregators (Plaid, Flinks, MX) rather than a first-party bank API. Interac e-Transfer is offered as a consumer feature but is not exposed as a documented public API.

companies.name: Mountain America Credit Union

companies.description: Nia Health GmbH is a Berlin-based digital health company and spin-off of Charité Universitätsmedizin Berlin that develops Nia, a mobile medical application supporting people living with atopic dermatitis (neurodermatitis) and other chronic skin conditions. Nia was the first atopic dermatitis app approved as a medical device, helping patients document flare-ups, identify triggers such as stress or fragrances, and manage their therapy day to day. companies.description: Nilo Therapeutics is a New York-based, preclinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering a differentiated approach to immunomodulation by targeting the neural circuits that regulate systemic inflammation. Building on seminal discoveries from the laboratories of Charles Zuker (Columbia University / HHMI), Ruslan Medzhitov (Yale), and Stephen Liberles (Harvard) that identified vagal neurons regulating systemic immune activation, and led by CEO Kim Seth, the company harnesses the body-brain axis to restore immune homeostasis centrally, moving beyond conventional immunosuppression to treat autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Nilo launched in 2025 with a $101M Series A co-led by DCVC Bio, Lux Capital, and The Column Group, with participation from Alexandria Venture Investments and the Gates Foundation. As a therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

companies.name: Nocion Therapeutics
companies.description: Nocion Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company discovering and developing a novel class of biologically selective charged sodium channel (NaV) blockers designed to selectively silence overactive sensory neurons to relieve chronic cough, pain, itch, and inflammation. Its lead candidate, inhaled taplucainium, is a first-in-class therapy in a Phase 2b (ASPIRE) trial for refractory and unexplained chronic cough, with topline results expected in 2026. Founded on foundational intellectual property licensed from Harvard University and Boston Children's Hospital and backed by Canaan Partners, F-Prime Capital, and other life-sciences investors, Nocion is a therapeutics R&D company with no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Noon
companies.description: Noon is a Dubai-headquartered e-commerce marketplace and digital ecosystem launched in 2017 as a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Emirati businessman Mohamed Alabbar. Frequently described as the Amazon of the MENA region, Noon operates as the leading online shopping destination across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Egypt, offering electronics, mobiles, fashion, beauty, home, appliances, baby, and grocery categories through a hybrid first-party and third-party seller marketplace. Beyond the core marketplace, Noon has expanded into a lifestyle super-app spanning Noon Food (quick-service restaurant delivery competing with Talabat and Deliveroo), Noon Daily (next-day grocery delivery), Noon Minutes (15-minute instant grocery and essentials delivery), Noon Pay and the Noon mobile wallet (QR payments, bill pay, and a co-branded credit card), Noon VIP (loyalty/subscription), NowNow (on-demand delivery in KSA), and SIVVI (acquired regional fashion brand). Noon operates its own last-mile logistics arm and warehouses across the region, and provides a Fulfilled by Partner Integration (FBPI) program with commercial APIs that allow third-party sellers and channel-integration partners (ChannelEngine, Unicommerce, Vinculum, Ecom Energize and others) to programmatically publish catalog, sync inventory, and manage shipments. These APIs are gated to onboarded sellers and certified integrators inside the noon.partners environment — there is no general public developer portal, no published OpenAPI specification, and no Noon-maintained SDKs, CLIs, or open-source repositories.

companies.name: Ohio National (Acquired by Constellation Insurance / Rebranded as AuguStar)
companies.description: Ohio National Financial Services was a Cincinnati-based mutual life insurance and annuities provider, historically operating through Ohio National Mutual Holdings, Inc. (ONMH). In March 2021 Constellation Insurance Holdings announced a sponsored demutualization of ONMH and Ohio National Financial Services for total consideration of approximately US$1 billion, including member consideration and new capital. The transaction closed on March 31, 2022, after a member vote on March 11, 2022, converting ONMH to a stock company renamed Ohio National Holdings, Inc. On July 17, 2023 Constellation repositioned and rebranded Ohio National's life insurance business as AuguStar Life, with the Ohio National Life Insurance Company and Ohio National Life Assurance Corporation expected to change their names to AuguStar Life Insurance Company and AuguStar Life Assurance Corporation in Q4 2023. Its platform combines a spatial genomics pipeline that maps gene expression while preserving tissue architecture, tissue phenotyping that grounds molecular findings in histology and protein measurements, and functional response testing that runs ex vivo drug and perturbation experiments on precision-cut tumor slices. On top of this proprietary sequencing and spatial-transcriptomics data the company trains multimodal AI models for therapeutic target discovery, treatment-response prediction, and patient stratification. Origin Bio is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company. As of this profile the company publishes no public-facing API, developer documentation, or SDKs; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

companies.name: VyStar Credit Union
companies.description: VyStar Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida. Founded in 1952 as Jax Navy Federal Credit Union to serve military members at Naval Air Station Jacksonville and renamed VyStar in 2002, it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly $14 billion in assets, more than 950,000 members, and approximately 80 branches across Florida and Georgia. It is state-chartered and federally insured by the NCUA. Like most US credit unions, VyStar publishes no public, first-party developer API program: there is no live developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definition, and no documented first-party data-access API. Consumer-permissioned account data is shared with third parties through financial-data aggregators rather than a documented open API, and the United States has no single mandated open-banking contract. VyStar's open-finance posture is therefore aggregator-mediated, with the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule as the relevant regulatory horizon.

The company operates a hybrid business model with a co-development partner network (40+ partners and 100+ antibody drug programs since 2015) alongside a growing wholly-owned pipeline that includes ABCL635 (non-hormonal vasomotor symptoms), ABCL575 (atopic dermatitis), ABCL688 (autoimmunity), and ABCL386 (oncology), plus 20+ discovery programs. AbCellera does not publish a public API or developer portal; capabilities are delivered through partner collaborations and contract terms.

companies.name: AdaptHealth
companies.description: AdaptHealth is a national provider of home medical equipment, supplies, and related services in the United States. The company supports patients with sleep therapy, respiratory care, diabetes care, mobility, and other home medical needs through a network of locations and partnerships with healthcare providers and insurers. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

companies.name: AICE
companies.description: AICE is a defense-technology company building the next generation of underwater defense systems: autonomous swarms of modular marine drones that secure naval assets and coastal infrastructure against evolving underwater threats. Founded in 2026 by former NASA engineer Gregoire Chomette and European Robotics Champion Remi Bouteiller, the company is part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area with hardware manufactured in France, and applies swarm robotics and AI to surveillance, detection, and protection of critical subsea infrastructure. AICE currently ships hardware and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Airbrite
companies.description: Airbrite was an early commerce-infrastructure startup (a16z portfolio) that offered a hosted order-management and payments/commerce backend API for merchants and developers, with JavaScript and Python client SDKs and an embeddable checkout. The product was later rebranded and pivoted to "Celery" (pre-order / crowdfunding commerce). Airbrite is now defunct: its primary developer domains (airbrite.io, getairbrite.com) no longer resolve and airbrite.com is a parked domain, so there is no live developer portal, API reference, or hosted API to enrich. What remains verifiable is the public github.com/airbrite organization and the client libraries still published on npm and PyPI. This profile records that residual, evidence-backed surface; most enrichment artifact types are legitimately empty because the provider no longer operates.

companies.name: Alien Labs
companies.description: Alien Labs, Inc. was a San Francisco software startup founded by Cristian Strat, Mircea Pasoi and Liana Dumitru, and a seed-stage portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Under the Alien Labs banner the team shipped Summify, a social news digest acquired by Twitter in January 2012, and later Memo — "the wiki that's always up-to-date" — a Slack-native team knowledge base that let 8,000+ teams star a Slack message to save it as a searchable note, edit rich-text and code-block documents in context, and retrieve them with a /memo-find slash command. Memo stopped accepting new signups on January 16, 2018 and shut down on March 16, 2018; most of the engineering team joined Coinbase. The company operates no live developer portal, documentation, or public API today, and this profile is retained as a historical network record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: Altera
companies.description: Altera is an applied AI research company founded in December 2023 by former MIT computational neuroscientist Robert Yang, building "digital human beings" — autonomous, collaborative, and socially intelligent AI agents. Its research began with multi-agent experiments in games such as Minecraft and Roblox (agents that can play alongside a person like a friend), and produced Project Sid, a large-scale AI-agent civilization powered by its PIANO architecture. The team is drawn from MIT EECS, the Stanford NLP Group, Google X, and Citadel. Altera raised a $2M pre-seed and a $9M seed (backers include a16z SPEEDRUN, Patron, First Spark Ventures, and Eric Schmidt) and has since rebranded to Fundamental Research Labs following a $33M Series A led by Prosus. Altera is a research organization and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; its only public developer surface is the altera-al GitHub organization (the project-sid research codebase).

companies.name: Applica
companies.description: Applica was an AI-based document understanding and text automation company founded in Warsaw, Poland, built on deep-learning research in natural language processing for unstructured documents. Its platform read, interpreted, and extracted information from documents such as invoices, contracts, insurance claims, legal documents, and financial filings across the finance, insurance, legal, and media industries. Applica went through the Barclays Accelerator powered by Techstars and raised a Series A led by Cogito Capital Partners in 2020. Snowflake announced its intent to acquire Applica in August 2022 and absorbed the technology into the Snowflake platform. Applica no longer operates as an independent product or API provider, and applica.ai is no longer a live developer surface; this profile is retained for historical/network provenance.

Aquantia was acquired by Marvell Technology in 2019; the aquantia.com domain now redirects to marvell.com. It operated no public HTTP/developer API or developer portal — its published developer surface is silicon: Linux kernel and DPDK "Atlantic" NIC drivers, firmware, and tooling in the github.com/Aquantia organization. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead stub; there is no API to enrich.

companies.name: Atom Computing
companies.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

companies.name: Atomwise
companies.description: Atomwise pioneered the use of deep convolutional neural networks for structure-based drug discovery, with its AtomNet platform applying AI to virtual screening of small molecules against protein targets. The company ran the Artificial Intelligence Molecular Screen (AIMS) academic collaboration program, partnered with biotech and pharma companies on discovery contracts, and built an internal pipeline of small-molecule programs. As of 2026, atomwise.com redirects to Numerion Labs (numerionlabs.ai), reflecting an apparent rebrand or successor entity that positions itself as an AI superplatform exploring drug-like chemical space with programs in immune and inflammatory diseases. Atomwise never exposed a public commercial API; AtomNet screening was delivered to partners as a service. The legacy GitHub organization (github.com/atomwise) hosts no public repositories.

companies.name: Automatic
companies.description: Automatic (Automatic Labs, Inc.) was a San Francisco connected-car company founded in 2011 by Thejo Kote and Jerry Jariyasunant. Its OBD-II adapter and companion mobile app turned almost any car built since 1996 into a connected car, adding trip logging, fuel and MPG tracking, engine-light diagnostics, parking recall, and automatic crash alerts. Automatic ran a public developer platform at developer.automatic.com built around three surfaces: a REST API exposing trip, user, and vehicle data; an Events API delivering real-time driving events such as ignition on/off, hard braking, acceleration, speeding, and location changes over webhooks and websockets; and a private-beta Streaming SDK that read raw OBD-II data from the second-generation adapter over Bluetooth. SiriusXM acquired the company on 2017-04-27 for approximately $115 million, and all operations were shut down on 2020-05-28. THIS COMPANY IS DEFUNCT — no API, developer portal, or documentation remains online, and the automatic.com domain now belongs to the unrelated company Automattic. This profile is retained as a historical record of a notable connected-car API platform.

companies.name: Axionorbital Space
companies.description: AxionOrbital Space is a San Francisco Bay Area startup (Y Combinator Winter 2026) building foundation models for continuous Earth observation through clouds and darkness. Its flagship model, ORION, converts Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into high-resolution, photorealistic optical imagery in real time using deterministic one-step diffusion, overcoming the limitation that traditional optical satellites are unusable roughly 70% of the time due to weather and night cycles. The technology targets 24/7 situational awareness for defense and intelligence, commodities and financial analytics, disaster response, agriculture, and climate monitoring. Founded in 2025 by Dhenenjay Yadav (CEO, former ISRO ML engineer) and Atharva Peshkar (CTO, PhD, CU Boulder / Harvard VCG). At the time of profiling the company is pre-product with no public API, developer portal, or specifications published; this record captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: BBDO Worldwide
companies.description: BBDO Worldwide is a global advertising agency network founded in 1928 and headquartered in New York City. It is the largest of the creative-agency networks owned by Omnicom Group, with roughly 15,000 employees across approximately 289 offices in 81 countries (per Wikipedia, citing company data). The agency's positioning is "Do Big Things," and its public work is campaign-led — Pepsi, Budweiser, McDonald's, M&M's, Snickers, Visa, AT&T Business, Volkswagen, Skoda, Whiskas, and many more. BBDO has been named Cannes Lions Network of the Year multiple times since 2007 and Network of the Decade in 2020. BBDO does not publish a developer portal, public REST APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, status page, or pricing — its product is creative work delivered to brand clients, not software offered to developers. This repository indexes the public properties (homepage, network site, news, parent company, GitHub org, and notable agency network members) so the API Evangelist network can track the absence of a developer surface and link BBDO to its parent Omnicom and sibling networks (DDB Worldwide, TBWA Worldwide).

companies.name: Beme
companies.description: Beme Inc. (stylized "beme") was an American multimedia company founded in 2014 in New York City by YouTube filmmaker Casey Neistat and engineer Matt Hackett. Its mobile app, released on iOS in July 2015 and on Android in May 2016, let users capture and instantly share unedited two-to-eight-second videos without previewing or editing them, aiming at a more authentic alternative to curated social video. Beme raised a seed round backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Vayner/RSE, and CNN acquired the company in November 2016 in a deal reported at $25 million. The consumer app was shut down on January 31, 2017, and on January 25, 2018 the founders departed and Beme was folded into CNN Digital Studios. The company is defunct. Beme never published a public API, developer portal, or API documentation; its only public technical artifact is an open-source Go testing utility. The beme.com domain has since changed hands and now redirects to an unrelated company.

companies.name: Bidgely
companies.description: Bidgely is a Mountain View, California energy analytics company that builds AI software for electric and gas utilities. Its flagship platform, UtilityAI, applies patented non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) and disaggregation techniques to smart meter interval data to infer appliance-level energy usage — air conditioning, heat pumps, electric vehicles, pool pumps, water heaters and more — from the whole-home meter signal alone, without surveys, sub-meters, or smart plugs. The platform layers GenAI natural-language interfaces and Agentic AI workflows on top of disaggregation to support utility programs across demand-side management, customer engagement and high-bill alerts, load flexibility and time-of-use, electrification (EV and heat pump targeting), grid resiliency and DER planning, affordability and income-qualified outreach, gas efficiency, small and mid-sized business programs, and energy theft detection. Bidgely is sold to utilities as SaaS or deployable into customer AWS, Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, and Oracle environments, and exposes embeddable customer-facing widgets to utility digital channels. Bidgely has been deployed by more than 50 utilities across four continents — including FortisBC, Arizona Public Service, PacifiCorp, Avista, NV Energy, Nova Scotia Power, and SoCalGas — covering tens of millions of meters. Bidgely operates an internal REST API surface across regional endpoints (naapi.bidgely.com, api.eu.bidgely.com) for its own pilot deployments and embeddable widgets, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API key program; integration is conducted under utility contracts.

companies.name: Binary Thumbs
companies.description: Binary Thumbs (operating name "Binary Thumb", Y Combinator Summer 2012) was a San Francisco startup founded in 2012 by Josh Leong, Michael Lin, and Matt Monson to reinvent the spreadsheet for touch devices. Its single product, Grid, was a collaborative grid-based spreadsheet and organizational app for iPad and iPhone that let people keep notes, pictures, people, and places in a freeform grid rather than rigid rows and columns. The company raised roughly $2.15M across a 2012 YC round and a 2013 seed, with participation from angel and institutional investors, and appears on the Andreessen Horowitz public investment list. Y Combinator now lists the company as inactive; Josh Leong led it as CEO from 2012 to 2016. Binary Thumb never shipped a public API, developer portal, or documentation surface -- it was a consumer iOS product company. Its lasting public technical footprint is the BinaryThumb GitHub organization and a handful of open-source React and JavaScript utility libraries published to npm.

companies.name: Binpress
companies.description: Binpress was a marketplace for commercial source code and open-source software components, founded in 2011 in Israel by Adam Benayoun (CEO) and Eran Galperin (CTO) and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global). The platform let developers publish, discover, buy, and sell SDKs, libraries, and code components on a 70/30 revenue split, growing to roughly 1,000 listings with GitHub integration and later adding hosted storefronts for digital goods. The company was acquired by CodersClan in 2016 and no longer operates as an active developer platform; the binpress.com domain has since been repurposed as an unrelated digital-business content site with no public API. This profile originated as a 500 Global portfolio lead surfaced into the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Blubblub
companies.description: Blub Blub Inc. is the company behind Speech Blubs, a speech-therapy and language-development app for children aged 1 to 8. Created by speech-language pathologists and child-development experts, the app uses video modeling, speech exercises, face filters, and play-based activities to help kids with speech delays, autism, Down syndrome, and apraxia learn to talk. Speech Blubs is available on iOS and Android, supports English, Spanish, and German, and has been downloaded by over 10 million families worldwide. Blub Blub is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. This is a consumer mobile-app company; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so the entry is limited to verified company identity and published web properties.

companies.name: Bluetalon
companies.description: BlueTalon was a data-centric security company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, that provided centralized data access control, dynamic data masking, and policy enforcement across big-data and hybrid data environments (Hadoop, Spark, relational databases, and cloud data stores). Its platform let enterprises define and enforce fine-grained authorization, auditing, and data- protection policies from a single control point. BlueTalon was backed by DCVC (Data Collective) among other investors, and was acquired by Microsoft in 2019, with its technology folded into Microsoft's Azure data-governance and security portfolio. The company no longer operates independently: bluetalon.com is no longer resolvable and the GitHub organization retains only archived, deprecated repositories. This profile is retained as a network record of an acquired provider; there is no live public API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Boston Scientific
companies.description: Boston Scientific is a global medical device manufacturer that develops, manufactures, and markets devices used in interventional medical specialties including interventional cardiology, cardiac rhythm management, electrophysiology, urology, pelvic health, endoscopy, neuromodulation, and peripheral interventions. The company advances science for life by transforming patient lives through innovative medical solutions.

companies.name: Bouffalo Lab
companies.description: Bouffalo Lab (博流智能) is a fabless chip design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nanjing, China, focused on ultra-low-power AIoT (AI + IoT) and edge-computing system chips. Its product line centers on RISC-V based microcontrollers with integrated wireless connectivity — the BL602/BL604 (Wi-Fi 2.4G + BLE 5.0), BL702/BL704/BL706 (Zigbee 3.0 + BLE 5.0), BL606P (quad-mode dual-core Wi-Fi/BT/BLE/Zigbee), and the BL616/BL618 and BL808 families — combining wireless radios, audio/video processing, and on-device AI algorithms. The company ships the open-source BouffaloSDK (a merge of bl_mcu_sdk and bl_iot_sdk) under Apache 2.0 through its public GitHub organization, along with hardware abstraction drivers, Matter/Thread support, and NuttX RTOS ports. Bouffalo Lab is a hardware/firmware provider rather than a web-API provider; it exposes no public HTTP/REST developer API, so the enrichment pipeline captures its developer surface (GitHub SDK org) and domain security posture. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

The company is no longer active as a startup; today the BrainTripping GitHub organization publishes open-source ClojureScript tooling such as cljs-live, magic-tree, and the Lark editor. As of the 2026 enrichment pass the company appears dormant: the buildscience.com domain no longer serves a live product (the host returns a CloudFront default certificate that does not match the domain and a broken origin), no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be located, and the organization's single public GitHub repository was last updated in January 2020. This profile is retained as a verified-identity network record; no API artifacts could be enriched because the provider publishes no live API.

companies.name: Caffeine
companies.description: Caffeine was a social broadcasting and live-streaming platform founded in 2016 by former Apple designers Ben Keighran and Sam Roberts, and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Greylock Partners. Built on a proprietary WebRTC-based real-time video distribution network, Caffeine positioned itself as a low-latency, social-first alternative to Twitch for gaming, entertainment, and — in its later years — live sports, partnering with roughly 200 sports organizations and reaching tens of millions of monthly users. The company published open-source broadcasting tooling under its caffeinetv GitHub organization (libcaffeine, caffeine-rtc, an OBS plugin, and the CaffQL GraphQL code generator) but never shipped a public, documented developer API program. Caffeine announced it was ceasing operations, and its web presence is now a shutdown notice; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead and is archival rather than an active, integrable API provider.

companies.name: Cambridge Blockchain
companies.description: Cambridge Blockchain, Inc. was a blockchain-based digital identity and compliance software company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Cambridge / Boston, Massachusetts. Its enterprise platform let financial institutions deliver strong digital identities to end users while meeting KYC/AML and data privacy obligations (including European GDPR), giving individuals control over their own personal identity data shared across institutions. The company was backed by investors including Partech and PayPal, and was acquired by Blockchains, Inc. in December 2020, after which its team and identity technology were folded into Blockchains' digital identity product. The former company website (cambridge-blockchain.com) is no longer served; the surviving public developer surface is its GitHub organization and two first-party npm cryptographic libraries. No public HTTP API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or hosted documentation was ever published.

The company operates medical centers offering primary care, wellness, pediatrics, and other services with an emphasis on preventive care and chronic disease management. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

companies.name: Capsule Social
companies.description: Capsule Social was a decentralized-innovation company founded in early 2021 by cryptography researcher Nadim Kobeissi to build tools for a web3 future. Its flagship product, Blogchain, was a decentralized publishing and social platform — a Substack-like blogging experience with Twitter-like social elements — built on IPFS for serverless content storage and the NEAR Protocol for identity, digital-asset management, and tokenized community governance, letting creators own their content and monetize it behind optional paywalls. The company raised a ~$2.6M seed round from investors including Polychain, Naval Ravikant, Fyrfly, and former Coinbase CTO Balaji Srinivasan. The Blogchain product and the capsulesocial GitHub organization have been inactive since roughly October 2023, and the capsule.social domain has since been re-registered by an unrelated "social memory" consumer app — so the surviving authoritative surface for this entity is its open-source GitHub org, not the current website. There is no hosted REST API: Blogchain is a client-side web3 dApp (Vue frontend, NEAR smart contracts, IPFS).

Customers order through a B2B e-commerce platform (re-platformed to Optimizely B2B in 2021, previously Magento) and companion iOS and Android wholesale-ordering apps built in partnership with Unbound Commerce.
