companies.name: Cloud Elements
companies.description: Cloud Elements was a Denver-based API integration platform that offered pre-built connectors ("Elements") and category-level Unified APIs (CRM, Documents, Finance, Helpdesk, Messaging, etc.) so SaaS vendors could embed third-party integrations without building each connector from scratch. UiPath acquired Cloud Elements in March 2021 and has since folded the technology into UiPath Integration Service. The original cloud-elements.com developer portal and the my.cloud-elements.com console are no longer marketed as a standalone product, so the canonical developer surface today is UiPath Integration Service. This profile is retained as a historical record and a pointer to the successor platform.

companies.name: Clutch Wallet
companies.description: Clutch Wallet was a Los Angeles-based web3 startup building a non-custodial "social wallet" and web3 toolkit — a seedless browser extension and mobile wallet (leaning on account abstraction and seamless sign-in) paired with a dApp offering token search, three-click DeFi, a web3 social profile, a personalized crypto media feed, aggregated multi-wallet balances in a single dashboard, integrated crypto education, and community tools. Founded by Bec Jones (CEO), James Kouzinas (CFO/COO), and Sheela Vats (CTO), it raised ~$800K backed by Anthemis (Female Innovators Lab Fund), Emmeline Ventures, Everywhere Ventures, and Rogue Women. The company is now permanently closed: its clutchwallet.xyz domain is parked and it exposed no public production API. It remains in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile; its clutch-wallet GitHub organization (mostly forks of Zerion, Argent, and MetaMask projects) and one first-party npm library survive as artifacts.

companies.description: ConAgra Foods, Inc. was the prior corporate name of Conagra Brands. In 2015 the company spun off its foodservice ingredients business as Lamb Weston and renamed the remaining packaged-foods business to Conagra Brands, Inc. This profile is preserved as a historical alias; the active company profile lives at the conagra-brands repository. No public developer APIs were ever published under the ConAgra Foods brand.

companies.name: CoreOS
companies.description: CoreOS was a San Francisco-based container infrastructure company founded in 2013 that built a lightweight, automatically-updating Linux distribution (Container Linux, originally CoreOS Linux) and a family of now-foundational cloud-native open source projects: etcd (the distributed key-value store at the heart of Kubernetes), the Quay container registry, the Tectonic enterprise Kubernetes platform, the rkt container engine, flannel networking, Clair image-vulnerability scanning, and Ignition provisioning. Red Hat acquired CoreOS in January 2018 for approximately $250 million. Its technologies were folded into Red Hat's portfolio — Container Linux became Red Hat CoreOS and the community Fedora CoreOS, Tectonic merged into OpenShift, Quay continues as Red Hat Quay, and etcd and rkt were donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. The company no longer operates independently; coreos.com redirects to Red Hat OpenShift. The github.com/coreos organization remains active as the upstream home for Fedora CoreOS components such as Ignition, Butane, and fleetlock.

companies.name: Cornershop by Uber
companies.description: Cornershop is an on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service founded in 2015 in Chile by Oskar Hjertonsson, Daniel Undurraga, and Juan Pablo Cuevas, simultaneously launching in Santiago, Chile and Mexico City, Mexico. The platform connects consumers with personal shoppers who pick and deliver groceries, pharmacy items, and other goods from local supermarkets, specialty stores, and big-box retailers. After a 2018 acquisition attempt by Walmart was blocked by Mexican regulators, Uber agreed in October 2019 to acquire majority ownership, completing full acquisition in July 2021 at a reported valuation north of US$3 billion — Chile's first unicorn exit. At its peak Cornershop operated in eight countries across the Americas: Chile, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Peru, Canada, and the United States. Beginning in 2021 Uber merged the Cornershop brand into Uber Eats, migrating the grocery vertical ("Uber Eats Grocery") into its main consumer app and progressively shutting down the standalone Cornershop apps and websites. As of 2026 cornershopapp.com and cornershop.io redirect to ubereats.com, the Cornershop LLC GitHub organization (archived October 2024) has zero public repositories, and there is no public developer API, SDK, partner program, or technical documentation under the Cornershop brand — Cornershop survives only as engineering history and as the LatAm backbone of Uber Eats Grocery. Community-built unofficial Python wrappers exist on GitHub but reverse-engineer the consumer mobile app and are not sanctioned by Uber.

companies.name: Cypress
companies.description: Cypress Semiconductor Corporation was a San Jose, California semiconductor company founded in 1982, and an early Mayfield venture investment. It designed and manufactured mixed-signal, embedded, and connectivity silicon — most notably the PSoC programmable system-on-chip microcontrollers, WICED Wi-Fi and Bluetooth wireless combos, USB controllers (EZ-USB), NOR flash and SRAM memory, and automotive Traveo microcontrollers — supported by the ModusToolbox and PSoC Creator developer tooling and the Cypress Developer Community. Infineon Technologies AG acquired Cypress in April 2020 for approximately 9.4 billion dollars; the business, its developer community, and its GitHub repositories have since been folded into Infineon. cypress.com now redirects to infineon.com and the developer resources live at community.infineon.com. Cypress shipped hardware SDKs and embedded toolchains rather than a public web/REST API, so there is no independent HTTP API surface to catalog for this entity — this profile documents it as a historical, acquired provider.

As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (dashbase.io) no longer resolves / times out and its GitHub organization retains only a single archived fork, so the company appears to be defunct or to have been acquired and wound down; no live developer surface, API, SDK, OpenAPI, or documentation could be located. The company positions itself as a global technology leader in travel product connectivity and is backed by investors including IDG Capital.

companies.name: Distelli
companies.description: Distelli was a Seattle-based DevOps and application-deployment company founded in 2013 by Rahul Singh and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It offered a SaaS platform and command-line tooling for building, deploying, and managing applications across servers and cloud infrastructure, later adding a Docker container pipeline and a Kubernetes (K8s) dashboard for managing container clusters. Puppet acquired Distelli in September 2017 and rebranded its products — the VM/CI-CD dashboard became Puppet Pipelines for Applications and the Kubernetes dashboard became Puppet Pipelines for Containers. The standalone Distelli company, product, and API no longer operate: the distelli.com domain is parked and the Distelli GitHub organization is archived and explicitly "no longer supported nor actively maintained." This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record (a16z) in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: eFishery
companies.description: eFishery is an Indonesian aquaculture technology ("fishtech") company founded in 2013 in Bandung by Gibran Huzaifah and Chrisna Aditya. Its platform combined an IoT smart auto-feeder (eFeeder) that dispenses feed to fish and shrimp ponds and streams pond telemetry to a smartphone app, with an integrated services layer: eFisheryKu / eFarm farm-management software, eFund (including the Kabayan "pay later" financing product) linking smallholder farmers to lenders, and eFresh / eMart marketplaces connecting farmers to feed suppliers and downstream buyers. The company raised a $90M Series C (2022) and a $200M Series D (2023) at a unicorn valuation, backed by investors including 500 Global, Aqua-Spark, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Temasek, and Northstar. In late 2024 an audit alleged large-scale financial-statement fraud dating to 2018; both founders resigned and the company underwent multiple rounds of layoffs and restructuring through 2025. This record was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; eFishery exposes no public developer API or developer portal, and its primary efishery.com domain currently resolves to a parked/forwarding host.

companies.name: ElasticBox
companies.description: ElasticBox was a multi-cloud application management and deployment platform founded in 2011 by former Microsoft engineers Alberto Arias Maestro, Amadeo Casas, and Ravi Srivatsav (AngelPad-backed, offices in San Francisco and Madrid). Its "boxes" model let enterprise IT define, version, and orchestrate application deployments across more than a dozen clouds — AWS, Microsoft Azure, IBM SoftLayer, VMware, vCloud Air and others — with a self-service catalog, a REST API (token-authenticated, JSON), and a Jenkins CI plug-in. The company raised roughly $12.4M across three rounds, including a $9M Series A in 2014 with participation from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Nexus Venture Partners, Intel Capital and Sierra Ventures. CenturyLink acquired ElasticBox in June 2016 and rebuilt the technology as CenturyLink Cloud Application Manager (now part of Lumen). The standalone ElasticBox product, its developer portal, and its public API documentation have been retired; the elasticbox.com domain no longer serves the platform. This profile is preserved as a historical portfolio-lead record — no live, first-party API surface remains to enrich.

companies.name: Embark Trucks
companies.description: Embark Trucks was an autonomous-trucking company founded in 2016 and backed by Y Combinator, building a self-driving software stack (the Embark Driver) for Class 8 semi-trucks operating on interstate highway freight lanes. The company went public via a SPAC merger with Northern Star Investment Corp II in late 2021, but wound down operations in November 2023 after failing to secure additional funding; its autonomous-driving technology and engineering assets were subsequently acquired by Applied Intuition. Embark never operated a public developer platform, REST API, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile is an identity record rather than a live API. Its only surviving public technical surface is the embarktrucks GitHub organization, which hosts open-source robotics and autonomous-vehicle tooling (ROS drivers, LIDAR/camera integrations, and the webviz visualization libraries) rather than first-party API client SDKs.

companies.name: Enel X
companies.description: Enel X is the advanced-energy-services business line of the Enel Group, an Italian multinational utility headquartered in Rome. Enel X delivers smart energy products and services across electrification, e-mobility, demand response, virtual power plants, and distributed energy resource (DER) management for residential, commercial, industrial, public-sector, and utility customers. Its principal offerings include the Enel X Way app and network for electric-vehicle charging (the consolidated successor to JuicePass and JuiceNet), the JuiceBox and JuicePedestal hardware lines, the JuiceNet Utility Edition managed-charging platform, the DER.OS / DER optimization software (now run as Calibrant Energy in North America after Enel's 2023 divestiture of its North American demand-response business), Enel X Flex flexibility management software, and VPP Connect, a set of API endpoints that lets third-party DER operators — OEMs, automation providers, and equipment manufacturers — aggregate EV chargers, batteries, HVAC systems, heat pumps, and other controllable assets into Enel's virtual power plant and earn revenue from demand-response and grid-services programs via either the open Automated Demand Response (oADR) protocol or a custom Enel API. Enel X exposes additional non-public surfaces — including the emobility.enelx.com OAuth/charging endpoints used by the Enel X Way mobile apps — but does not publish OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal; VPP Connect documentation is delivered under partnership agreement after a guided onboarding process. The official Enelx GitHub organization has effectively no public engineering presence, and the legacy JuiceNet public API has been deprecated as part of the platform migration to Enel X Way.

companies.name: Engine ML
companies.description: Engine ML was a machine-learning infrastructure startup (founded 2018, backed by Kleiner Perkins) that offered a hosted platform for distributed model training and experiment tracking. Its product surface centered on the `engine` command-line tool and the `eml` Python library, which let data scientists launch experiments, track code, system utilization, logs, and output files, and run image classifiers (PyTorch/TensorFlow/Keras) against datasets such as MNIST. The company appears to be defunct: engineml.com serves an empty page behind an expired TLS certificate (expired March 2023), the documentation site docs.engineml.com returns an empty S3 bucket, and the public GitHub organization (EngineML) has not been updated since 2020-2021. No live API, OpenAPI description, package-registry release, or reachable developer docs could be found. This profile preserves the historical identity and the still- live GitHub organization as the only verifiable surviving surface.

companies.name: Eventtus
companies.description: Eventtus was a Cairo, Egypt-based event technology company that built a mobile event app and attendee-engagement platform for conferences, trade shows, and community events. Its product offered event apps with agendas, networking and matchmaking, live Q&A and polls, push notifications, social feeds, lead capture, badge printing, online registration, and organizer analytics. Founded by Mai Medhat and Nihal Fares, Eventtus raised venture funding from investors including 500 Startups (500 Global), Vodafone Ventures, and Endure Capital, and was acquired by the community-events platform Bevy in July 2021. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no live public API, developer portal, or first-party SDK — the eventtus.com domain no longer resolves and the engineering blog is offline — so the profile is retained as identity only.

companies.name: Exscientia
companies.description: Exscientia was an Oxford UK-based AI-driven precision medicine and drug design company, founded in 2012 as a spin-out from the University of Dundee. Its platform combined generative chemistry (Centaur Chemist) with patient tissue-based screening (EVE, an automated single-cell platform for testing drug candidates directly against patient-derived tumor samples) to design small-molecule drug candidates faster and at lower cost than conventional pharma R&D. Notable firsts included EXS-21546 (an A2A antagonist developed with Evotec), DSP-1181 (the first AI-designed molecule to enter human clinical trials, with Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma), and DSP-0038 (a dual 5-HT1A/5-HT2A modulator for Alzheimer's psychosis). Exscientia maintained active pharma partnerships with Sanofi, Bristol Myers Squibb, Bayer, Sumitomo, and Merck KGaA. Exscientia was acquired by Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) in an all-stock deal that closed in November 2024; the combined company operates under the Recursion brand and the legacy exscientia.ai website now redirects to recursion.com. The Exscientia name persists primarily through its GitHub organization, which continues to host open-source scientific Python packages for molecular predictive modelling (molflux), physics-based ML potentials (physicsml), antibody structure prediction (abodybuilder3), and biomolecular simulation (biosimspace) used by the wider computational chemistry and structural biology community. Exscientia did not expose any public commercial APIs, SDKs, or developer products before or after the merger; platform access was always delivered through collaborative drug-discovery agreements.

companies.name: Fei Protocol
companies.description: Fei Protocol was an Ethereum-based decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol that launched in April 2021, introducing FEI, an algorithmic stablecoin backed by Protocol Controlled Value (PCV), alongside the TRIBE governance token. Founded by Joey Santoro, it merged with Rari Capital in December 2021 to form the Tribe DAO. Following the April 2022 Rari Fuse exploit, the Tribe DAO voted to wind down and dissolve the protocol later that year. Fei Protocol was backed by a16z (Andreessen Horowitz), Framework Ventures, and other investors. Its smart-contract code and documentation remain public on GitHub, but the protocol is no longer operational and its web properties (fei.money, docs.fei.money) are offline. Fei Protocol is an on-chain smart-contract system and exposes no public REST/HTTP API, so it carries no OpenAPI, SDK, or hosted API artifacts.

companies.name: ffrree
companies.description: ffrree (GitHub organization "Free") was an early-stage, Slow Ventures-backed mobile software company active around 2015-2016. Its only public engineering footprint is a GitHub organization of eight repositories - seven of them forks of third-party iOS and backend libraries (AFNetworking, jot, TheAmazingAudioEngine, protobuf-objc, redis-py, slack) plus an original CocoaPods "Specs" podspec mirror - with all repository activity ceasing in 2016. The company is defunct: ffrree.com now serves a GoDaddy/Afternic domain-for-sale parking lander, and there is no product, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface of any kind. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a verified dead lead rather than deleted, so the slug is not re-researched from scratch.

companies.name: Fimio
companies.description: Fimio was a developer-tooling startup founded in 2022 in Oakland, California by Omoju Miller (formerly of Google and GitHub). Its first product was an ML-trained fraud-detection / malicious-smart-contract reputation API for Web3 builders (Ethereum), with data supported by Spice AI, released as an alpha. The company later repositioned around "collaborative tooling for serverful applications" and "reproducible builds made easy." Fimio appears to be defunct: as of the enrichment probe both fimio.xyz and www.fimio.xyz 302-redirect to google.com, the docs/api subdomains do not resolve, the blog returns 404, and the GitHub organization (fimio-xyz) was archived on 2026-01-27 with only Careers and feedback repositories and no published API artifacts. It was backed by a ~$2.19M seed led by Neo with Redpoint Ventures, Protocol Labs, The House Fund and angel investors.

companies.name: Finiata
companies.description: Finiata was a Berlin-founded fintech providing working-capital and invoice financing to small businesses, freelancers and micro-enterprises, operating principally in Germany and Poland and backed by investors including Point Nine. The only live first-party assets found are the company's GitHub organization (github.com/debitech) and one unmaintained internal npm tooling package. No API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, documentation, or well-known surface exists to catalog.

companies.name: FitStar

companies.name: General Galactic Corporation
companies.description: General Galactic Corporation was an early-stage web3 studio founded by Rob Mee (founder of Pivotal Labs) and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It built open-source Ethereum developer tooling published under the generalgalactic GitHub organization, including eip4361-tools for Sign-In With Ethereum (EIP-4361), the ERC721Sequential (ERC721S) gas-optimized NFT contract, an ENS registry (skyteller-ens-registry), and related SIWE authentication utilities. The company wound down its products and experiments in 2023; its site now runs as an ENS/IPFS page announcing the closure. This profile catalogs the remaining public open-source and package footprint. No hosted or public API is currently operated by the company.

General Mills operates in over 100 countries. The company does not currently publish a public developer API portal and primarily relies on EDI and direct supply chain integrations with retail partners.

companies.name: Gestoos
companies.description: Gestoos was a computer-vision company that built a real-time gesture-recognition and touchless-interaction SDK, letting developers add camera-based hand-gesture and motion control to interactive installations, digital signage, kiosks, and embedded devices. Its public developer surface centered on an interactive SDK with sample integrations (including bindings for the Cinder C++ creative-coding framework). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment its primary web presence at gestoos.com is offline — the domain no longer resolves to the company and now redirects to an unrelated parked site — and the only surviving public developer asset is the gestoos GitHub organization, whose most recent activity dates to 2020. This profile is retained as a historical network record; the API/SDK product appears discontinued.

companies.name: GGFolks
companies.description: GGFolks (Good Game Folks) is a small, experimental independent game-development group that publishes its work as open source on GitHub under the ggfolks organization, with the tagline "We make good feels." Its repositories are early-stage games and supporting tooling rather than a commercial API product: platform is a TypeScript social-multiplayer web game framework (the `tfw` package, MIT-licensed), moncher is a monster-ranching social game, spaced is a web-based space editor, chatapp is a Dart messaging experiment, and ggdobj/esl provide shared C#/Unity client-server and simulation code. GGFolks does not publish a public developer portal, hosted API, OpenAPI definition, or released client SDK, so it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile with no API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Gigacatalyst
companies.description: Gigacatalyst is a Y Combinator-backed enterprise AI platform that turns customer requirements into configured software demos, POCs, UAT environments, and implementation workspaces by writing real configurations through a customer's existing product APIs. It embeds an AI customization layer directly into SaaS applications so that sales, solutions-engineering, and customer-success teams can build the missing features and workflows they need using natural language, while inheriting the host product's authentication and role-based access controls, sandboxed execution, and AI model restrictions. Gigacatalyst is an API consumer: it operates on top of other providers' APIs rather than publishing its own public developer API, so this profile captures company identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: GM OnStar
companies.description: GM OnStar is General Motors' connected vehicle services platform, originally launched in 1996 as an in-vehicle safety, security, and concierge service and since extended into a commercial data platform under OnStar Business Solutions. The OnStar Business Solutions API and Data Services product delivers near-real-time embedded telematics straight from properly equipped 2015-model-year-or-newer GM vehicles — Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac — without aftermarket hardware, exposing vehicle location, speed, ignition status, odometer, fuel level, EV state-of-charge and charging status, tire pressure, seatbelt status, diagnostic trouble codes, and driver-behavior events such as hard brake and hard acceleration. The product is packaged into tiered plans (commonly referenced as API Starter and API Pro) and is distributed primarily through OnStar's enterprise channel under the GM Envolve commercial brand, plus integrations with fleet management providers including Samsara, Geotab, Wheels, Verizon Connect, and other approved telematic service providers. There is no public self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI specification — access is gated through GM/OnStar sales (developer.gm.com is a request-access endpoint) or via an authorized integration partner. Consumer-facing OnStar mobile features (remote start, remote lock, vehicle locate, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, Super Cruise telemetry) are delivered through GM's myChevrolet, myBuick, myGMC, and myCadillac apps and are not part of the published API surface.

companies.name: Hackpad
companies.description: Hackpad was a web-based real-time collaborative wiki and document editor, built on the open-source Etherpad codebase, that let teams write and edit documents together simultaneously. It was acquired by Dropbox in April 2014 and its underlying platform was released as open source under the Apache 2.0 license at github.com/dropbox/hackpad. The hosted hackpad.com service was wound down after Dropbox folded the team's work into Dropbox Paper, and the public service was discontinued in 2017. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hackpad as a historical, now-defunct portfolio company surfaced from the a16z portfolio; there is no live production API surface remaining, and the durable public artifact is the open-source repository.

companies.name: Harman International
companies.description: Harman International, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, is a global leader in connected technologies for automotive, consumer, and enterprise markets, including connected car systems, audio products, professional solutions, and connected services. Harman does not currently publish a public developer portal or open APIs; integrations with Harman platforms (such as Ignite, Ready Connect, and audio brands like JBL, Harman Kardon, and AKG) are typically delivered through commercial partnerships and OEM agreements.

This repository tracks public APIs, developer resources, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Hasbro. No public developer APIs have been published at this time.

companies.name: HeadsUp
companies.description: HeadsUp was an AI conversion engine for product-led growth (PLG) that helped go-to-market teams identify which product-qualified users to engage and when to engage them. It ingested product usage and analytics data (for example from Segment), applied feature engineering and machine-learning scoring to surface conversion, churn, and upsell signals, and synced those insights into sales tooling such as Salesforce so reps could act on in-product behavior without engineering, code, or SQL. Customers included Contentful, Dialpad, and Matillion. HeadsUp was backed by Wing Venture Capital and 645 Ventures and was acquired by composable-CDP company Hightouch in November 2023, after which its team joined Hightouch to work on Customer 360. The standalone headsup.ai product and developer surface have since been wound down; this profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: HotelUrbano
companies.description: HotelUrbano (later rebranded Hurb) was a Brazilian online travel agency founded in January 2011 by Joao Ricardo Mendes and headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, offering hotel bookings, flights, and flexible travel packages across domestic and international destinations. companies.description: Java EE (Java Platform, Enterprise Edition) was a set of specifications extending the Java SE platform with enterprise features such as distributed computing and web services. In 2017 Oracle transferred Java EE to the Eclipse Foundation, where it was rebranded as Jakarta EE. Jakarta EE 11 continues the platform with profiles for Platform, Web, and Core covering RESTful Web Services, JSON Processing, Persistence, CDI, Servlet, Security, and other enterprise Java specifications.

companies.name: Jewelbots

The wearable is an Arduino-compatible, Bluetooth Low Energy device built on a Nordic nRF chipset that friends can program with an Arduino IDE library and firmware, with a companion iOS/Android app for pairing and messaging. The project is largely open source: the Jewelbots GitHub organization publishes the Arduino library, firmware, companion app, and hardware/toolchain repositories. Jewelbots was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company; jewelbots.com now runs as a Shopify storefront. It is a hardware/firmware and education company rather than a web API provider, and exposes no first-party public HTTP/OpenAPI API.

companies.name: Klout
companies.description: Klout was a San Francisco social-analytics company, founded in 2008 by Joe Fernandez and Binh Tran, that scored individuals on their online social influence. The "Klout Score" was a single number from 1 to 100 derived from the size of a person's social network and how other people engaged with the content they published across connected accounts such as Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, and Google+. Klout operated a public REST API — the Klout API v2 at api.klout.com — that let developers resolve a social handle to a Klout identity, look up a user's score and score history, and retrieve influence graphs (who a user influences and is influenced by) and topic affinities; access was key-based and widely used by marketing, CRM, and social-listening tools, and a large community of third-party client libraries grew up around it in Ruby, Node.js, Python, and PHP. Lithium Technologies acquired Klout on 27 March 2014 for approximately $200 million. Lithium retired Klout as a standalone service on 25 May 2018 — the day the EU General Data Protection Regulation took effect — stating that Klout's AI and machine-learning capabilities were valuable to Lithium but the consumer service was not aligned with its long-term strategy. The Klout API was shut down with the service. Lithium has since been rebranded as Khoros, and klout.com now redirects into the Khoros website. The company is defunct and operates no live API; this profile is retained as a historical provider record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Kuva Space
companies.description: Kuva Space is a Finnish space-data company headquartered in Espoo that operates a fleet of hyperspectral Earth observation microsatellites and delivers AI-driven planetary intelligence through its Kuva Sense platform. Founded in 2016 (originally as Reaktor Space Lab) by Tuomas Tikka and Janne Kuhno in collaboration with Reaktor, the company designs, builds, and operates its own 6U CubeSat-class spacecraft carrying a patented in-orbit tunable Fabry-Perot 2D snapshot hyperspectral imager. Its operational Hyperfield-1A (launched August 2024 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg) and Hyperfield-1B (launched June 2025) cover the 475–950 nm VNIR range with up to 160 tunable spectral bands at 25 m spatial resolution and a 50 km swath from a 500 km polar sun-synchronous orbit. The larger 70 kg Hyperfield-2 microsatellite, scheduled for H2 2026, expands coverage to 450–1,650 nm at 15 m resolution with an additional 3.6 m GSD RGB camera. By 2030 Kuva Space plans to grow the constellation to roughly 100 satellites to enable sub-daily revisit anywhere on Earth. Onboard AI handles cloud filtering, spectral band alignment, and compression so that downlinked products feed directly into Kuva Sense, where automated analytics generate insights-as-a-service for agriculture (crop identification, yield forecasting, harvest timing), aquaculture (water quality, algal bloom detection, biomass), environment and carbon (sequestration monitoring, deforestation, pollution tracking), and safety and security (vessel detection and tracking, illegal activity warning, rapid change detection). Kuva Space is part of the European Space Agency InCubed-co-funded HYPERFIELD program, was awarded a €1.8M ESA Civil Security from Space contract within the SMART-CONNECT consortium to demonstrate rapid hyperspectral insights for crisis response, and in 2026 signed a Letter of Intent with SSC Space to strengthen Nordic space capabilities. The commercial model is subscription-based insights-as-a-service rather than pay-per-pixel imagery sales, with current access offered through the Kuva Sense Early Adopter Program; the company markets "robust APIs and customizable data formats" for system integration but does not currently publish open public API reference documentation, an OpenAPI specification, or a self-service developer portal. The only public engineering surface is the open-source kuva-data-processing Python toolkit (kuva-metadata, kuva-reader, kuva-geometry) on GitHub and PyPI, which reads Kuva GeoTIFF-based L0/L1AB/L1C/L2A data products and their metadata sidecars.

companies.name: PsiQuantum
companies.description: PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California photonic quantum computing company founded in 2016 by Jeremy O'Brien, Terry Rudolph, Pete Shadbolt, and Mark Thompson, building utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers based on single-photon qubits at telecom wavelength. Its Omega chipset — a silicon photonic system integrating on-chip single-photon sources, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, barium-titanate optical switches, and low-loss fiber couplers — is manufactured on 300mm wafers at GlobalFoundries' flagship fab in Malta, NY, leveraging mature semiconductor processes rather than exotic cryogenic fabrication. The company is constructing two utility- scale, million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum computing sites: one at Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia (in partnership with the Australian and Queensland governments) and one at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago, Illinois (with additional R&D at PsiLabs in Daresbury, UK and assembly at PsiFactory in Milpitas, CA). PsiQuantum exposes a developer surface aimed at fault-tolerant quantum algorithm researchers: Construct, an enterprise platform for FTQC algorithm development, resource analysis, and training; Circuit Designer, a free web tool for prototyping and visualizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits; Circuit Hub, a shared library of `.circuit` files; and two open-source Python projects on GitHub — Bartiq, a symbolic quantum resource estimator that compiles subroutine-level costs to global T-gate, Toffoli, qubit, and circuit-volume estimates, and QREF, an open JSON-Schema-based format for representing quantum algorithms as hierarchical DAGs with a Pydantic validation library and a `qref-render` visualization tool. NVIDIA's CUDA-Q is integrated into Construct for accelerated simulation. PsiQuantum does not currently publish a commercial cloud-access REST API, OpenAPI specification, or a general-purpose quantum-execution SDK comparable to those of gate-model quantum cloud providers — its public developer artifacts are confined to FTQC resource-estimation tooling and algorithm-design surfaces — and there is no public pricing or self-serve tier for the underlying quantum hardware.

companies.name: Sokowatch / Wasoko

Wasoko's revenue model is wholesale-to-retail product sales plus fintech (credit, payments) and logistics fees. companies.name: NuScale Power
companies.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

companies.name: Rubicon
companies.description: Rubicon (formerly NYSE: RBT) is a waste, recycling, and sustainability technology company founded in 2008. It went public in 2022 via a SPAC merger with Founder SPAC at a pro forma valuation of roughly $1.7 billion, branding itself a "digital challenger" to the traditional waste-hauling industry with a marketplace connecting waste generators to independent haulers plus the RUBICONSmartCity fleet-and-routing platform used by more than 70 municipalities. Operating Status: the company subsequently faced severe financial distress - layoffs and debt restructuring in 2023, a June 2024 NYSE delisting, and a May 2024 divestiture of its entire fleet technology and smart-city business unit (RUBICONSmartCity, RUBICONPro, RUBICONPremier) to Rodina Capital for roughly $68 million plus a possible $12 million earnout; those assets were subsequently absorbed by Routeware. In early 2025 Rubicon deregistered its securities and became a privately held company, majority-owned by Jose Miguel Enrich through MBI Holdings, and remains the subject of shareholder litigation over the change-of-control terms. The surviving company operates as a smaller enterprise waste brokerage and sustainability-data business built around the RUBICONConnect platform (service, equipment, pickup, and cost visibility for enterprise customers such as Chipotle and FedEx), alongside RUBICONRegWatch compliance tooling, sustainability reporting, technical advisory services, and the Rubicon Now on-demand dumpster-rental service in a handful of cities. rubicon.com publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no OpenAPI specification. The only discoverable API artifact tied to the rubicon.com domain is a "Routeware Smartcity Public Api" Swagger UI hosted at a dev subdomain (haulerpublic-api.dev.aws.rubicon.com) - leftover infrastructure from the divested fleet/smart-city business - which returned a 503 Service Unavailable on every check during this review and is not publicly documented or reachable. Any hauler or municipal system integration Rubicon references (for example, connecting to city 311 systems) is negotiated per partner and gated behind sales and onboarding rather than exposed through self-serve developer documentation. Pricing across RUBICONConnect and Rubicon's enterprise services is entirely quote-based and negotiated per contract; no public pricing, tiers, or rate limits are published. This entry is maintained as an honest stub pending any future public API surface.

companies.description: SINAI Technologies is a San Francisco–headquartered enterprise SaaS company providing a Decarbonization Intelligence platform for carbon management, sustainability planning, and ESG compliance. The platform unifies organization-wide emissions accounting, climate transition planning, climate financial planning, and execution management so industrial enterprises can measure, report, and reduce Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions using science-based methodologies. Core modules include Carbon Accounting & Reporting, the Climate Transition Planner (with marginal abatement cost curves and scenario modeling), the Climate Financial Planner, and Execution & Management for tracking decarbonization projects. SINAI's Decarbonization Intelligence Portal layers Tableau-based dashboards, AI-powered bulk data ingestion, and AI Emissions Match (which maps unstructured emissions data to emission factors) on top of the underlying carbon ledger. The platform is designed around major reporting frameworks including CDP, TCFD, SEC climate disclosure, CSRD, CBAM, California SB 253 / SB 261, Brazil SBCE, and Brazil CVM resolutions 217 and 218, and is SOC 2 compliant with TÜV SÜD ISO 14064 verification. Customers include Siemens Energy, ArcelorMittal, Harley-Davidson, Emirates, Natura &Co, Minerva Foods, Wilson Sons, BRK Ambiental, and Japan's largest bank MUFG. SINAI states publicly that it can connect to enterprise customer systems through APIs to automate roughly 70% of emissions data ingestion, but it does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, public API reference, or a GitHub organization — its API surface is delivered as a private integration capability negotiated with enterprise customers rather than a self-serve developer product.

companies.description: Supercritical is a London-based carbon removal marketplace founded in 2021 by Michelle You and Aaron Randall, the team behind Songkick. The company builds the market infrastructure that turns carbon dioxide removal (CDR) commitments into delivered tonnes, connecting corporate buyers with vetted suppliers of durable, engineered, and nature-engineered carbon removal. Supercritical's marketplace covers the major durable CDR pathways — biochar, BECCS, enhanced weathering, direct air capture (DAC), DAC with ocean storage, woody biomass sinking, and bio-oil — with published per-tonne pricing and live availability data. The platform layers a proprietary 118-point vetting protocol on top of supplier listings, spanning climate science, environmental impact, delivery risk, and social benefits, and reports that 84% of assessed projects fail to meet its standards. Supercritical also provides supply sourcing and creation services to originate new CDR projects, buffer-pool-based delivery-risk mitigation, and policy and science advisory work (its team advises SBTi on CDR guidance). Customers include Virgin Atlantic, The Economist Group, Rothschild & Co, XTX Markets, and Tide, with reported coverage of roughly 80% of the global durable CDR market and 1.3M tonnes contracted across 200+ corporate buyers and 600+ tracked suppliers. The business is funded by Lightspeed Venture Partners, MMC Ventures, and GreenCode Ventures. Supercritical does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository; transactions, supplier discovery, and pricing data are delivered through its hosted marketplace, advisor relationships, and contracted buyer accounts.

companies.name: TAE Technologies
companies.description: TAE Technologies (formerly Tri Alpha Energy) is a Foothill Ranch, California fusion energy company founded in 1998, pursuing commercial fusion power using aneutronic hydrogen-boron (p-B11) fuel in an advanced beam-driven field-reversed configuration (FRC). Because the p-B11 reaction is aneutronic, TAE's approach produces virtually no neutron flux or on-site radioactive waste compared with conventional deuterium-tritium concepts. The company has built a progression of plasma machines — Sewer Pipe, CBFR-SPS, C-2, C-2U, and C-2W ("Norman") — and is constructing Copernicus in Irvine, California to demonstrate net energy gain, with Da Vinci planned as the grid-connected power-plant demonstration. TAE has raised more than USD 1.2 billion from investors including Google, Chevron, NEA, Goldman Sachs, Vulcan, Venrock, Wellcome Trust, and the Kuwait Investment Authority, and runs research collaborations with Japan's National Institute for Fusion Science (NIFS). Two operating subsidiaries commercialize spin-off technology: TAE Life Sciences develops accelerator-based Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) systems for cancer treatment, and TAE Power Solutions builds modular, software-controlled power-management systems for e-mobility and battery applications. TAE is a private hardware and deep-science company; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or public open-source code repository.

The company also develops satellite technology and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities to extend its intelligence services beyond the airborne domain. Tekever's revenue model is built on government and defence contracts, platform sales, and managed ISR-as-a-service offerings; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and engagement with the company is conducted through direct sales, government procurement, and partnership channels.

companies.name: .cursorrules
companies.description: .cursorrules is a project-level configuration file used by the Cursor AI code editor to define custom rules, coding conventions, and behavioral instructions that shape how the editor's AI assistant generates and edits code. The file is placed in the root of a repository and is read automatically by Cursor when the project is opened, giving teams a way to enforce architectural patterns, style guides, framework conventions, and tooling preferences across all AI-generated code. The format is intentionally flexible - rules are typically written in plain Markdown or natural language and may include sections describing project structure, technology stack, naming conventions, testing requirements, and out-of-scope behaviors. Cursor has since extended the concept with .cursor/rules/ directories of multiple scoped rule files, but the original .cursorrules file remains widely used and supported.

companies.description: AquaShield is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26 batch) startup building AI-driven water leak detection for buildings and large real estate portfolios. Non-invasive sensors clamp onto existing pipes in minutes with no pipe cutting, retrofits, or downtime; the platform learns each building's normal water-flow patterns and flags anomalies in real time before they escalate into costly damage. Water damage is the largest preventable loss in real estate — more than fire and theft combined. Founded by former MIT and Harvard/EPFL robotics researchers Paul Beckers (CEO) and Marguerite Benoist (CTO), the company is based in San Francisco and works with some of the largest residential portfolios in the world. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; AquaShield currently publishes a marketing site only and does not yet expose a public API or developer program.

companies.description: Aril Inc. (Arilinc) is a fabless semiconductor company in Los Gatos, California designing efficient AI processors and memory technology for edge inference. Its two core products are the Aril Standard Cell Memory, a patented on-chip memory offering roughly 40% lower active power and 3.6x smaller area, and a scalable RISC-V-based AI Processor Engine delivering hundreds of TOPS of inference per block with integrated vector and matrix engines. The company targets robotics, industrial automation, drones, defense and aerospace, autonomous vehicles, and edge vision systems where power efficiency is critical. Founded by a team of engineers who have collectively shipped 20M+ processors and worked on silicon for Cisco, Intel, AMD, and Google. Arilinc sells custom silicon and IP to hardware makers rather than a public developer API; it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic surface at this time.

ArrowPoint no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no documentation, no APIs and no SDKs, and the arrowpoint.com domain — still delegated to Cisco nameservers — serves no live web or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Matrix Partners portfolio exit.

companies.name: Atexto
companies.description: Atexto was a speech-recognition data company (self-described "the accuracy platform for speech recognition") based in Mexico City, founded around 2016 by Brenda Mana Pastrian and Esteban Gorupicz. It helped machine-learning and voice-assistant teams create, collect, annotate, transcribe, and benchmark audio/speech datasets, combining an enterprise data platform with a global paid crowdsourcing community that transcribed and labeled audio across roughly 24 languages and their regional accents. The company also offered a hybrid human-plus-machine audio-to-text transcription service and ASR training-data services. It was backed by 500 Global, Redwood Ventures, MC Capital, and a Start-Up Chile grant. The company now appears inactive: its former domain atexto.com has been repurposed to an unrelated third-party site, and no live developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification could be located. This profile captures verified historical identity only; no API artifacts were enriched because no live API surface exists.

companies.name: AtheroMed
companies.description: AtheroMed, Inc. was a privately-held medical device company based in Menlo Park, California, founded to treat peripheral artery disease (PAD). Its sole product was the Phoenix Atherectomy System, an over-the-wire, low-profile atherectomy catheter that uses a rotating front-cutting element at the distal tip to shave diseased material directly into the catheter, where an internal Archimedes screw continuously captures and removes the debulked material without requiring specialized capital equipment. The Phoenix system received FDA 510(k) clearance in January 2014 and CE Mark approval in Europe. AtheroMed was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and U.S. Venture Partners, and was acquired by Volcano Corporation in June 2014 for $115 million upfront plus milestone payments; Volcano was in turn acquired by Royal Philips in February 2015. AtheroMed no longer operates as an independent company, its atheromed.com domain is parked and listed for sale, and it has no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind. The Phoenix catheter is now sold as a Philips Volcano product.

companies.name: Atomic Alchemy
companies.description: Atomic Alchemy is a deep-tech nuclear company that designs, builds, and operates non-power research reactors to manufacture high-value radioisotopes for medical, research, industrial, defense, and space applications. Its proprietary Versatile Isotope Production Reactor (VIPR) technology and Meitner-1 facility are intended to create a scalable, onshore supply of isotopes such as molybdenum-99 (for cancer diagnostics and treatment), strontium-90, and americium-241, reducing US dependence on foreign isotope production. Founded by CEO Thomas Eiden and headquartered in Idaho Falls, Idaho, the company was backed by DCVC and Y Combinator and was acquired by advanced-fission company Oklo (NYSE: OKLO) in early 2025, operating as a wholly owned subsidiary. In 2026 the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission granted Atomic Alchemy a materials license to handle, process, and distribute isotopes. As a physical radioisotope manufacturer, Atomic Alchemy publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures company identity only.

Atrisa is designed to fit into existing workflows: teams bring their own toolkit, PDKs (process design kits), and design documents, which Atrisa reads, understands, and adopts to produce schematic-level outputs and iterate on analog designs. As an early-stage company it currently ships a hosted web application rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public surface pending any future API release.

The company appears to be defunct as of this profile — its primary domain (braid.ai) now redirects to a domain-for-sale listing and no developer, documentation, or API surface could be found. companies.name: Customer Database
companies.description: Customer Database is the topic dedicated to APIs, schemas, vocabularies, and reference designs for the systems of record that store customer identity, profile, contact, preference, consent, and account data. A customer database underpins CRM, marketing automation, customer data platforms (CDPs), customer service, billing, and analytics use cases, and is increasingly expected to support API-first access, schema-on-write data quality, real-time eventing, GDPR/CCPA consent and erasure workflows, and identity resolution across web, mobile, and offline channels. This repository tracks the vendors, standards, and patterns that make customer data accessible, governed, and portable.

companies.name: Customer Portals
companies.description: Customer Portals is the topic dedicated to the architecture, APIs, schemas, and reference designs behind self-service customer portals. A customer portal is a secure web or mobile experience where authenticated customers can manage their profile, view orders and invoices, pay bills, submit and track support tickets, download documents, manage notification preferences, and access account-specific resources. Modern customer portals are typically composed of multiple back-end APIs - authentication and identity, profile and preference management, billing and invoicing, support and ticketing, notifications, and document delivery - surfaced through a single front-end shell. This repository tracks the vendors, patterns, and standards that make customer portals reliable, accessible, and API-driven.

companies.name: HawkEye 360
companies.description: HawkEye 360 is a Herndon, Virginia-based radio frequency (RF) data analytics and geospatial intelligence company that operates the first commercial satellite constellation purpose-built to identify, process, and geolocate a broad range of RF signals from space. Founded in 2015 by Chris DeMay, Charles Clancy, and Bob McGwier, the company flies clusters of three small satellites in formation that use time- and frequency-difference-of-arrival triangulation to pinpoint emitters across VHF through Ku-band. As of 2025, HawkEye 360 has placed 36 Hawk satellites on orbit across 12 operational clusters. Its core products include RFGeo (the underlying RF signal mapping and geolocation data product), RFIQ (its RF intelligence data product recently selected by NASA Commercial LEO programs), and Mission Space, a web-based RF geospatial intelligence analysis platform. The company also offers a Regional Awareness Subscription (RAS) service providing persistent monitoring of high-interest regions such as the Mediterranean, South China Sea, and the Korean Peninsula. In December 2023 HawkEye 360 acquired Maxar Intelligence's RF Solutions business (formerly Aurora Insight), expanding its spectrum-mapping capabilities. Customers are concentrated in defense, intelligence, national security, and maritime domain awareness — including the US Government, allied partners, and foreign military sales (a 2025 FMS to India was approved by the Defense Security Cooperation Agency). HawkEye 360 has filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO. There is no public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open-source release; data access is delivered through gated commercial and government contracts via the Mission Space platform and a customer-facing API for ordering and integration of RF analytics into customer systems.

companies.description: Iridium Communications Inc. (NASDAQ: IRDM) is a McLean, Virginia satellite communications company operating a constellation of 66 cross-linked Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that deliver truly global L-band voice, data, IoT, and positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) services across every region of the Earth, including the polar oceans. Iridium sells satellite phones (Iridium Extreme), satellite messengers, satellite IoT modules and modems (Iridium 9602/9603, Iridium Certus 9770/9810/9704, Iridium Edge, Iridium Edge Pro, Iridium Edge Solar), Short Burst Data (SBD) messaging, broadband Certus terminals, and next-generation Iridium NTN Direct 5G Non-Terrestrial Network services built on 3GPP NB-IoT for direct-to-device smartphone and IoT connectivity. Iridium CloudConnect — co-developed with Amazon Web Services — pipes satellite IoT data as JSON into customer-owned Amazon SQS queues inside their own AWS VPC over a dedicated private Iridium-AWS interconnect, making Iridium the first global cloud-native satellite IoT backhaul. The company serves aviation, maritime, government/defense, land-mobile, autonomous systems, and IoT markets through a partner ecosystem of more than 500 service providers, value-added resellers, and hardware OEMs, and in May 2026 announced a planned acquisition of Aireon, operator of the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance network. Iridium's business model is airtime/subscription revenue plus hardware module licensing and engineering services; there is no public, self-service developer API or OpenAPI — network access is mediated through Iridium-authorized service providers, the Iridium CloudConnect AWS integration, and hardware-level AT-command and SBD interfaces on Iridium modems.

companies.name: Product Backlog
companies.description: A product backlog is a prioritized list of features, enhancements, and fixes that serves as the single source of requirements for product development. It is most commonly used in Agile and Scrum methodologies, where the product owner is responsible for ordering items based on business value, customer feedback, dependencies, and technical considerations. The backlog evolves continuously as new requirements emerge and priorities shift, providing development teams with a clear, ordered view of upcoming work.

companies.name: Product Backlog Items
companies.description: Product backlog items (PBIs) are the individual units of work that make up a product backlog, representing features, enhancements, bug fixes, and technical tasks in Agile and Scrum methodologies. Each PBI typically includes a description, acceptance criteria, priority, and an estimate of effort. PBIs are continuously refined through grooming and refinement sessions, and the highest-priority items are pulled into sprints by development teams to be implemented and delivered as increments of working software.

companies.name: Zap Energy
companies.description: Zap Energy is a Seattle, Washington fusion energy company pursuing commercial fusion power via the sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch — a compact, magnet-free pulsed-power approach in which a flowing column of deuterium plasma is compressed (pinched) to fusion conditions inside a roughly two-meter metal tube, with shear in the axial flow stabilizing the pinch in place of the heavy superconducting magnets used by tokamak and stellarator designs. Founded in 2017 by Benj Conway, Brian A. Nelson, and Uri Shumlak as a spinout of University of Washington and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory research, the company has developed a lineage of devices — ZaP, ZaP-HD, FuZE, FuZE-Q, and FuZE-3 — culminating in 2024 with Century, a 100-kW-scale repetitive pulsed-power test platform with liquid-metal walls intended to demonstrate plant-relevant technologies. In November 2025 FuZE-3 reported plasma electron pressures of 830 MPa (1.6 GPa total), the highest pressure measured in any sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch and a marker on the path to scientific energy gain (Q>1). Zap Energy was selected for the U.S. Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program in May 2023 and received DOE approval of the preconceptual design of its Fusion Pilot Plant. The company has raised over $325 million across Series A–D from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, Energy Impact Partners, Chevron Technology Ventures, Shell Ventures, DCVC, Valor Equity Partners, and Addition. As of April 2026, Zabrina Johal serves as CEO with Conway as President, and the company has expanded its mandate to also pursue small modular fission alongside its fusion roadmap. Zap Energy has no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release; the technical surface is published as peer-reviewed papers and DOE milestone reports.

By 2016 Clinkle had quietly shut down with no official announcement. companies.name: Klutter
companies.description: Klutter is an unresolved entry harvested from the 500 Global portfolio listing and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The 2026-07-19 enrichment pass could not establish a verifiable identity for this company. The URL captured alongside the name in the 500 Global portfolio scrape, price.com, resolves to Price Technologies Inc. (Los Angeles, CA), a consumer cash-back, coupon and price-comparison platform that is a different company and is tracked separately; that pointer has therefore been removed rather than misattributed to Klutter. No company named Klutter with a matching profile could be confirmed in the 500 Global portfolio through public sources. The klutter.com domain is parked (it serves only a JavaScript redirect to a registrar lander), and the other public uses of the name are unrelated third parties: the Klutter Flutter/Kotlin Multiplatform framework by buijs-dev, a Komga comic-server client app for iOS and Android by Mark Winckle, and a music project.
